act-001.name: Construction Access Route Visual Barrier Evaluation
act-001.text: Evaluate construction access routes (e.g., SR 160, Hood-Franklin Road, Walnut Grove Road, Byron Highway, levee roads) and identify the portions where visual barriers would reduce truck headlight light and glare on nearby residents.
act-001.expectedEvidence: Copy of the access route evaluation identifying where visual barriers are needed.

locators.excerpt: DWR will evaluate construction routes and identify portions of access routes where the use of visual barriers would minimize the introduction of new light and glare from construction truck headlights and the impact on nearby residents. Access routes could include SR 160, Hood-Franklin Road, West Walnut Grove Road, Mountain House Road, South Holt Road, Byron Highway, West Bethany Road, and various levee roads.

act-002.name: Covered Species Survey Protocols (Pre-implementation PAP)
act-002.text: Develop with CDFW species survey protocols for CTS, GGS, SWHA, TRBL, CBB and MALI (number and timing of surveys, habitat types, methods and rationale, capture and identification protocols, presence/absence methodology), submit them in the Pre-implementation Phase Authorization Package, and obtain CDFW written approval.
act-002.expectedEvidence: Copy of the Pre-implementation Phase Authorization Package with the species survey protocols and CDFW's written approval.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall develop, in coordination with CDFW, species survey protocols specific to CTS, GGS, SWHA, TRBL, CBB, and MALI. Survey protocols specific to each forementioned Covered Species shall be provided to CDFW as part of the Pre-implementation Phase Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6.1) for review and approval. Protocols shall be finalized and approved in writing by CDFW prior to initiation of any Covered Activity including but not limited to preconstruction field investigation activities or preconstruction species site surveys necessary for Construction Phase Authorization. Survey protocols shall include but not be limited to: the number of surveys that will be conducted for each Covered Activity and/or location; when the surveys are planned to take place (i.e., season and how much time between surveys); what type of habitat will be surveyed (i.e., foraging, nesting, and/or overwintering); associated habitat characteristics, survey methods and supporting rationale including references as appropriate; capture and identification protocol(s)if appropriate; and survey methodology developed specifically for determining presence or absence of a species, if appropriate.

act-003.name: Phase Impact and Mitigation Calculation
act-003.text: Calculate total Covered Species impacts and the corresponding compensatory mitigation, on-site restoration, and other mitigation for each Phase, and include the calculation in the Phase Authorization Package.
act-003.expectedEvidence: Copy of the Phase Authorization Package showing the Phase's Covered Species impact and mitigation calculation as submitted to CDFW.

locators.excerpt: As described in Conditions of Approval 6.2 and 7.1, Permittee shall calculate the total impacts on Covered Species and the corresponding amount of compensatory mitigation, on-site restoration, or other mitigation obligations required for each Phase of the Project prior to the beginning of each Phase, which calculation shall be included in the Phase Authorization Package submitted to CDFW for review.

act-004.name: Over-Water Geotechnical Exploration Description
act-004.text: Submit a description of all over-water geotechnical exploration activities, including activities, number of sites, spatial extent, depths and species-specific minimization measures, to CDFW in the Pre-implementation Phase Authorization Package for review and approval.
act-004.expectedEvidence: Copy of the over-water geotechnical exploration description submitted in the Pre-implementation Phase Authorization Package and CDFW's approval.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall submit a description of all over- water geotechnical exploration activities to CDFW as part of the Pre-implementation Phase Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6.1) to be reviewed and approved prior to the initiation of preconstruction activities. Information provided to CDFW shall include the description of the activities to be undertaken, number of exploratory sites, spatial extent of over- water activities, exploration depth for each exploration, and minimization measures for over- water exploratory activities specific to Covered Species.

act-005.name: In-Water Construction Notice to USACE, DBW and USCG
act-005.text: Notify the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Department of Boating and Waterways, and U.S. Coast Guard before in-water construction begins
act-005.expectedEvidence: Copies of the notices sent to USACE, the Department of Boating and Waterways and the U.S. Coast Guard before in-water construction.

locators.excerpt: DWR will notify agencies, including the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, the Department of Boating and Waterways, and the U.S. Coast Guard, before in-water construction or maintenance activities begin and will notify appropriate fish and wildlife agency representatives and others when these activities could affect water quality or aquatic species.

act-006.name: Take Contact Representative Notification
act-006.text: Provide the name and telephone number of the special-status species take contact representative to the fish and wildlife agencies.
act-006.expectedEvidence: Record of the take contact representative's name and telephone number provided to the fish and wildlife agencies.

locators.excerpt: DWR will appoint a representative to be the primary point of contact for any employee or contractor who might inadvertently take a special-status species, or a representative 19 will be identified during the employee education program and the representative’s name and telephone number provided to the fish and wildlife agencies.

act-007.name: Background Air Monitoring Station Confirmation
act-007.text: Identify representative background PM and/or NO2 monitoring stations in coordination with the local air district, based on proximity and spatial scale, and obtain the district's confirmation that the selected stations represent ambient air quality for the study area.
act-007.expectedEvidence: Written confirmation from the local air district that the selected background monitoring stations are representative.

locators.excerpt: DWR will identify representative background PM and/or NO air quality monitors in 2 coordination with the local air district. Project construction features must be within the spatial scale of representativeness for the 5 selected monitors. DWR will identify background monitoring stations based on their proximity to project construction features and registered spatial scale. DWR will confirm with the local air district that the selected stations are representative of ambient air quality for the study area(s).

act-008.name: Refined PM and NO2 Concentration Modeling
act-008.text: Conduct refined PM and NO2 concentration modeling: NO2 refined with seasonal and diurnal hourly background data and a Tier 3 1-hour NO2 analysis using EPA's ozone limiting method; PM2.5 and PM10 refined with site-specific silt loading and soil moisture measurements.
act-008.expectedEvidence: Copy of the refined PM and NO2 concentration modeling results.

locators.excerpt: Conduct refined PM and NO 2 in the air quality analysis as exceeding the SIL or ambient air quality standards (as appliable, depending on background concentrations). NO 2 modeling will be refined by using seasonal and diurnal hourly background NO concentration data for the local air quality study area. In addition, 2 ozone data from the same hourly meteorological period will be used to perform a Tier 3 analysis of 1-hour NO using the EPA’s ozone limiting 2 method. The refined PM modeling (both PM2.5 and PM10) will be performed using local site-specific representative data collected for silt loading and soil moisture content. These site-specific silt loading and soil moisture measurements will be used to determine emissions estimates for use in the refined PM concentration modeling.

act-009.name: SMAQMD Off-Site Mitigation Program
act-009.text: Develop the alternative or complementary off-site mitigation program to reduce NOx and PM10 emissions to the performance standard: a program funding emissions reduction projects through grants, ERCs or similar mechanisms, with pollutant-specific formulas to monetize and calculate reductions and a documented fee schedule basis (e.g., consistency with CARB Carl Moyer cost-effectiveness limits).
act-009.expectedEvidence: Copy of the off-site mitigation program, including pollutant-specific formulas and fee schedule basis.

locators.excerpt: DWR will develop an alternative or complementary off-site mitigation program to reduce NO and PM10 X emissions according to the performance standard described above. DWR will establish a program to fund emissions reduction projects through grants, ERCs, or similar mechanisms. Alternative fuel, low-emissions school buses, transit buses, and other vehicles.  Diesel engine retrofits and repowers.  Locomotive retrofits and repowers.  Electric vehicle or lawn equipment rebates.  Electric vehicle charging stations and plug-ins.  Video-teleconferencing systems for local businesses.  Telecommuting start-up costs for local businesses.  As part of its alternative or complementary off-site mitigation program, DWR will develop pollutant-specific formulas to monetize, calculate, and achieve emissions reductions in a cost-effective manner. DWR will document the fee schedule basis, such as consistency with the CARB’s Carl Moyer Program cost-effectiveness limits and capital recovery factors.

act-010.name: SMAQMD Emissions Reduction MOU
act-010.text: Enter into an MOU with SMAQMD to reduce NOx and PM10 emissions to the performance standard.
act-010.expectedEvidence: Copy of the executed MOU with SMAQMD.

locators.excerpt: DWR will enter into an MOU with SMAQMD to reduce NO and PM10 according X to the performance standard described above.

act-011.name: BAAQMD Annual Emissions Offset Report
act-011.text: Prepare annual emissions offset report verifying funded projects achieve a 1:1 reduction of construction NOx emissions: describe projects funded over the prior year, emissions reductions realized, compliance with mitigation requirements, and any corrective actions needed; finalize and post on DWR's website.
act-011.expectedEvidence: Copy of each finalized annual emissions offset report and its posting on DWR's website.

locators.excerpt: DWR will conduct annual reporting to verify and document that emissions reductions projects achieve a 1:1 reduction with construction emissions to ensure claimed offsets meet the required performance standard. Each report should describe the projects that were funded over the prior year, identify emissions reduction realized by the funded projects, document compliance with mitigation requirements, and identify corrective actions (if any) needed to ensure the offsetting program achieves the performance standards for NOx. Annual reports will be finalized and posted on DWR’s website by December 31 of the following year.

act-012.name: Bay Area Clean Air Foundation MOU
act-012.text: Enter into an MOU with the Bay Area Clean Air Foundation to reduce NOx emissions to the performance standard.
act-012.expectedEvidence: Copy of the executed MOU with the Bay Area Clean Air Foundation.

locators.excerpt: DWR will enter into an MOU with the (Clean Air) Foundation to reduce NO X according to the performance standard described above.

act-013.name: Bay Area Clean Air Foundation Offset Fee Payment
act-013.text: Pay the mitigation offset fee, set by the Foundation at the time of mitigation, plus an administrative fee of at least 5% of the total, and provide documentation of payment to DWR or its designated representative.
act-013.expectedEvidence: Receipt or other documentation of the offset and administrative fee payment provided to DWR.

locators.excerpt: The mitigation offset fee amount will be determined at the time of mitigation to fund one or more emissions reduction projects within the SFBAAB. The Foundation will require an additional administrative fee of no less than 5% of the total offset fee. The mitigation offset fee will be determined by the Foundation based on the type of projects available at the time of mitigation. Documentation of payment will be provided to DWR or its designated representative.

act-020.text: Pay the mitigation offset fee, set by DWR and SJVAPCD at the time of mitigation, plus an SJVAPCD administrative fee of at least 4% of the total, and provide documentation showing receipt of payment to DWR or its designated representative.
act-020.expectedEvidence: Documentation showing receipt of the offset fee and administrative fee payment.

locators.excerpt: The mitigation offset fee amount will be determined at the time of mitigation to fund one or more emissions reduction projects within the SJVAB (or in a nearby area of equal or higher nonattainment classification, as allowed under 40 CFR 93.158(2)). SJVAPCD will require an additional administrative fee of no less than 4% of the total offset fee. The mitigation offset fee will be determined by DWR and SJVAPCD based on the type of projects available at the time of mitigation. Documentation showing receipt of payment will be provided to DWR or its designated representative.

act-021.name: Locomotive Operating Hours Reports
act-021.text: Each contractor provides DWR monthly and annual reports of locomotive operating hours documenting compliance
act-021.expectedEvidence: Copies of the monthly and annual locomotive operating hours reports submitted to DWR.

locators.excerpt: Each contractor will provide DWR with monthly and annual reports of locomotive operating hours documenting compliance.

act-022.name: CARB Renewable Diesel Fleet Affirmation
act-022.text: Contractors submit to CARB an affirmation that the fleet complied with the renewable diesel mandate
act-022.expectedEvidence: Copies of each annual renewable diesel affirmation submitted to CARB.

locators.excerpt: Pursuant to the In-Use Off-Road Diesel-Fueled Fleets Regulation (In-Use Regulation), contractors will also be required to submit to CARB an affirmation that the fleet complied with the renewable diesel mandate in each year that annual reporting is required under the In-Use Regulation.

act-023.text: Provide a plan for enforcing the 5-minute equipment idling limit
act-023.expectedEvidence: Copy of the equipment idling enforcement plan.

locators.excerpt: Provide clear signage that posts this requirement for workers at the entrances to the site and provide a plan for the enforcement of this requirement.

act-024.name: On-Road Vehicle Compliance Reports
act-024.text: Each contractor provides DWR monthly and annual reports documenting compliance with the on-road vehicle requirements
act-024.expectedEvidence: Copies of the monthly and annual on-road vehicle compliance reports submitted to DWR.

locators.excerpt: Each contractor will provide DWR with monthly and annual reports documenting compliance.

act-025.text: Prepare an Air Quality Control Plan detailing equipment maintenance schedules and an Air Quality Management Plan documenting tire inflation program procedures
act-025.expectedEvidence: Copies of the Air Quality Control Plan and the Air Quality Management Plan.

locators.excerpt: Maintenance schedules will be detailed in an Air Quality Control Plan prior to commencement of construction. Procedures for the tire inflation program will be documented in an Air Quality Management Plan prior to commencement of construction.

act-026.name: Vessel Engine Operating Hours Reports
act-026.text: Each contractor provides DWR monthly and annual reports of vessel engine operating hours documenting compliance
act-026.expectedEvidence: Copies of the monthly and annual vessel engine operating hours reports and DWR's record of receipt.

locators.excerpt: Each contractor will provide DWR with monthly and annual reports of engine operating hours documenting compliance.

act-027.name: Equipment Operating Hours Reports
act-027.text: Each construction contractor provides DWR monthly and annual reports of equipment operating hours documenting compliance
act-027.expectedEvidence: Copies of each contractor's monthly and annual equipment operating hours reports as received by DWR.

locators.excerpt: Each contractor will also provide DWR with monthly and annual reports of equipment operating hours documenting compliance.

act-028.name: Fugitive Dust Control and Monitoring Plan
act-028.text: Prepare a Fugitive Dust Control and Monitoring Plan identifying the dust measures and submit it to CDFW in the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package(s).
act-028.expectedEvidence: Copy of the Fugitive Dust Control and Monitoring Plan as submitted to CDFW in the Construction Phase Authorization Package.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall identify measures within a Fugitive Dust Control and Monitoring Plan and submit the Plan to CDFW as part of the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package(s) (Condition of Approval 6.2).

act-029.name: Batch Plant BACT Dust Documentation
act-029.text: Batch plant managers provide DWR documentation that each batch plant meets the BACT dust standard during operation
act-029.expectedEvidence: Documentation from batch plant managers showing each batch plant meets the BACT dust standard.

locators.excerpt: Prior to beginning operations, batch plant managers must provide to DWR documentation that each batch plant meets this standard during operation.

act-030.name: Annual Renewable Diesel and Fuel Use Report
act-030.text: Each construction contractor provides DWR annual reports of renewable diesel purchase records and equipment and vehicle fuel consumption
act-030.expectedEvidence: Copies of the annual renewable diesel purchase and fuel consumption reports submitted to DWR.

locators.excerpt: Each project contractor responsible for construction of a project facility will provide DWR with monthly and annual reports of renewable diesel purchase records and equipment and vehicle fuel consumption.

act-031.name: Monthly Renewable Diesel and Fuel Use Report
act-031.text: Each construction contractor provides DWR monthly reports of renewable diesel purchase records and equipment and vehicle fuel consumption
act-031.expectedEvidence: Copies of the monthly renewable diesel purchase and fuel consumption reports submitted to DWR.

locators.excerpt: Each project contractor responsible for construction of a project facility will provide DWR with monthly and annual reports of renewable diesel purchase records and equipment and vehicle fuel consumption.

act-032.name: Annual GHG Reduction Report
act-032.text: Prepare annual GHG reduction report verifying selected strategies mitigate project emissions to net zero: describe strategies implemented over the prior year, summarize past, current and anticipated phasing, document compliance with Plan requirements, identify any corrective actions, and include offset retirement verification for any credits used; finalize and post on DWR's website.
act-032.expectedEvidence: Copy of the finalized annual GHG reduction report, including offset retirement verification, and its posting on DWR's website.

locators.excerpt: DWR will conduct annual reporting to verify and document that selected strategies achieve sufficient emissions reductions to mitigate project emissions to net zero. Each report should describe the GHG reduction strategies that were implemented over the prior year, summarize past, current, and anticipated project phasing, document compliance with Plan requirements, and identify corrective actions (if any) needed to ensure the Plan achieves the net zero performance standard. If GHG credits have been purchased to reduce emissions for the reporting year, the annual report must include copies of the offset retirement verification. Annual reports will be finalized and posted on DWR’s website by December 31 of the following year.

act-033.name: GHG Reduction Plan Phase Update
act-033.text: Update the GHG Reduction Plan before each phase: calculate anticipated phase emissions, prior-phase emissions and projected total net emissions; identify and quantify the reduction strategies for the phase per Section A.1; account for reductions achieved in prior phases; and in the final phase address operational emissions, including displaced CVP electricity emissions persisting beyond 2045 and the strategies to offset them.
act-033.expectedEvidence: Copy of the updated GHG Reduction Plan for each phase, issued before that phase starts.

locators.excerpt: Prior to the start of each phase, DWR will update the Plan to calculate the amount of GHG emissions anticipated in the covered phase, as well as emissions from prior phases (if applicable) and the projected total net emissions of the project. The Plan will identify the specific GHG reduction strategies that will be implemented to meet the net zero performance standard for the covered phase and quantify the expected reductions that will be achieved by each strategy. All emissions and reductions will be quantified in accordance with the requirements outlined in Section A.1. Subsequent amendments to the Plan will identify reductions that have been achieved during prior phases and determine if those reductions exceed emissions generated by the project. The final phase of the Plan must address operational emissions following construction, accounting for regulations adopted at that time that will reduce project emissions. Specifically, DWR will confirm statewide emissions from electricity transmission will achieve carbon neutrality no later than December 31, 2045, pursuant to SB 100 and the SF Switchgear 6 Regulation (or subsequent regulations). If GHG emissions from displaced purchases of CVP electricity are expected to persist beyond 2045, DWR will calculate the amount of GHG emissions anticipated until the industry achieves carbon neutrality. The final Plan will identify GHG reduction strategies that will be implemented by DWR to meet the net zero performance standard for these emissions.

act-034.name: Construction Contract VMT Reduction Provisions
act-034.text: Include provisions in construction contracts requiring contractors' crews and schedules to be coordinated to reduce construction employee VMT through park-and-ride lots and carpooling/vanpooling, and requiring that project plans and specifications be followed.
act-034.expectedEvidence: Copies of construction contracts containing the VMT reduction provisions.

locators.excerpt: Prior to construction, DWR will require that provisions be included in construction contracts stating that contractors’ crews and schedules are to be coordinated to reduce total construction employee VMT during construction periods through the use of park-and-ride lots and carpooling/vanpooling, and that the plans and specifications that are developed as part of the project alternatives design are being followed.

act-035.name: Construction Worker Ride Share Program
act-035.text: Develop a project-specific ride share program encouraging carpools, shuttle vans, transit passes, and secure bicycle parking for construction worker commutes
act-035.expectedEvidence: Copy of the construction worker ride share program description.

locators.excerpt: Develop a project specific ride share program to encourage carpools, shuttle vans, transit passes and/or secure bicycle parking for construction worker commutes.

act-036.name: GHG Reduction Plan
act-036.text: Retain a qualified consultant to develop a GHG Reduction Plan that mitigates GHG emissions from construction and displaced purchases of CVP electricity to net zero.
act-036.expectedEvidence: Copy of the completed GHG Reduction Plan prepared by the retained consultant.

locators.excerpt: Prior to issuance of the first construction or grading permit for the project, DWR will retain a qualified consultant to develop a GHG Reduction Plan (Plan) to mitigate GHG emissions resulting from construction and displaced purchases of CVP electricity to net zero.

act-037.name: Bird Strike Diverter Type Approval
act-037.text: Obtain CDFW approval of the bird strike diverter type.
act-037.expectedEvidence: CDFW approval of the bird strike diverter type.

locators.excerpt: 35 Permittee shall use the most effective and appropriate diverter for minimizing strikes, according to the best available science and as approved by CDFW.

act-038.name: Golden Eagle Survey Results
act-038.text: Submit all golden eagle survey results to USFWS and CDFW.
act-038.expectedEvidence: Copy of the golden eagle survey results and transmittal to USFWS and CDFW.

locators.excerpt: Survey methods will be determined based on coordination with USFWS and CDFW and all survey results will be submitted to USFWS and CDFW.

act-039.name: Golden Eagle Survey Methods Agreement
act-039.text: Agree golden eagle survey methods with USFWS and CDFW.
act-039.expectedEvidence: Written record of the golden eagle survey methods agreed with USFWS and CDFW.

locators.excerpt: Survey methods will be determined based on coordination with USFWS and CDFW and all survey results will be submitted to USFWS and CDFW.

act-040.name: White-Tailed Kite Survey Results
act-040.text: Provide white-tailed kite survey results to CDFW by phone or email.
act-040.expectedEvidence: Copy of the phone log or email transmitting white-tailed kite survey results to CDFW.

locators.excerpt: DWR will provide survey results to CDFW by phone or email no less than 5 days prior to commencement of construction activities.

act-041.name: White-Tailed Kite Nesting Survey Protocol Approval
act-041.text: Obtain CDFW approval of the white-tailed kite nesting survey protocol.
act-041.expectedEvidence: CDFW's written approval of the white-tailed kite nesting survey protocol.

locators.excerpt: Surveys for nesting white-tailed kites will be conducted, following a protocol approved by CDFW, within 30 days prior to construction to ensure nesting activity is documented prior to the onset of construction activity during the nesting season.

act-042.name: Archaeological Resources Management Plan (ARMP)
act-042.text: Prepare the Archaeological Resources Management Plan (ARMP) before field investigations, construction and ground disturbance, describing procedures to avoid, minimize and mitigate impacts with feasible avoidance as the first step, and procedures for phased identification, treatment, post-review discovery and monitoring recognizing Delta TCL character-defining features, and obtain approval from DWR's Archaeologist.
act-042.expectedEvidence: Copy of the ARMP and approval from DWR's Archaeologist.

locators.excerpt: DWR will prepare an Archaeological Resources Management Plan (ARMP) prior to field investigations and construction activities to guide the archaeological resources technical studies and resource-specific treatments to be conducted prior to and during construction activities. The ARMP will describe procedures that have been identified for avoiding, minimizing, and mitigating known or potential project impacts on archaeological resources. The first step in each procedure will be to implement feasible avoidance of archaeological resources.

This mitigation measure will be implemented through the development of an Archaeological Resources Management Plan (ARMP) subject to review and approval by DWR’s Archeologist. Native American archaeological resources that are character-defining features Cultural Resources, of the Delta TCL will be subject to Chapter 19, Mitigation Prepare and Implement an Archaeological Resources Measure CUL-3a: Management Plan with additional recognition of their role as part of the Delta TCL. As described in Mitigation Measure CUL-3a, the ARMP will include procedures for archaeological resources phased identification, archaeological treatment, post-review discovery, and archaeological monitoring.

act-043.name: Historic Resources Inventory Report
act-043.text: Prepare an inventory report summarizing recorded resources and evaluations, with a determination of which resources will be significantly impacted (demolition or material alteration of eligibility qualities).
act-043.expectedEvidence: Copy of the completed historic resources inventory report with its significant-impact determinations.

locators.excerpt: The recorded resources and the resource evaluations will be summarized in an inventory report. The inventory report will include a determination of whether individual resources qualifying as historical resources or historic properties will be subject to significant impacts. DWR will make such a finding if the project will result in the following: i. Demolish or materially alter the qualities that make the resource eligible for listing in the CRHR (CEQA Guidelines § 15064.5(b)(2)(A),(C)). ii. Demolish or materially alter the qualities that justify the inclusion of the resource on a local register or its identification in an historical resources survey meeting the requirements of California Public Resources Code Section 5024.1(g).

act-044.name: Built-Environment Treatment Plan (BETP)
act-044.text: Prepare a Built-Environment Treatment Plan (BETP) for each significantly impacted historical resource, by a qualified architectural historian, reviewing related noise and visual measures, and have it reviewed by relevant parties.
act-044.expectedEvidence: Copy of the BETP for each affected resource and record of review by relevant parties.

locators.excerpt: A BETP will be prepared for each built-environment historical resource with a significant impact from the project. For each BETP prepared, DWR will review mitigation measures from other resource topics in this EIR, such as noise and visual, to identify other mitigation activities related to the historical resource that is the subject of the treatment plan. The BETP will be prepared by an architectural historian who meets the Secretary of the Interior’s Standards with demonstrated experience preparing treatment for similar kinds of resources and reviewed by relevant parties prior to any demolition or ground-disturbing activity with potential to affect a built-environment resource.

act-045.name: Historic Resources Stabilization Plan
act-045.text: Prepare a stabilization plan for all resources based on the condition assessment.
act-045.expectedEvidence: Copy of the historic resources stabilization plan.

locators.excerpt: The condition assessment will be used to prepare a stabilization plan for all resources and to identify resources in poor condition.

act-046.name: Preconstruction Condition Assessment
act-046.text: Prepare a preconstruction condition assessment for all resources in the built-environment area of impact and include it in every BETP.
act-046.expectedEvidence: Copy of the preconstruction condition assessment included in each BETP.

locators.excerpt: A preconstruction condition assessment is required for all resources in the AI-BE and will be included in every BETP. Should damage caused by the project be questioned, these condition assessments will provide evidence of the preconstruction condition. ii.

act-047.name: HAER/HALS Recordation of Levees and Linear Features
act-047.text: Record levees and other linear historical features following HAER guidelines and their settings following HALS guidelines, with written and photographic documentation of character-defining features.
act-047.expectedEvidence: Copies of the completed HAER and HALS recordation reports.

locators.excerpt: The levees and other linear historical resource features will be recorded following HAER guidelines. Additionally, the settings will be recorded following HALS guidelines. These reports will include written and photographic documentation of the significant and character-defining features of these properties.

act-048.name: Paleontological Resources Monitoring and Mitigation Plan (PRMMP)
act-048.text: Retain a qualified professional paleontologist to develop a comprehensive Paleontological Resources Monitoring and Mitigation Plan (PRMMP) for the project.
act-048.expectedEvidence: Copy of the PRMMP prepared by the qualified professional paleontologist.

locators.excerpt: Before ground-breaking construction begins, DWR will retain a qualified professional paleontologist (as defined by the SVP Standard Procedures [Society of Vertebrate Paleontology 2010:10]) to develop a comprehensive Paleontological Resources Monitoring and Mitigation Plan (PRMMP) for the project, to help avoid destroying unique paleontological resources.

act-049.name: Paleontological Mitigation Monitoring Report
act-049.text: Prepare the paleontological mitigation monitoring report, covering effects, regulatory requirements, mitigation purpose, regional geology, stratigraphy, fossil distribution, methods, fossil recovery, significance, cross sections, maps, illustrations, and appendices including a specimen catalogue, locality descriptions, glossary, and a signed curation agreement with an approved repository.
act-049.expectedEvidence: Copy of the final paleontological mitigation monitoring report with the signed curation agreement.

locators.excerpt: The report will include, at a minimum, discussions of effects, regulatory requirements, purpose of mitigation, regional geologic context, project area stratigraphy, stratigraphic and geographic distribution of paleontological resources, field and laboratory methods and procedures, fossil recovery, and paleontological significance. The report will also include geological cross sections and stratigraphic sections depicting fossil discovery localities and excavated rock units; maps showing the activity location and vicinity, as well as geology and location of discovered fossil localities; appropriate illustrations depicting monitoring conditions, field context of collecting localities, and laboratory activities; and appendices including an itemized listing of catalogued fossil specimens, complete descriptions of all fossil collecting localities, an explanation of report acronyms and terms, and a signed curation agreement with an approved paleontological repository.

act-050.name: Paleontological Monitoring Report Guidelines
act-050.text: Establish paleontological mitigation monitoring report preparation guidelines consistent with SVP Standard Procedures and obtain DWR approval.
act-050.expectedEvidence: Copy of the paleontological monitoring report guidelines and DWR approval.

locators.excerpt: Mitigation monitoring report preparation guidelines will be established that are consistent with the SVP Standard Procedures guidelines (Society of Vertebrate Paleontology 2010) and approved by DWR.

act-051.name: Paleontological 90% Design Evaluation
act-051.text: Have a qualified individual review the 90% design submittals and produce an evaluation, considering depth of disturbance, construction technique, and alignment geology, that finalizes which construction activities involve highly sensitive units and specifies how mitigation applies across construction phases (monitoring locations and schedule).
act-051.expectedEvidence: Copy of the qualified individual's 90% design paleontological evaluation with monitoring locations and schedule.

locators.excerpt: DWR will have a qualified individual review the 90% design submittals to finalize the identification of construction activities involving geologic units considered highly sensitive for paleontological resources for the purpose of determining monitoring location and schedule. Evaluation will consider the anticipated depth of disturbance, the selected construction technique, and the geology of the alignment. The purpose of this evaluation will be to develop specific language identifying how the mitigation measures will be applied to the various phases of construction along the alignment (e.g., which areas would require monitors).

act-052.name: Tribal Cultural Resources Management Plan (TCRMP)
act-052.text: Prepare a Tribal Cultural Resources Management Plan (TCRMP) with procedures for Tribal consultation, identification, resource-specific treatment, Native American burial treatment, post-review discovery, and Tribal monitoring, and obtain approval from DWR's Archaeologist.
act-052.expectedEvidence: Adopted TCRMP and approval from DWR's Archaeologist.

locators.excerpt: This mitigation measure will be implemented through the development of a Tribal Cultural Resources Management Plan (TCRMP) subject to review and approval by DWR’s Archaeologist. DWR will prepare a TCRMP prior to field investigations and construction activities to guide continued consultation, refinement of resource identification, and procedures for developing resource-specific treatment to be conducted prior to and during construction activities. The TCRMP will describe procedures for avoiding, minimizing, and mitigating project impacts on known or potential Tribal cultural resources. The TCRMP will be developed during the permitting and design process and will be adopted within 2 years of certification of the EIR. The TCRMP will include procedures for the following: a. Tribal Consultation b. Principles and Procedures for the Identification of Tribal Cultural Resources c. Developing Resource-Specific Treatment d. Native American Burial Treatment e. Post-Review Discovery f. Tribal Monitoring

act-053.name: Burrowing Owl Artificial Burrow and Exclusion Plans
act-053.text: Develop Burrowing Owl Artificial Burrow and Exclusion Plans covering the relocation activities and obtain CDFW approval.
act-053.expectedEvidence: Copy of the Burrowing Owl Artificial Burrow and Exclusion Plans and CDFW approval.

locators.excerpt: DWR will develop Burrowing Owl Artificial Burrow and Exclusions Plans to be approved by CDFW prior to relocation, which will include the following relocation activities or revised relocation activities based on CDFW guidance and approval.

act-054.name: CRLF Compensation Habitat Location Approval
act-054.text: Obtain USFWS approval of the location for protected California red-legged frog habitat.
act-054.expectedEvidence: USFWS approval of the location for protected California red-legged frog habitat.

locators.excerpt: Fish and Wildlife Service 2002), at a location subject to USFWS approval.

act-055.name: CRLF Relocation Plan
act-055.text: Prepare and submit a CRLF relocation plan for USFWS written approval: USFWS-approved biologist names, relocation method if different, map, release sites outside exclusion fencing within 300 feet of the work area (or an agreed distance), and landowner written permission for each release site.
act-055.expectedEvidence: Copy of the CRLF relocation plan submitted to USFWS and USFWS's written approval.

locators.excerpt: At least 15 days prior to any ground disturbance activities, DWR will prepare and submit a relocation plan for USFWS’s written approval. The relocation plan will contain the name(s) of the USFWS-approved biologist(s) to relocate California red-legged frogs, the method of relocation (if different than described), a map, and a description of the proposed release site(s) outside of exclusion fencing and within 300 feet of the work area or at a distance otherwise agreed to by USFWS, and written permission from the landowner to use their land as a relocation site

act-056.name: CTS Mortality Reduction and Relocation Plan
act-056.text: Prepare a California tiger salamander Mortality Reduction and Relocation Plan naming the approved biologist(s), the relocation method, a map and description of release sites within 300 feet of the work area (or as agreed), and the landowner's written permission, submit it in the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package at least 30 days before any ground-disturbing activities and before initiating Covered Activities, and obtain USFWS and CDFW written approval.
act-056.expectedEvidence: Copy of the CTS Mortality Reduction and Relocation Plan as submitted and USFWS and CDFW written approvals.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall prepare a CTS Mortality Reduction and Relocation Plan (CTS Relocation Plan) and submit it to CDFW for written approval as part of the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package (see Condition of Approval 6.2) prior to initiating Covered Activities.

At least 30 days prior to any ground-disturbing activities, DWR will prepare and submit a relocation plan for USFWS’s and CDFW’s written approval. The relocation plan will contain the name(s) of the USFWS- and CDFW-approved biologist(s) to relocate California tiger salamanders, the method of relocation (if different than described), a map, and a description of the proposed release site(s) within 300 feet of the work area or at a distance otherwise agreed to by USFWS and CDFW, and written permission from the landowner to use their land as a relocation site.

act-057.name: CTS Preconstruction Watering Protocol
act-057.text: Prepare with CDFW a preconstruction watering protocol describing water application methodology (duration, timing, quantity) to stimulate CTS emergence on permanently impacted sites, and submit it in the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package.
act-057.expectedEvidence: Copy of the CTS preconstruction watering protocol as submitted in the Construction Phase Authorization Package.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall prepare in consultation with CDFW a preconstruction watering protocol and submit the protocol as part of the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6.2) describing the methodology to be used to stimulate CTS emergence from burrows on permanently impacted Project construction sites. The preconstruction watering protocol shall include but not be limited to the proposed water application methodology, discussing duration, timing, and quantity of water applied to mimic a rain event to stimulate CTS to emerge from burrows for capture and relocation, and any other pertinent information.

act-058.name: CTS Preconstruction Survey Results
act-058.text: Submit the CTS preconstruction survey results to CDFW in the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package for written approval.
act-058.expectedEvidence: CTS preconstruction survey results as submitted in the Construction Phase Authorization Package and CDFW written approval.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall submit the CTS preconstruction survey results to CDFW as part of the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package for written approval.

act-059.name: CTS Exclusion Barrier Design
act-059.text: Submit site-specific CTS exclusion barrier design and location details, based on preconstruction survey results, in the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package.
act-059.expectedEvidence: Copy of the CTS exclusion barrier design and location details as submitted to CDFW in the Construction Phase Authorization Package.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall submit site-specific CTS exclusion barrier design and location details to CDFW as part of the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package based on preconstruction survey results (see Condition of Approval 11.42).

act-060.name: CBB Nest Relocation Plan
act-060.text: Develop the Crotch bumble bee Nest Relocation Plan and submit it to CDFW for approval in the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package, before ground disturbance and prior to initiating Covered Activities.
act-060.expectedEvidence: Copy of the CBB Nest Relocation Plan as submitted in the Construction Phase Authorization Package and CDFW's approval.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall develop a CBB Nest Relocation Plan (CBB Plan) and submit it to CDFW as part of the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6.2) prior to initiating Covered Activities.
A bumble bee nest relocation plan will be prepared and submitted to CDFW for approval prior to ground disturbance.

act-061.name: CBB Presence Survey Results
act-061.text: Submit the site-level CBB presence survey results to CDFW in the Construction Phase Authorization Package.
act-061.expectedEvidence: CBB presence survey results as submitted in the Construction Phase Authorization Package.

locators.excerpt: Prior to initiation of ground disturbing Covered Activities for each Project Phase, site-level surveys shall be conducted consistent with CDFW-approved survey protocols (Condition of Approval 11.38) to determine whether CBB is present within or adjacent to proposed Covered Activities and submitted to CDFW as part of the appropriate Construction Phased Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6.2).

act-062.name: CBB Construction-Phase Survey Reporting
act-062.text: Report CBB construction-phase survey results to CDFW in the Monthly Compliance Reports and summarize them in each Annual Status Report.
act-062.expectedEvidence: Copies of the Monthly Compliance Reports and Annual Status Reports containing the CBB survey results.

locators.excerpt: The three survey efforts conducted during the Project construction phase(s) shall occur each year Covered Activities are expected to occur in suitable CBB habitat and shall be reported to CDFW by the Permittee within the Monthly Compliance Reporting (Condition of Approval 10.12) and summarized within each Annual Status Report (Condition of Approval 10.13).

act-063.name: CBB Buffer Zone Design Plan
act-063.text: Submit the CBB buffer zone design plan to CDFW in the Phase Authorization Package.
act-063.expectedEvidence: Copy of the CBB buffer zone design plan as submitted to CDFW in the Phase Authorization Package.

locators.excerpt: A CBB buffer zone design plan shall be submitted to CDFW as part of the appropriate Phase Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6.2).

act-064.name: GGS Survey Protocol Approval (COA 11.38)
act-064.text: Obtain CDFW written approval of the GGS survey protocol (COA 11.38), covering the preconstruction, burrow investigation (methodology per COA 11.62.2) and overwintering surveys, before the surveys it governs begin.
act-064.expectedEvidence: CDFW written approval of the GGS survey protocol.

locators.excerpt: The Designated Biologist(s) with assistance (if needed) from the Biological Monitor(s) shall conduct CDFW approved preconstruction surveys (Condition of Approval 11.38) within the boundaries of each Project site and include a three-foot buffer zone around the Project site, prior to initiation of any Covered Activities, including preconstruction activities, during the GGS active season (May 1 to October 1).

The first Project construction site GGS survey following approval of the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package (i.e., after a baseline preconstruction survey(s) has been completed) shall begin no more than seven days prior to initiating ground disturbing Covered Activities and be conducted consistent with CDFW-approved protocols (Condition of Approval 11.38).

Within the Project construction site and three-foot boundary, the Designated Biologist(s) with assistance (if needed) from the Biological Monitor(s) shall investigate all burrows within suitable upland habitat outside of established ESAs using a CDFW-approved methodology (see Condition of Approval 11.62.2) to determine whether the burrows are occupied by GGS.

In-channel work shall be limited to removal of accumulated sediments, acoustic monitoring, and aquatic vegetation removal in canals or other areas where GGS may be overwintering within 200 feet of the activity, until CDFW-approved surveys (Condition of Approval 11.38) have occurred and absence of overwintering GGS has been confirmed by the Designated Biologist(s).

If in-channel work needs to occur within the GGS active season, Permittee shall request written approval by CDFW and have the Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) survey following CDFW-approved protocols (Condition of Approval 11.38) for GGS prior to initiating work and monitor throughout the duration of Covered Activities for GGS.

act-065.name: GGS Mortality Reduction and Relocation Plan
act-065.text: Prepare the giant garter snake Mortality Reduction and Relocation Plan, with names of relocating biologists, relocation method if different, a map, release sites within 300 feet of the work area (or an agreed distance), and landowner written permission; submit it in the Construction Phase Authorization Package at least 30 days before any ground disturbance and before initiating Covered Activities, and obtain USFWS and CDFW written approval.
act-065.expectedEvidence: Copy of the GGS Relocation Plan as submitted in the Construction Phase Authorization Package and the USFWS and CDFW written approvals.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall prepare a GGS Mortality Reduction and Relocation Plan (GGS Relocation Plan) and submit it to CDFW as part of the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6.2) prior to initiating Covered Activities.

At least 30 days prior to any ground-disturbing activities, DWR will prepare and submit a relocation plan for USFWS’s and CDFW’s written approval. The relocation plan will contain the name(s) of the biologist(s) to relocate giant garter snakes, the method of relocation (if different than described), a map, and a description of the proposed release site(s) within 300 feet of the work area or at a distance otherwise agreed to by USFWS and CDFW, and written permission from the landowner to use their land as a relocation site.

act-066.name: GGS Exclusion Fencing Design
act-066.text: Submit the GGS exclusion fencing design and locations in the Construction Phase Authorization Package.
act-066.expectedEvidence: GGS exclusion fencing design and location plans as submitted in the Construction Phase Authorization Package.

locators.excerpt: The Permittee shall submit the fencing design and locations as part of the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package.

act-067.name: GGS Habitat and Disturbance Area Identification
act-067.text: Identify suitable GGS habitat, proposed surface-disturbing and ground-disturbance areas, and habitat removal in the Phase Authorization Package and obtain CDFW review and approval.
act-067.expectedEvidence: Copy of the Phase Authorization Package identifying GGS habitat and disturbance areas, with CDFW's approval.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall identify suitable GGS habitat, locations of proposed surface-disturbing activities, proposed areas for ground disturbance, and habitat removal within the appropriate Phase Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6.1 and 6.2) for CDFW review and approval prior to initiation of Covered Activities.

act-068.name: GGS Preconstruction Survey Results
act-068.text: Submit GGS preconstruction survey results to CDFW as part of the Construction Phase Authorization Package.
act-068.expectedEvidence: Copy of the GGS preconstruction survey results as submitted to CDFW in the Construction Phase Authorization Package.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall submit the GGS preconstruction survey results to CDFW as part of the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6.2).

act-069.name: Sandhill Crane Roosting Habitat Location Approval
act-069.text: Obtain CDFW approval of the location for created sandhill crane roosting habitat.
act-069.expectedEvidence: CDFW approval of the location for created sandhill crane roosting habitat.

locators.excerpt: Roosting habitat may be created on Bouldin Island or in suitable lands that provide connectivity between the Stone Lakes National Wildlife Refuge boundary and the Cosumnes River Preserve, subject to CDFW approval.

act-070.name: Crane Enhanced Foraging Habitat Management Plan
act-070.text: Complete a management plan for the enhanced crane foraging habitat, prepared with a qualified biologist experienced in crane habitat on cultivated lands, consistent with Appendix 13B, Section 13B.58.
act-070.expectedEvidence: Copy of the completed enhanced crane foraging habitat management plan.

locators.excerpt: A management plan for the enhanced habitat will be completed prior to establishing the habitat, in coordination with a qualified biologist with experience managing sandhill crane habitat on cultivated lands, or experience directing such management, consistent with the foraging Greater Sandhill habitat values in Appendix 13B, Section 13B.58, Crane.

act-071.name: Sandhill Crane Foraging Habitat Approval
act-071.text: Obtain CDFW approval of the protected greater sandhill crane foraging habitat.
act-071.expectedEvidence: CDFW's written approval of the protected greater sandhill crane foraging habitat.

locators.excerpt: Protect high- to very high-value foraging habitat for greater sandhill crane (corn, rice, wheat, and freshwater emergent wetlands), with at least 80% maintained in very high-value types (corn and rice) in any given year, subject to CDFW approval.

act-072.name: Crane Habitat Loss Evaluation
act-072.text: Using crane survey data and GIS, evaluate habitat loss and acres within the 50 dB contour, identify lands for minimization, and determine total affected and compensatory habitat required.
act-072.expectedEvidence: GIS analysis report quantifying crane habitat loss, acres within the 50 dB contour, minimization lands, and total compensatory habitat required.

locators.excerpt: The sandhill crane survey data will be used with GIS- based methods to evaluate habitat loss, the acres of habitat affected by the 50 dB sound level contour, to identify lands in fulfillment of minimization requirements, and to determine the total affected and compensatory habitat required, at the time of project footprint finalization.

act-073.name: Staten Island Crane Avoidance and Minimization Plan
act-073.text: Prepare a plan, based on the final Staten Island construction design and developed with the qualified biologist, containing all avoidance and minimization measures needed for no net decrease in crane use on Staten Island, and obtain wildlife agency review and approval.
act-073.expectedEvidence: Copy of the Staten Island crane avoidance and minimization plan and the wildlife agencies' approval.

deadline.milestone: Start of Construction on Staten Island

locators.excerpt: Prior to construction on Staten Island, the qualified biologist will coordinate with DWR to develop a strategy for achieving no net decrease in crane use on Staten Island using a combination of the measures described above, and prepare a plan based on the final construction design on Staten Island that includes all avoidance and minimization measures necessary for achieving no net decrease in crane use on Staten Island. This plan will be subject to review and approval by the wildlife agencies prior to its implementation.

act-074.name: Crane Lighting and Visual Disturbance Review
act-074.text: Have DWR's approach to the crane lighting and visual-disturbance measures reviewed and approved by a qualified biologist.
act-074.expectedEvidence: Qualified biologist's written approval of DWR's crane lighting and visual-disturbance approach.

locators.excerpt: DWR’s approach to satisfying these measures will be reviewed and approved by a qualified biologist prior to construction.

act-075.name: 50 dBA Sound Contour Map
act-075.text: Have a noise expert produce a 50 dBA sound level contour map for the type and location of construction, including existing levees and embankments.
act-075.expectedEvidence: Copy of the 50 dBA sound level contour map prepared by the noise expert.

locators.excerpt: Prior to construction, a noise expert will create a sound level contour map showing the 50 dBA sound level contour specific to the type and location of construction to occur in the area and existing noise barriers such as levees or embankments.

act-076.name: Vireo 60 dBA Sound Contour Map

act-076.expectedEvidence: Copy of the 60 dBA sound level contour map prepared by the noise expert for the planned construction in vireo habitat areas.

locators.excerpt: Prior to the construction, a noise expert will create a sound level contour map showing the 60 dBA sound level contour specific to the type and location of construction to occur in the area.

act-077.name: Vireo Riparian Restoration Plan
act-077.text: Prepare a riparian restoration plan identifying the location and methods for riparian creation or restoration, and obtain USFWS approval of it.
act-077.expectedEvidence: Copy of the riparian restoration plan and USFWS approval.

locators.excerpt: DWR will develop a riparian restoration plan that will identify the location and methods for riparian creation or restoration, and this plan will be subject to USFWS approval.

act-078.name: Mason's Lilaeopsis Restored Habitat Location Approval
act-078.text: Obtain CDFW approval of the locations for restored Mason’s lilaeopsis habitat.
act-078.expectedEvidence: CDFW's approval of the restored Mason's lilaeopsis habitat locations.

locators.excerpt: Restored habitat will be sited in locations subject to CDFW approval.

act-079.name: MALI Preconstruction Survey Results
act-079.text: Submit the MALI preconstruction survey results to CDFW in the Construction Phase Authorization Package and obtain written approval.
act-079.expectedEvidence: Copy of the MALI preconstruction survey results submitted to CDFW and CDFW's written approval.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall submit the preconstruction survey results to CDFW as part of the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6.2) for written approval prior to initiating Covered Activities.

act-080.name: MALI Mortality Reduction and Translocation Plan
act-080.text: Prepare the MALI Mortality Reduction and Translocation Plan, submit it to CDFW in the Construction Phase Authorization Package, and obtain written approval.
act-080.expectedEvidence: Copy of the MALI Translocation Plan as submitted in the Construction Phase Authorization Package and CDFW written approval.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall prepare a Mortality Reduction and Translocation Plan (MALI Translocation Plan) for MALI and submit it to CDFW as part of the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6.2) for written approval prior to the initiation of Covered Activities.

act-081.name: MALI Construction-Phase Survey Reporting
act-081.text: Report MALI construction-phase survey results to CDFW in the Monthly Compliance Reports and summarize them in each Annual Status Report.
act-081.expectedEvidence: Copies of the Monthly Compliance Reports and Annual Status Reports containing the MALI survey results.

locators.excerpt: Subsequent survey efforts conducted during the Project construction phase(s) shall occur each year Covered Activities are expected to occur in MALI habitat and shall be reported to CDFW by the Permittee within the Monthly Compliance Reporting (Condition of Approval 10.12) and summarized within each Annual Status Report (Condition of Approval 10.13).

act-082.name: MALI Buffer Zone Design Plan
act-082.text: Submit the MALI buffer zone design plan to CDFW for approval in the Phase Authorization Package.
act-082.expectedEvidence: Copy of the Phase Authorization Package containing the MALI buffer zone design plan and CDFW's approval.

locators.excerpt: The buffer zone design plan shall be submitted to CDFW for approval as part of the appropriate Phase Authorization Package.

act-083.name: Kit Fox Survey Results
act-083.text: Submit written kit fox survey results to USFWS and CDFW.
act-083.expectedEvidence: Copy of the written kit fox survey results and transmittal records showing submission to USFWS and CDFW.

locators.excerpt: Written results of the surveys will be submitted to USFWS and CDFW within 5 calendar days of the completion of surveys and prior to the beginning of ground disturbance and/or construction activities in San Joaquin kit fox modeled habitat.

act-084.name: SWHA Survey Protocol Approval
act-084.text: Obtain CDFW written approval of the SWHA survey protocol (COA 11.38) the surveys follow.
act-084.expectedEvidence: CDFW's written approval of the SWHA survey protocol.

locators.excerpt: The Designated Biologist(s) with assistance (if needed) from the Biological Monitor(s) shall conduct CDFW approved SWHA survey protocols (Condition of Approval 11.38) to identify the presence of suitable SWHA nest trees and known nest trees (occupied within one or more years of the past five years) within 0.5 miles of each preconstruction activity site, SCADA, transmission line, and access road sites, construction site, and postconstruction maintenance site, prior to initiation of any Covered Activities.

act-085.name: SWHA Mortality Reduction and Relocation Plan
act-085.text: Prepare the SWHA Mortality Reduction and Relocation Plan, phase-specific, describing mortality reduction strategies, buffer sizes, and the response procedure for each scenario, and submit it to CDFW in the Construction Phase Authorization Package.
act-085.expectedEvidence: Copy of the SWHA Relocation Plan as submitted to CDFW in the Construction Phase Authorization Package.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall develop a SWHA Mortality Reduction and Relocation Plan (SWHA Relocation Plan) and submit it to CDFW as part of the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6.2) prior to initiating Covered Activities. The SWHA Relocation Plan shall describe mortality reduction strategies and buffer sizes that Permittee will implement at the Project Site and shall describe the response procedure for each of the following scenarios, and shall be specific to the Project Phase:

act-086.name: Swainson's Hawk Foraging Habitat Location Approval
act-086.text: Obtain CDFW approval of the locations for protected Swainson’s hawk foraging habitat.
act-086.expectedEvidence: CDFW's written approval of the Swainson's hawk foraging habitat locations.

act-088.text: Map all existing or potential SWHA nesting and foraging sites and provide the maps to CDFW.

act-089.name: Swainson's Hawk Vegetation Restoration Plan
act-089.text: Prepare a Vegetation Restoration Plan specifying the replacement nest site location within preserved mitigation lands, and obtain CDFW’s written approval of it.
act-089.expectedEvidence: Copy of the Vegetation Restoration Plan and CDFW's written approval.

act-090.name: SWHA Preconstruction Survey Results
act-090.text: Submit SWHA preconstruction survey results to CDFW in the Construction Phase Authorization Package.
act-090.expectedEvidence: Copy of the Construction Phase Authorization Package containing the SWHA preconstruction survey results.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall submit the SWHA preconstruction survey results to CDFW as part of the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6.2).

act-091.name: Swainson's Hawk Survey Results Notice
act-091.text: Provide Swainson's hawk survey results to CDFW by phone or email.
act-091.expectedEvidence: Record of the phone call or email providing Swainson's hawk survey results to CDFW.

act-092.name: Swainson's Hawk Written Survey Report
act-092.text: Submit a written report of Swainson's hawk survey results to CDFW.
act-092.expectedEvidence: Copy of the written Swainson's hawk survey report and its transmittal to CDFW.

locators.excerpt: DWR will provide survey results to CDFW by phone or email no less than 5 days prior to commencement of construction activities, and in a written report within 30 days after commencement of construction activities.

act-093.name: SWHA Buffer Zone Design
act-093.text: Submit the SWHA buffer zone design and location to CDFW for approval in the Construction Phase Authorization Package.
act-093.expectedEvidence: Copy of the Construction Phase Authorization Package with the SWHA buffer zone design and CDFW's approval.
