act-094.name: Swainson's Hawk Nesting Habitat Location Agreement
act-094.text: Obtain CDFW’s written agreement on the location for restored and protected Swainson’s hawk nesting habitat.
act-094.expectedEvidence: CDFW's written agreement on the Swainson's hawk nesting habitat location.

locators.excerpt: Swainson’s hawk nesting habitat will be restored and protected at a location agreed upon in writing by CDFW at that time.

act-095.name: TRBL Nesting and Foraging Site Maps
act-095.text: Map all existing or potential TRBL nesting and foraging sites and provide the maps to CDFW in the Phase Authorization Package.
act-095.expectedEvidence: TRBL nesting and foraging site maps as submitted to CDFW in the Phase Authorization Package.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall map all existing or potential nesting or foraging sites and provide these maps to CDFW as part of the appropriate Phase Authorization Package (see Condition of Approval 10.3).

act-096.name: TRBL Survey Protocol Approval (COA 11.38)
act-096.text: Obtain CDFW written approval of the tricolored blackbird survey protocol (COA 11.38), including the breeding season and roosting survey protocols, before the surveys it governs begin.
act-096.expectedEvidence: CDFW's written approval of the TRBL survey protocol, including the breeding season and roosting protocols.

locators.excerpt: Prior to the commencement of Covered Activities for each Project Phase, the Designated Biologist(s) shall conduct a habitat assessment consistent with CDFW-approved protocols (Condition of Approval 11.38) to determine if existing or potential nesting or foraging sites are present within the Project site and include areas within three miles of Project sites, where feasible.

The Designated Biologist(s) with assistance (if needed) from the Biological Monitor(s) shall conduct CDFW approved TRBL survey protocols (Condition of Approval 11.38) to identify the presence of suitable nesting habitat and roosting habitat, within each preconstruction activity site, SCADA, transmission line and access road site, construction site, and maintenance area, prior to initiation of any Covered Activities.
Permittee shall use a breeding season survey protocol approved by CDFW as part of the TRBL survey protocol (Condition of Approval 11.38).
Permittee shall use a roosting survey protocol approved by CDFW as part of the TRBL survey protocol (Condition of Approval 11.38).

Occupied roost sites that are within the 300 feet no-activity buffer (Condition of Approval 11.87) shall be monitored daily by the Designated Biologist(s), with assistance (if needed) from the Biological Monitor(s), for at least four hours each day or until the roost site is no longer occupied and consistent with CDFW-approved TRBL survey protocol (Condition of Approval 11.38) to verify that Covered Activities are not disrupting roosting TRBL.
DWR will use a breeding season survey protocol approved in writing by CDFW.
DWR will use a roosting survey protocol approved in writing by CDFW.

act-097.name: TRBL Preconstruction Survey Results
act-097.text: Submit TRBL preconstruction survey results to CDFW in the Construction Phase Authorization Package.
act-097.expectedEvidence: Copy of the Construction Phase Authorization Package containing the TRBL preconstruction survey results.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall submit results of the preconstruction surveys to CDFW as part of the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6.2) prior to initiating Covered Activities.

act-098.name: TRBL Colony Buffer Zone Design
act-098.text: Submit the TRBL colony buffer zone design and location to CDFW for approval in the Construction Phase Authorization Package.
act-098.expectedEvidence: TRBL colony buffer zone design and location as submitted in the Construction Phase Authorization Package and CDFW approval.

locators.excerpt: The buffer zone design and location shall be submitted to CDFW for approval as part of the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package.

act-099.name: Preconstruction Survey Protocol Approval
act-099.text: Obtain CDFW approval of the preconstruction survey protocol (Condition 11.38).
act-099.expectedEvidence: CDFW approval of the preconstruction survey protocol.

locators.excerpt: The Designated Biologist(s) shall survey each Project construction site before Covered Activities resume, using the CDFW-approved preconstruction survey protocol (Condition of Approval 11.38).

act-100.name: TRBL Roost Buffer Zone Design
act-100.text: Submit the TRBL roost buffer zone design and location to CDFW for approval in the Construction Phase Authorization Package.
act-100.expectedEvidence: Copy of the Construction Phase Authorization Package with the TRBL roost buffer zone design and CDFW's approval.

locators.excerpt: The buffer zone design and location shall be submitted to CDFW for approval as part of the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package.

act-101.name: TRBL Nesting Habitat Location Approval
act-101.text: Obtain CDFW approval of the location for protected or restored tricolored blackbird nesting habitat.
act-101.expectedEvidence: CDFW written approval of the location for protected or restored tricolored blackbird nesting habitat.

locators.excerpt: To offset the loss of occupied tricolored blackbird nesting habitat, or previously occupied tricolored blackbird colonies (colonies that have been active within the past 15 years) will be permanently protected or restored and managed at a location subject to CDFW approval, and within 5 miles of the nearest breeding colony observed within the past 15 years if possible.

act-102.name: TRBL Mortality Reduction and Relocation Plan
act-102.text: Prepare the TRBL Mortality Reduction and Relocation Plan and submit it to CDFW in the Construction Phase Authorization Package.
act-102.expectedEvidence: Copy of the TRBL Relocation Plan as submitted to CDFW in the Construction Phase Authorization Package.

locators.excerpt: The Designated Biologist(s) shall prepare a TRBL Mortality Reduction and Relocation Plan (TRBL Relocation Plan) and submit it to CDFW as part of the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package prior to commencing Covered Activities (Condition of Approval 6.2).

act-103.name: TRBL Nesting and Roosting Site Maps
act-103.text: Map all existing or potential TRBL nesting and roosting sites and provide the maps to CDFW.
act-103.expectedEvidence: Copy of the TRBL nesting and roosting site maps and their transmittal to CDFW.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall map all existing or potential nesting or roosting sites and provide these maps to CDFW (see Condition of Approval 10.3).

act-104.name: TRBL Breeding Foraging Habitat Location Approval
act-104.text: Obtain CDFW approval of the location for protected tricolored blackbird breeding foraging habitat.
act-104.expectedEvidence: CDFW's written approval of the tricolored blackbird breeding foraging habitat location.

locators.excerpt: To support protected or restored tricolored blackbird nesting habitat, or to offset the loss of breeding foraging habitat (i.e., foraging habitat used during the breeding season), breeding foraging habitat will be protected using a site protection Site Protection Instruments. instrument as described in Section 3F.4.2.2, Breeding foraging habitat will be protected at a location subject to CDFW approval within 6 kilometers of (1) protected or restored nesting habitat that is managed for tricolored blackbird or (2) a recently or historically (to encourage recolonization) occupied tricolored blackbird nesting habitat.

act-105.name: TRBL Nesting Sites on Phase Plans
act-105.text: Note TRBL nesting sites (currently occupied and occupied within the last five years) on the plans submitted in the Phase Authorization Package.
act-105.expectedEvidence: Phase Authorization Package plans showing current and recent TRBL nesting sites.

locators.excerpt: Nesting sites, including both currently occupied nesting sites and sites known to have been occupied within the last five years, shall be noted on plans that are submitted as a part of a Phase Authorization Package (see Condition of Approval 6.1 and 6.2).

act-106.name: Cuckoo Riparian Restoration Plan
act-106.text: Prepare a riparian restoration plan identifying the location and methods for riparian creation or restoration, and obtain USFWS approval of it.
act-106.expectedEvidence: Copy of the riparian restoration plan and USFWS's approval.

locators.excerpt: DWR will develop a riparian restoration plan that will identify the location and methods for riparian creation or restoration, and this plan will be subject to USFWS approval.

act-107.name: Fish Rescue and Salvage Plan
act-107.text: Develop a fish rescue and salvage plan with detailed procedures to minimize fish stranding during cofferdam placement and removal, submit it in the appropriate Phase Authorization Package before initiating Covered Activities and before in-water construction with potential to strand fish, and obtain written approval and an authorization letter from NMFS, USFWS and CDFW.
act-107.expectedEvidence: Copy of the fish rescue and salvage plan, CDFW's written approval, and the NMFS, USFWS and CDFW authorization letter.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall collaborate with CDFW to develop a fish rescue and salvage plan that describes procedures for fish rescue and salvage to minimize the number of Covered Fish Species stranded during Project construction activities. Permittee shall submit the fish salvage plan to CDFW as part of the appropriate Phase Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6.2) for review and approval prior to initiating Covered Activities.

Fish rescue and salvage plans will be developed by DWR or its contractors and will include detailed procedures for fish rescue and salvage to minimize the number of fish subject to stranding during placement and removal of cofferdams. The plans will be approved by NMFS, USFWS, and CDFW.

A draft plan will be submitted to the fish and wildlife agencies for review and approval. An authorization letter from NMFS, USFWS, and CDFW will be required before in-water construction activities with the potential for stranding fish can proceed.

act-108.name: Fish Salvage Annual Summary
act-108.text: Describe fish salvage plan implementation and summarize salvage results (date, time, location, method, species, number, age, condition, release location and time) in the Annual Status Report.
act-108.expectedEvidence: Annual Status Report section describing fish salvage plan implementation and summarizing salvage results.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall describe implementation of the fish salvage plan and provide a summary of the results of the fish salvage operations (including date, time, location, comments, method of capture, fish species, number of fish, approximate age, condition, release location, and release time) to CDFW as part of the Annual Status Report (Condition of Approval 10.13).

act-109.name: ESA and Burrow Area Identification
act-109.text: Identify proposed ESAs and areas with suitable burrows or refugia in the Phase Authorization Package and obtain CDFW review and approval.
act-109.expectedEvidence: Phase Authorization Package section identifying proposed ESAs and burrow areas and CDFW approval.

locators.excerpt: Proposed ESAs and any area containing suitable burrows or refugia shall be identified as part of the appropriate Phase Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6.1 and 6.2) for CDFW review and approval prior to the initiation of any Covered Activity.

act-110.name: Conceptual Exclusion Fencing Plan
act-110.text: Submit a conceptual exclusion fencing plan to USFWS and CDFW.
act-110.expectedEvidence: Copy of the conceptual exclusion fencing plan and the transmittal to USFWS and CDFW.

locators.excerpt: A conceptual fencing plan will be submitted to USFWS and CDFW prior to the start of construction and the exclusion fencing will be shown on the final construction plans.

act-111.name: Final Invasive Plant Species Management and Control Plan
act-111.text: Develop a final Invasive Plant Species Monitoring, Management, and Control Plan for each construction site, in consultation with CDFW and local experts, covering preconstruction conditions, annual percent-cover monitoring, annual reporting, Cal-IPC mapping and treatment guidance, and control techniques, and submit it to CDFW with each Construction Phase Authorization Package.
act-111.expectedEvidence: Copy of the final IPSMMCP as submitted to CDFW with the Construction Phase Authorization Package.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall submit a completed final IPSMMCP to CDFW for each Construction Phase Authorization Package, and submit related reporting as part of the Annual Status Report (Condition of Approval 10.13).

DWR will also develop an invasive plant species management and control plan prior to construction for each construction site. The plan will ensure that invasive plant species and populations are kept below preconstruction abundance and distribution levels and will be developed in consultation with CDFW and local experts (e.g., California Invasive Plant Council). The invasive plant species management plan will include the following elements. Documentation of preconstruction conditions.  Annual monitoring to document percent cover of native and nonnative invasive  plant species. Guidance provided by the California Invasive Plant Council (2012) for weed  mapping field protocols and treatment plans, with particular attention given to species rated as high-level invasives with a negative ecological impact in California (California Invasive Plant Council 2006). Invasive plant species management and control techniques employed where  necessary.

act-112.name: Draft IPSMMCP (Pre-implementation PAP)
act-112.text: Develop a draft Invasive Plant Species Monitoring, Management, and Control Plan with CDFW and local invasive species experts such as Cal-IPC, keeping invasives below preconstruction levels, incorporating the approved sampling methodology, pre-Project conditions, annual percent-cover monitoring, yearly invasive type, location and quantity records, and prevention BMPs; include it in the Pre-implementation Phase Authorization Package.
act-112.expectedEvidence: Copy of the draft IPSMMCP as included in the Pre-implementation Phase Authorization Package.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall consult with CDFW and local invasive species experts such as the California Invasive Plant Council to develop a draft invasive plant species monitoring, management, and control plan (IPSMMCP) prior to starting Covered Activities that ensures invasive plant species and populations are kept below preconstruction distribution levels. The draft IPSMMCP shall be included in the Pre-implementation Phase Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6.1). The IPSMMCP shall incorporate the CDFW-approved sampling methodology and include (1) documentation of pre-Project conditions; (2) annual monitoring to document percent cover of native and nonnative invasive plant species throughout each Project site; (3) the type, location, and quantity of all observed invasive plant species for the year prior to commencement of Covered Activities, the current monitoring year, and any prior monitoring years during construction and operations; and (4) best management practices utilized to avoid introduction of control invasive plant species.

act-113.name: Annual Invasive Plant Report
act-113.text: Prepare an annual invasive plant report with baseline and annual survey results, the type, location and quantity of invasive species, percent cover for the preconstruction year, current year and prior years, and management problems and remedial actions, and submit it to CDFW in the Annual Status Report.
act-113.expectedEvidence: Copy of each annual invasive plant report as submitted to CDFW in the Annual Status Report.

locators.excerpt: The pre-Project baseline condition survey results and subsequent annual surveying shall be utilized by the Permittee in the Invasive Plan Species Monitoring, Management, and Control Plan (IPSMMCP Condition of Approval 11.19.1) and reporting provided to CDFW in the Annual Status Report (Condition of Approval 10.13).

Permittee shall submit a completed final IPSMMCP to CDFW for each Construction Phase Authorization Package, and submit related reporting as part of the Annual Status Report (Condition of Approval 10.13).

Preparation of an annual report that includes the type, location, and quantity of the  invasive plant species; the percent cover of invasive plant species for (i) the year prior to preconstruction, (ii) the current monitoring year, and (iii) any prior monitoring years; and a description of any management problems and remedial actions taken.

act-114.name: Invasive Plant Baseline Sampling Methodology

act-114.expectedEvidence: Copy of the invasive plant sampling methodology as submitted to CDFW in the Phase Authorization Package.

locators.excerpt: The Designated Biologist(s) qualified to do botanical surveys and approved by CDFW shall submit the sampling methodology to CDFW as part of the appropriate Phase Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6.1 and 6.2).

act-115.name: Phytophthora Prevention BMPs

act-115.expectedEvidence: Copy of the Phase Authorization Package containing the CDFW-approved Phytophthora prevention BMPs.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall incorporate best management practices approved by CDFW as part of the appropriate Project Phase Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6.1 and 6.2) to minimize risk of introduction and/or spread of molds such as Phythophthora spp. within the Project Area as introduction or exacerbation in the Project Area may reduce viability of restoration plantings and already occurring native plant species.

act-116.expectedEvidence: Copy of each annual plant mitigation monitoring report and CDFW's compliance determination.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall provide the number and approximate location(s) of proposed culverts designed for wildlife road under-crossings within the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package for CDFW- approval.

act-119.name: Contamination Investigation Work Plan Approval

act-119.expectedEvidence: Copy of the investigation work plan and the regulatory oversight agency's approval.

locators.excerpt: All environmental investigation, sampling, and remediation activities associated with properties in the project area will be conducted under a work plan approved by the regulatory oversight agency (e.g., DTSC, EPA) and will be conducted by an appropriate environmental professional.

act-120.name: Phase I Environmental Site Assessment

act-120.expectedEvidence: Copy of the completed Phase I environmental site assessment report.

locators.excerpt: Prior to construction, DWR will conduct a Phase I environmental site assessment in conformance with the American Society for Testing and Materials Standard Practice E1527-05.

act-121.name: Fire Prevention and Control Plan
act-121.text: Develop a fire prevention and control plan in consultation with the appropriate fire suppression agencies, covering prevention and suppression measures by activity, the affected jurisdictions' policies and standards, the minimum listed components, and an explanation for any component omitted
act-121.expectedEvidence: Copy of the fire prevention and control plan and record of consultation with fire suppression agencies.

locators.excerpt: DWR will develop and implement a fire prevention and control plan in consultation with the appropriate fire suppression agencies to verify that the necessary fire prevention and response methods are included in the plan. The plan will include fire prevention and suppression measures as appropriate for different activities and will consider the policies and standards in the affected jurisdictions. At a minimum, the following components, as applicable, will be included in the plan. If a component is not applicable to a specific activity, DWR or its contractor will explain in the plan why that component or a portion thereof is not included in the plan.

act-122.name: Hazardous Materials Handling and Disposal Protocol
act-122.text: Establish the protocol for proper handling and disposal of hazardous materials.
act-122.expectedEvidence: Copy of the hazardous materials handling and disposal protocol.

locators.excerpt: A specific protocol for the proper handling and disposal of hazardous materials will be established before construction activities begin, will be implemented during project construction, and will be enforced by DWR.

act-123.name: Site-Specific Hazardous Materials Management Plans
act-123.text: Prepare site-specific hazardous materials management plans from each project contractor before initiating Covered Activities, covering hazardous materials used or stored on site and known historic contamination, material types, emergency agency phone numbers, cleanup procedures, spill response procedures, and handling and disposal protocol.
act-123.expectedEvidence: Copies of the site-specific hazardous materials management plans for each contractor.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall develop and implement a hazardous materials management plan (HMMP) prior to initiating Covered Activities. HMMPs shall be prepared for site-specific Project construction activities to address hazardous materials present on site and known historic site contamination. The HMMPs shall provide detailed information on the types of hazardous materials used or stored at all sites; phone numbers of applicable city, county, state, and federal emergency response agencies; primary, secondary, and final cleanup procedures; emergency-response procedures in case of a spill of toxic chemicals or other hazardous waste (see Condition of Approval 11.22); a specific protocol for the proper handling and disposal of hazardous materials; and other applicable information that shall be implemented during Project construction and enforced by Permittee.

DWR will require that each project contractor responsible for construction of a project facility or project develop and implement a hazardous materials management plan (HMMP) before beginning construction. Multiple HMMPs will be prepared for the overall project construction activities, each considering site-specific conditions such as hazardous materials present on site and known historic site contamination. The HMMPs will provide detailed information on the types of hazardous materials used or stored at all sites associated with the water conveyance facilities (e.g., intake pumping plants, maintenance facilities); phone numbers of applicable city, county, state, and federal emergency response agencies; primary, secondary, and final cleanup procedures; emergency-response procedures in case of a spill; and other applicable information.

act-124.name: Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans
act-124.text: Have each construction contractor prepare a site-specific Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan for each project construction site per 40 CFR 112, addressing the spill-prevention actions and spill-response actions including emergency notification procedures and minimizing effects of oil spills during construction and operation, and submit the plans to CDFW in the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package for review and confirmation of consistency with the ITP before initiating Covered Activities.
act-124.expectedEvidence: Copies of the site-specific SPCC plans as submitted in the Construction Phase Authorization Package and CDFW confirmation of consistency.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall ensure compliance with all construction stormwater permitting requirements and shall develop and implement a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan (SPCCP) at each Project construction site to control short-term and long-term effects associated with construction- generated stormwater runoff. Each SPCCP shall address site-specific actions used to prevent spills and actions that will be taken should any spills occur, including emergency notification procedures. The SPCCPs shall be developed and implemented to minimize effects from spills of oil or oil- containing products (i.e., gasoline, diesel fuel, motor oil, hydraulic fluid, aviation fuel, oil-based paint, oil-based paint thinner, roofing tar, and petroleum-based solvents) during Project construction and operation.

Permittee shall submit the SPCC plans to CDFW as part of the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6.2) for CDFW’s review and confirmation of consistency with this ITP prior to initiating Covered Activities.

DWR will require that each project contractor responsible for construction of a project facility or project develop and implement a spill prevention, containment, and countermeasure plan (SPCCP) for each project site (typically required to meet state and federal water quality requirements). Multiple SPCCPs will be prepared for project construction activities, each taking into account site-specific conditions. The SPCCPs will be developed in accordance with the regulatory requirements of Title 40 of the Code of Federal Regulations (CFR), Part 112, or the Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Rule under the Oil Pollution Act of 1990, which includes requirements for oil spill prevention, preparedness, and response to prevent oil discharges to navigable waters of the United States and adjoining shorelines. Each SPCC plan will address 20 actions used to prevent spills in addition to specifying actions that will be taken should any spills occur, including emergency notification procedures.

act-125.name: Mitigation Site Mosquito Management Plan
act-125.text: Develop a mosquito management plan, with BMPs and proposed mosquito monitoring, for the Bouldin Island and I-5 Ponds compensatory mitigation sites where freshwater marsh, lake/pond, riparian, or seasonal wetland habitat is created or enhanced, and submit it to the San Joaquin County MVCD for review during design.
act-125.expectedEvidence: Copy of the mosquito management plan and record of review by the San Joaquin County MVCD.

locators.excerpt: To aid in vector management and control, DWR will develop and implement a mosquito management plan for the compensatory mitigation sites where freshwater marsh, lake/pond, riparian, or seasonal wetland habitat is created/enhanced on Bouldin Island and at the I-5 Ponds.

Consultation will include, but may not be limited to, review of the mosquito management plan and best management practices (BMPs) to be implemented at the compensatory mitigation sites, review of proposed mosquito monitoring efforts at the sites, and assistance with monitoring efforts where feasible.

act-126.expectedEvidence: Copy of the final bat replacement habitat and monitoring plans and records of coordination with CDFW.

locators.excerpt: Replacement habitat on bridges/overpasses and associated Caltrans Bat Mitigation: A Guide to Developing monitoring will follow the guidance in Feasible and Effective Solutions (Johnston et al. 2019), or the most recent guidance available at that time, with final plans developed in coordination with CDFW.

act-127.expectedEvidence: CDFW approval of the replacement roosting habitat plans and location.

locators.excerpt: Evictions will not occur until temporary or permanent replacement roosting habitat is established at a location subject to CDFW approval. Replacement habitat plans will be reviewed and approved by CDFW.

act-128.name: Special-Status Species Habitat Design Guidelines

act-128.expectedEvidence: Copy of the special-status species habitat design guidelines including the no-net-loss framework.

deadline.milestone: Start of Compensatory Mitigation Site Development

locators.excerpt: These design guidelines will address critical life functions for special-status species. It will also include a framework to ensure that any substantial habitat loss or conversion associated with compensatory mitigation site development are offset so that there would be no net loss in habitat value for special-status species.

act-129.name: Stay-Ahead Mitigation Land Documentation

act-129.expectedEvidence: Copy of the submitted Annual Status Report containing the stay-ahead HM land documentation for each Covered Species.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall include in its Annual Status Report, pursuant to Condition of Approval 10.13, documentation demonstrating that cumulative HM lands permanently protected (and restored where required) for each Covered Species is at least 10 percent (10%) greater than the proportional cumulative impacts to each Covered Species habitat, based on the requirements shown in Table 12-1 and Table 12-2 below (10 percent stay-ahead requirements). The Annual Status Report shall also demonstrate that land and identified habitat features anticipated to be disturbed over the succeeding twelve months in accordance with Conditions of Approval 10.3 and 10.5, will be preceded by HM lands permanent protection, and restoration if required.

act-139.text: Submit the HMMPs to CDFW in the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package for review and confirmation of consistency with the ITP.
act-139.expectedEvidence: Copy of the HMMPs as submitted in the Construction Phase Authorization Package and CDFW confirmation of consistency.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall submit the HMMPs to CDFW as part of the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6.2) for CDFW’s review and confirmation of consistency with this ITP prior to initiating Covered Activities.

act-140.name: Nontidal Freshwater Emergent Wetland Restoration and Monitoring Plan
act-140.text: Prepare a restoration and monitoring plan for nontidal freshwater perennial emergent wetland describing how it will be created and monitored, including funding mechanisms, long-term management measures, and agency reporting requirements.
act-140.expectedEvidence: Copy of the nontidal freshwater perennial emergent wetland restoration and monitoring plan.

locators.excerpt: A restoration and monitoring plan will be developed and implemented concurrently with project construction. The plan will describe how nontidal freshwater perennial emergent wetland will be created and monitored, including funding mechanisms and appropriate long-term management measures, and agency reporting requirements.

act-141.name: Vegetation Restoration Plan for Temporary Disturbance
act-141.text: Prepare a vegetation restoration plan for revegetating temporary disturbance footprints for each covered species habitat, including post-disturbance grading to elevations and hydrology suitable for Mason's lilaeopsis where unoccupied suitable habitat is temporarily affected
act-141.expectedEvidence: Copy of the vegetation restoration plan for the temporary disturbance footprints.

locators.excerpt: A vegetation restoration plan will be prepared to facilitate revegetation of the temporary disturbance footprints on-site for each of the covered species habitats. Where there are temporary impacts to potentially suitable but unoccupied Mason’s lilaeopsis masonii) (Lilaeopsis habitat, the vegetation restoration plan will require post- disturbance grading to elevations and hydrology suitable for Mason’s lilaeopsis.

act-142.name: Tidal Perennial Restoration Siting and Design Criteria
act-142.text: Develop siting, design, and performance criteria for tidal perennial habitat restoration based on assessments of topography, local hydrodynamics, and sediment transport.
act-142.expectedEvidence: Copy of the tidal perennial restoration siting, design and performance criteria.

locators.excerpt: Siting, design, and performance criteria for tidal perennial habitat restoration will be developed based on assessments of topography, local hydrodynamic conditions, and sediment transport.

act-143.name: Channel Margin Restoration Site Approval
act-143.text: Obtain NMFS and CDFW approval of channel margin restoration sites.
act-143.expectedEvidence: NMFS and CDFW written approval of the channel margin restoration sites.

locators.excerpt: Sites for channel margin restoration will be subject to approval by NMFS and CDFW.

act-144.name: Updated Construction Noise Modeling
act-144.text: Update the construction noise modeling and analysis for all facilities using test pile sound-level results to determine where pile driving would affect receptors under daytime and nighttime criteria.
act-144.expectedEvidence: Copy of the updated construction noise modeling and analysis based on the test pile results.

locators.excerpt: Noise modeling will be updated based on result of test pile sound-level monitoring. 14 Updated sound-level modeling will be used to determine where impacts would occur to receptors due to pile driving, to update the construction noise analysis for all facilities, based on daytime and nighttime noise level criteria described in Section Thresholds of Significance.

act-145.name: 50 dBA Sound Contour Map
act-145.text: Have a noise expert produce a sound level contour map showing the 50 dBA contour for the type and location of construction, including existing noise barriers such as levees or embankments.
act-145.expectedEvidence: Copy of the 50 dBA sound level contour map prepared by the noise expert.

locators.excerpt: Prior to 11 eq construction, a noise expert will create a sound level contour map showing the 50 dBA sound level contour specific to the type and location of construction to occur in the area and existing noise barriers such as levees or embankments.

act-146.name: 60 dBA Sound Contour Map
act-146.text: Have a noise expert produce a sound level contour map showing the 60 dBA contour for the type and location of construction in the area.
act-146.expectedEvidence: Copy of the 60 dBA sound level contour map prepared by the noise expert.

locators.excerpt: Prior to the construction, a noise expert will create a sound level contour map showing the 60 dBA sound level contour specific to the type and location of construction to occur in the area.

act-147.name: Construction Noise Control Plan
act-147.text: Develop a construction noise control plan covering pre-construction actions, sound-level monitoring, best noise control practices, and noise barriers where construction sound levels are anticipated to exceed daytime or nighttime criteria.
act-147.expectedEvidence: Copy of the final construction noise control plan.

locators.excerpt: DWR and project contractors will develop and implement a noise control plan consisting of pre-construction actions, sound-level monitoring, best noise control practices, and noise barriers constructed in locations where sound levels from construction are anticipated to exceed daytime or nighttime noise level criteria.

act-148.name: Annual Pile Driving Monitoring Summary
act-148.text: Provide annual pile driving monitoring information in the Annual Status Report, summarizing observations, evaluating sound abatement plan performance, and describing exceedances and remediation measures.
act-148.expectedEvidence: Annual Status Report section summarizing pile driving monitoring, sound abatement performance and exceedances.

locators.excerpt: • Providing annual pile driving monitoring information to CDFW as part of the Annual Status Report (Condition of Approval 10.13). Reported information shall include a summary of pile driving monitoring observations over the course of each construction year, including an evaluation of the underwater sound abatement plan performance measures, as well as a description of exceedances of hydroacoustic thresholds and measures implemented to remediate impacts to Covered Species.

act-149.name: Underwater Sound Control and Abatement Plan
act-149.text: Develop an underwater sound control and abatement plan with CDFW (activity timing, best practices and equipment to minimize underwater construction noise on fish, especially from impact pile driving), submit it in the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package before initiating Covered Activities and any in-water impact pile driving, and obtain written approval from NMFS, USFWS and CDFW.
act-149.expectedEvidence: Copy of the underwater sound control and abatement plan and the written approvals from NMFS, USFWS and CDFW.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall coordinate with CDFW to develop an underwater sound abatement plan outlining specific measures to avoid and minimize the effects of underwater construction noise on Covered Fish Species. The underwater sound abatement plan shall be provided to CDFW as part of the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6.2) for review and written approval prior to initiating Covered Activities.

DWR will implement an underwater sound control and abatement plan outlining specific measures such as changing the time of activities, best practices, and equipment that will be used to avoid and minimize the effects of underwater construction noise on fish, particularly the underwater noise effects associated with impact pile driving activities. The underwater sound control and abatement plan will be provided to the appropriate fish and wildlife agencies for their review and approval prior to any in- water impact pile driving activities.

act-150.name: In-Water Pile Driving Information
act-150.text: Provide planned in-water pile driving information (locations, schedules, activities, expected effects, agency communications on channel closures) in the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package and obtain CDFW written approval.
act-150.expectedEvidence: Copy of the Construction Phase Authorization Package with the in-water pile driving information and CDFW's written approval.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall provide information regarding planned in-water pile driving, including the site location(s), schedules, work activities, anticipated effects to water quality or Covered Species, and communications with other agencies and organizations with site-specific details regarding any temporary partial channel closures within the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6.2) for CDFW review and written approval, prior to initiating in- water Covered Activities.

act-151.name: Pile Driving Plan
act-151.text: Develop a pile driving plan explaining how design minimizes pile count, piles and strikes per day, and duration and timing of pile driving inside and outside work windows, and submit it to CDFW in the Pre-implementation Phase Authorization Package for written approval.
act-151.expectedEvidence: Copy of the pile driving plan as submitted in the Pre-implementation Phase Authorization Package and CDFW written approval.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall develop a pile driving plan to minimize the impacts of pile driving on Covered Fish Species. Permittee shall submit the pile driving plan to CDFW as part of the Pre-implementation Phase Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6.1) for review and written approval prior to initiating Covered Activities. The pile driving plan shall include an explanation of how the Project engineering design minimizes the total number of pilings, the number of pilings that will be driven per day with an impact or vibratory pile driver, the number of pile driving strikes per day, the duration of pile driving within the in-water work windows, the duration and timing of impact or vibratory pile driving outside the in-water work windows, and the duration of pile driving within the daily in-water construction window.

act-152.name: Biological Monitor Qualifications Approval
act-152.text: Present the qualifications of biological monitors to the fish and wildlife agencies for review and written approval
act-152.expectedEvidence: Written approval of biological monitor qualifications from the fish and wildlife agencies.

locators.excerpt: The qualifications of the biologist(s) will be presented to the fish and wildlife agencies for review and written approval, consistent with permits and authorizations.

act-153.name: Environmental Compliance Monitoring Plan
act-153.text: Prepare a site- or activity-specific environmental compliance monitoring plan to monitor, enforce, and document measures protecting special-status species, their habitats, critical habitat, and sensitive natural communities; DWR approves if prepared by contractor
act-153.expectedEvidence: Copy of the environmental compliance monitoring plan and DWR approval where prepared by a contractor.

locators.excerpt: Before initiating construction, DWR or its contractor, with DWR approval, will prepare a site or activity-specific environmental compliance monitoring plan to monitor, enforce and document measures to protect special-status fish, wildlife, plant species, and their habitats, designated critical habitat, and sensitive natural communities.

act-154.name: Wastewater Disposal Site Soil and Groundwater Analysis
act-154.text: Conduct a site-specific analysis of soil characteristics and groundwater conditions (saturated hydraulic conductivity, depth to seasonal high water table, and other suitability factors) at each proposed wastewater disposal system site.
act-154.expectedEvidence: Copy of the site-specific soil and groundwater analysis for each wastewater disposal site.

locators.excerpt: At each proposed wastewater disposal system site, a site-specific analysis of soil characteristics and groundwater conditions will be conducted to determine the soil saturated hydraulic conductivity, depth to seasonal high water table, and other factors that affect the suitability of the site for use for on-site wastewater disposal.

act-155.name: Spoils Disposal Plan
act-155.text: Develop a spoils disposal plan in coordination with CDFW for storing spoils, RTM, and dredged material, describing storage site size, location, and characteristics; site preparation and dewatering; excavation of contaminated material; and chemical characterization, drainage, and treatment.
act-155.expectedEvidence: Copy of the spoils disposal plan and record of coordination with CDFW.

locators.excerpt: Before finalizing Project engineering design, Permittee shall coordinate with CDFW to develop a spoils disposal plan for the storage of spoils, RTM, and dredged materials. The spoils disposal plan shall describe, but not be limited to, the size, locations, and required characteristics of designated storage sites; storage site preparation and dewatering; excavation of contaminated material; and chemical characterization, drainage, and treatment.

act-156.name: Transportation Demand and Management Plans
act-156.text: Develop site-specific Transportation Demand Management plans (TDMs) and Transportation Management Plans (TMPs) addressing steps before, during, and after construction to minimize construction employee VMT, in consultation with the applicable transportation entities.
act-156.expectedEvidence: Copies of the final site-specific TDMs and TMPs and records of consultation with the transportation entities.

locators.excerpt: The project will also require development of site-specific TDMs and TMPs that address the specific steps to be taken before, during, and after construction to minimize VMT as a result of construction employees driving alone in their single occupancy vehicles to and from park-and-ride lots and construction sites. Construction contractors will be responsible for developing the TDMs and TMPs in consultation with the following applicable transportation entities.

locators.excerpt: To reduce potential conflicts with existing land uses, DWR will require that staged construction plans, roadway closure reports, and detour plans be prepared for major road improvements and approved by the applicable transportation entity (i.e., Caltrans, county, or city public works department).

act-158.name: Major Road Improvement Geometric Design Plans

act-158.expectedEvidence: Geometric design plans for the major road improvements with the approving transportation entity's sign-off.

deadline.milestone: Start of Major Road Improvement Construction

locators.excerpt: To eliminate potential hazards from a geometric design, DWR will require that geometric design plans that meet geometric standards be prepared and approved by the applicable transportation entity (i.e., Caltrans, county, or city public works department) for the major road improvements included in the conceptual design of the project alternatives. i.

act-159.name: Delta Community Events Disturbance Plan

locators.excerpt: In coordination with the Ombudsman, the contractor will prepare a site or activity-specific plan to minimize and avoid construction-related disturbances, such as noise and traffic, where feasible.

act-162.name: Final Barge Operations Plan
act-162.text: Submit the final Barge Operations Plan, developed by the construction contractor per DWR contract specifications and incorporating CDFW comments, at least one year before any in-water Covered Activity and before any barge use for construction or transport, and obtain NMFS, USFWS and CDFW written approval.
act-162.expectedEvidence: Copy of the final Barge Operations Plan as submitted and the written approvals from NMFS, USFWS and CDFW.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall work collaboratively with CDFW to incorporate comments into the draft plan and submit the final Barge Operations Plan to CDFW for review and approval a minimum of one year prior to initiating any in-water Covered Activity.

DWR will require that any construction contractor proposing to use barges (to perform construction or to transport materials or equipment) develop a barge operations plan, to be approved by NMFS, USFWS, and CDFW. Each plan will be developed and submitted by the construction contractors per standard DWR contract specifications.

act-163.name: Annual Barge Monitoring Report
act-163.text: Prepare annual barge monitoring report summarizing monitoring observations for each construction year, evaluating plan performance measures, with descriptions and representative photographs or videos of riverbank and vegetation conditions.
act-163.expectedEvidence: Copy of each annual barge monitoring report and its transmittal to DWR.

locators.excerpt: Provide annual reports to DWR, summarizing monitoring observations during each construction year, including an evaluation of the plan performance measures. The annual report will also include descriptions and representative photographs and/or videos of conditions of riverbanks and vegetation.

act-164.name: Draft Barge Operations Plan
act-164.text: Develop a draft barge operations plan with CDFW minimizing barge trips and routes' impacts on Covered Fish Species, and submit it in the Pre-implementation Phase Authorization Package.
act-164.expectedEvidence: Copy of the draft barge operations plan as submitted to CDFW in the Pre-implementation Phase Authorization Package.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall coordinate with CDFW to develop a barge operations plan to minimize the number of barge trips necessary to conduct Covered Activities including over-water geotechnical explorations and rip rap installation, identify the barge routes that minimize impacts on Covered Fish Species, and minimize general barge operation-related effects on Covered Species. Permittee shall submit the draft barge operations plan to CDFW as part of the Pre-implementation Phase Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6.1).

act-165.name: Dewatering Plan
act-165.text: Develop a dewatering plan with CDFW and submit it in the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package for review and written approval.
act-165.expectedEvidence: Copy of the dewatering plan as submitted in the Construction Phase Authorization Package and CDFW written approval.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall collaborate with CDFW to develop a dewatering plan. Permittee shall submit the dewatering plan to CDFW as part of the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6.2) for review and approval prior to initiation Covered Activities.

act-166.name: Erosion Control Stabilization Measures Approval
act-166.text: Submit proposed erosion control stabilization measures to CDFW, in the Erosion and Sediment Control Plan or the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package, and obtain CDFW written approval.
act-166.expectedEvidence: Copy of the erosion control stabilization measures submitted to CDFW and CDFW's written approval.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall submit proposed erosion control stabilization measures to CDFW as part of the Erosion and Sediment Control Plan (Condition of Approval 11.26) or separately within the appropriate Construction Phased Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6.2) for review and written approval prior to initiating Covered Activities.

act-167.name: Erosion and Sediment Control Plans
act-167.text: Have contractors prepare site-specific erosion and sediment control plans for each site, accounting for proximity to surface water, erosion potential and drainage, covering short- and long-term erosion, sedimentation and restoration of damaged soils and vegetation, including all CGP erosion-control requirements and the listed BMPs incorporated into the SWPPPs, and submit them to CDFW in the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package for review and confirmation of consistency with the ITP before initiating Covered Activities.
act-167.expectedEvidence: Copy of the Construction Phase Authorization Package with the erosion and sediment control plans and CDFW's confirmation of consistency with the ITP.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall submit the erosion and sediment control plans to CDFW as part of the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6.2) for CDFW’s review and confirmation of consistency with this ITP prior to initiating Covered Activities.

Each site-specific plan shall take into account conditions such as proximity to surface water, erosion potential, drainage, etc. The erosion and sediment control plan(s) shall include best management practices such as: physical erosion control stabilization (see Condition of Approval 11.27); maintaining emergency erosion control supplies at all times during construction and replacing used emergency materials within 48 hours; minimal disturbance of the terrain and natural land features; diverting runoff away from steep, denuded slopes or other critical areas with barriers, berms, ditches, or other facilities; retaining trees and vegetation where practicable to stabilize hillsides, retain moisture, and reduce erosion; limiting ground disturbance to areas of proven stability; using sequence clearing of native vegetation and soil disturbance to minimize overall time of soil disturbance; implementing construction management and site inspections before, during, and after rain events; scheduling measures to mitigate erosion from rainfall events, runoff, or flooding at construction sites; installing runoff and drainage control features (e.g., berms and swales, slope drains); installing wind erosion control features (e.g., application of hydraulic mulch or bonded fiber matrix); and use of watertight forms and other containment structures to prevent spills or discharge of raw concrete, wash water, and other contaminants from entering surface waters and other sensitive habitats.

DWR will require all contractors prepare and implement erosion and sediment control to control short-term and long-term erosion and sedimentation effects and to plans 21 restore soils and vegetation in areas damaged by construction activities. Multiple erosion and sediment control plans will be prepared for project-related construction activities, each taking into account site-specific conditions such as proximity to surface water, erosion potential, drainage, etc. The plans will include all the necessary CGP requirements regarding erosion control and will specify BMPs for erosion and sediment control that are to be implemented during construction activities. These BMPs will be incorporated into the stormwater pollution prevention plans (SWPPPs) (see EC-4b: Develop and Implement Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plans).

act-168.name: Underground Well Detection Plan
act-168.text: Develop the Underground Well Detection Plan, covering evaluation locations, affected Covered Species habitats, methodology including site visit frequency and duration, access routes and any ground disturbance, and submit it to CDFW in the Pre-implementation Phase Authorization Package for review and confirmation of consistency.
act-168.expectedEvidence: Copy of the Underground Well Detection Plan as submitted and CDFW confirmation of consistency.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall develop an Underground Well Detection Plan that will be used for the evaluation of the suitability of geophysical techniques to detect buried and abandoned wells. Permittee shall submit the Underground Well Detection Plan to CDFW as part of the Pre-implementation Phase Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6.1) for CDFW’s review and confirmation of consistency with this ITP prior to the initiation of preconstruction Covered Activities. The Underground Well Detection Plan shall include but not be limited to the identification of the location(s) for the proposed evaluation and associated Covered Species habitat(s) potentially impacted by the evaluation, description of the methodology to be utilized for the evaluation including the frequency and duration of site visits, access roads or pathways to be utilized, and any potential ground-disturbing activity.

act-169.name: Groundwater Testing and Monitoring Plan
act-169.text: Develop and submit a Groundwater Testing and Monitoring Plan to CDFW in the Pre-implementation Phase Authorization Package, including test well, monitoring well and piezometer number and locations, instruments and installation methods, monitoring methodology and habitat impacts, and affected Covered Species habitats with site-specific minimization actions, for review and confirmation of consistency.
act-169.expectedEvidence: Copy of the Groundwater Testing and Monitoring Plan as submitted and CDFW confirmation of consistency.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall develop a Groundwater Testing and Monitoring Plan to be submitted to CDFW as part of the Pre-implementation Phase Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6.1) for CDFW’s review and confirmation of consistency with this ITP, prior to the initiation of Covered Activities within the Project Area including the preconstruction, construction, or monitoring Phase(s). The Groundwater Testing and Monitoring Plan shall include but not be limited to the number and location of proposed test wells, groundwater monitoring wells, and vibratory wire piezometers; identification of instruments and related installation methods; description of monitoring methodology and discussion of the associated impact to Covered Species suitable habitat (e.g., frequency of site visits, duration of testing, total area of impact per monitoring technique); and identification of Covered Species’ habitats that will be affected with identified minimization actions, referencing Conditions of Approval within this ITP, to be applied on a site specific basis.

act-170.name: Buried and Abandoned Well Disclosure
act-170.text: Disclose any buried or abandoned wells identified through the Underground Well Detection Plan in the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package.
act-170.expectedEvidence: Construction Phase Authorization Package section disclosing buried or abandoned wells identified.

locators.excerpt: Any buried or abandoned wells identified through implementation of the Underground Well Detection Plan shall be disclosed within the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6.2).

act-171.name: Annual Groundwater Monitoring Report
act-171.text: Publish annual groundwater monitoring reports summarizing monthly data with EC chemographs, current and preconstruction water level contour maps, and hydrographs.
act-171.expectedEvidence: Copy of each published annual groundwater monitoring report.

The annual report will summarize monthly data and show EC chemographs (figures showing changes in EC values with time) and the most recent water level contour map as well as the preconstruction contour map and hydrographs.

locators.excerpt: All monitoring data will be reported to the public monthly, annually, and in a  final report. The monthly reports will contain tabular water level data as well as changes in water levels from the previous months.

act-173.name: Final Groundwater Monitoring Report

act-173.expectedEvidence: Copy of the published final groundwater monitoring report with contour maps and EC chemographs.

locators.excerpt: All monitoring data will be reported to the public monthly, annually, and in a  final report. The final report will include water level contour maps (for the area of the groundwater aquifer that is affected by dewatering) and EC chemographs. The contour maps will show initial preconstruction water levels, construction phase water levels, post- construction water levels, and annual conveyance operations water levels, as applicable.

act-174.text: Submit the preconstruction (baseline) MMMP information to CDFW in the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package.
act-174.expectedEvidence: Copy of the Construction Phase Authorization Package containing the baseline MMMP information.
