act-184.name: Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plans (SWPPPs)
act-184.text: Before construction, have a Qualified SWPPP Developer prepare SWPPPs for each construction site or contract meeting SWRCB and Central Valley RWQCB requirements, including the QSD's CGP Risk Level determination and all state stormwater collection, detention, treatment, and discharge requirements, and covering erosion and sediment control, materials and waste management, water pollution control, dewatering and pipeline testing, spill prevention and response, hazardous materials management, site inspection and monitoring, non-stormwater discharge prevention, site characteristics, schedules, materials and fill sources, housekeeping BMPs, BMP schedules and personnel training.
act-184.expectedEvidence: Copies of the SWPPPs prepared by the Qualified SWPPP Developer, including the CGP Risk Level determinations.

locators.excerpt: Permittee and its contractors shall ensure compliance with all construction stormwater permitting requirements and shall prepare a stormwater pollution prevention plan (SWPPP) to control short- term and long-term effects associated with construction-generated stormwater runoff to Covered Species, prevent sediment from entering sensitive habitats, and reduce erosion, dust, and other deleterious aspects of Covered Activities. The SWPPP shall include all applicable SWRCB and Central Valley RWQCB requirements regarding construction-generated stormwater collection, detention, treatment, and discharge that will be in place throughout the duration of Covered Activities. The SWPPP shall include measures that address erosion and sediment control (Condition of Approval 11.26), management of construction materials, waste management measures, water pollution control measures, site dewatering and pipeline testing, accidental spill prevention and response, hazardous materials management plan (Condition of Approval 11.21), site inspection and monitoring, and measures to prevent non-stormwater discharges from reaching surface waters. Non-stormwater discharge examples include washing vehicles, cleaning streets, or applying erodible landscape material during rain. The SWPPP shall also describe site topographic, soil, and hydrologic characteristics; construction activities and schedules; construction materials to be used, including sources of imported fill material and other potential polluting sources; housekeeping BMPs; BMP site, implementation, and inspection schedules; and ongoing personnel training requirements.

In accordance with this environmental commitment, DWR will require the preparation and implementation of stormwater pollution prevention plans (SWPPPs) to control short-term and long-term effects associated with construction-generated stormwater runoff. The SWPPPs will include all the necessary state requirements regarding construction-generated stormwater collection, detention, treatment, and discharge that will be in place throughout the construction period. For the alternative selected, a series of separate but related SWPPPs will be prepared by a Qualified SWPPP Developer (QSD) and will be implemented under the supervision of a Qualified SWPPP Practitioner (for each construction site and/or each construction contract). As part of the procedure to gain coverage under the CGP, the QSD will determine the “Risk Level” (Levels 1, 2, or 3, or Types 1, 2, or 3 for linear underground/overhead projects) of the construction activities covered by a given SWPPP, which involves an evaluation of the site’s

act-185.name: Notice of Termination
act-185.text: File a Notice of Termination with the State Water Board
act-185.expectedEvidence: Copy of the filed Notice of Termination and the State Water Board's acknowledgement.

locators.excerpt: Once post construction BMPs are constructed and revegetation is appropriately established, a Notice of Termination will be filed with the State Water Board.

act-186.name: CDFW Approval of Biological Criteria Compliance Models
act-186.text: Obtain CDFW approval of all models used to assess compliance with the Biological Criteria, including the salmon and White Sturgeon Biological Criteria, before the models are used to assess compliance.
act-186.expectedEvidence: CDFW's written approval of each model used to assess compliance with the Biological Criteria.

locators.excerpt: All models used to assess compliance with the Biological Criteria shall be subject to CDFW approval.
All models used to assess compliance with the Biological Criteria shall be subject to CDFW approval.
All models used to assess compliance with the Biological Criteria shall be subject to CDFW approval.

act-187.name: Performance Criteria Assessment Peer Review and Approval
act-187.text: Obtain independent scientific peer review and NMFS, USFWS, and CDFW approval of assessments of achievement of performance criteria
act-187.expectedEvidence: Copy of the independent scientific peer review and the NMFS, USFWS and CDFW approval of the performance criteria assessment.

locators.excerpt: Assessments of achievement of performance criteria will receive independent scientific peer review and will be subject to approval by NMFS, USFWS, and CDFW.

act-188.name: NDDMT Charter
act-188.text: Develop the NDDMT charter with CDFW describing membership, roles, and processes; submit drafts for CDFW review and obtain CDFW approval of the final charter.
act-188.expectedEvidence: Copy of the draft NDDMT charter submitted to CDFW and CDFW's approval of the final charter.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall, in collaboration with CDFW, develop a charter for the NDDMT. Team membership, roles, and processes shall be described in the team charter. Permittee shall submit drafts of the team charter to CDFW for review no less than eight months prior to the start of Phase 1 Operations. After CDFW comments are incorporated, the final team charter shall be subject to CDFW approval.

act-189.name: Hydraulic Data Plan
act-189.text: Develop the Hydraulic Data Plan with CDFW for using real-time and upstream monitoring station data to implement operating criteria, accounting for non-Project diversions, equipment accuracy, and pump and screen constraints, and obtain CDFW approval.
act-189.expectedEvidence: Copy of the Hydraulic Data Plan and CDFW approval.

locators.excerpt: As required by Condition of Approval 10.20.1 Permittee shall work collaboratively with CDFW to develop a Hydraulic Data Plan to use the data obtained from the new real-time monitoring station, in addition to upstream monitoring stations described in Section 20.2.1 of the Project Description and existing stations, to implement operating criteria described in this Condition of Approval and Condition of Approval 11.111. The plan shall take into consideration non-Project diversions that may occur between the north Delta intakes and the location of the station used to calculate bypass flows. The plan shall also take into account accuracy of equipment used for real time measurements of Sacramento River flow and diversions, and physical constraints associated with pump operations and intake screens. This plan shall be subject to CDFW approval.

act-190.name: Real-Time Information Sharing Process
act-190.text: Develop a real-time information sharing process with CDFW covering data to determine balanced or excess conditions, track excepted upstream releases, and calculate carriage water savings, and obtain CDFW approval.
act-190.expectedEvidence: Copy of the final real-time information sharing process and CDFW's approval.

locators.excerpt: No less than three years prior to initiating Phase 1 Operations, Permittee shall collaborate with CDFW to develop a process to share information with CDFW in real time and facilitate evaluation of hydrologic and operational data required to implement this Condition of Approval and Condition of Approval 11.112. This real-time information sharing process shall include, at a minimum, all data and analyses needed to 1) determine whether the system is in balanced or excess conditions (as defined by Project Description Section 15.10), 2) track upstream reservoir releases that meet the exceptions identified in Condition of Approval 11.112, and 3) and calculate carriage water savings. The final information sharing process shall be subject to CDFW approval.

act-191.name: NDDMT Operations Risk Assessments
act-191.text: Prepare NDDMT operations risk assessments covering at least Components A through G: hydrologic, operational and meteorological information; biological information for each Covered Fish Species; salmon through-Delta survival; exposure at the north Delta intakes; routing risk; status of south Delta conditions; and the Sacramento River hydrograph.
act-191.expectedEvidence: Copy of each weekly NDDMT risk assessment covering Components A through G.

locators.excerpt: Risk assessments shall include, but not be limited to, Components A – G below, and associated data sources. A. Assessment of biological information for Covered Fish Species i. Salmon through-Delta survival • Entrainment into the central and south Delta • Available data, including acoustic telemetry, regarding releases of tagged fish to assess survival in real time • Monitoring and survey data including rotary screw traps, seines, and trawls • STARS, ECO-PTM and EPTM, or an equivalent real-time survival modeling tool D. Risk of exposure to impacts at the north Delta intakes • Assessments of Covered Fish Species biological data in section B above • All available hydrologic and operation data and forecasts • Other data and modeling tools as informed by science and monitoring required by Conditions of Approval in this ITP E. Routing risk and potential increase in exposure to south Delta operations (low, medium, high): • Flows in the Sacramento River predicted with upcoming storm events • DCC gate position • Status of operations of the Georgiana Slough Salmonid Migratory Barrier • Prediction of tidal interaction at Georgiana Slough o Inflow to Delta from Sacramento River and the interaction of the muting of tidal effects around Georgiana Slough • Precipitation in the forecast for the coming week and increasing river flow effects of routing into central and south Delta F. Status of south Delta Conditions of Approval in the 2024 ITP (ITP No. G.

act-192.name: Sediment Performance Criteria
act-192.text: Develop sediment performance criteria with input from the permitting fish agencies and independent peer review
act-192.expectedEvidence: Copy of the final sediment performance criteria and records of agency input and peer review.

locators.excerpt: The specifics of the performance criteria will be developed with the input of the permitting fish agencies and independent peer review. The performance criteria are expected to include assessments of habitat indicators such as the percentage of time that turbidity at monitoring stations exceeds an established threshold (e.g., 12 nephelometric turbidity units; Sommer and Mejia 2013).

act-193.name: Annual Sediment Entrainment Monitoring Plans and Reports
act-193.text: Prepare annual sediment entrainment monitoring plans and results reports, with initial and periodic independent peer review through the Delta Science Program, and obtain NMFS, USFWS, and CDFW approval
act-193.expectedEvidence: Copies of each annual sediment entrainment monitoring plan and results report with the NMFS, USFWS and CDFW approvals.

locators.excerpt: Annual monitoring plans and results reporting will receive initial and periodic independent peer reviews facilitated by the Delta Science Program, and will be subject to approval by NMFS, USFWS, and CDFW.

act-194.name: North Delta Diversion Optimization Study
act-194.text: Evaluate a wide range of approaches to operate the north Delta diversions jointly with the south Delta export facilities through the Optimization Study required by COA 10.21.8.
act-194.expectedEvidence: Copy of the completed Optimization Study evaluating joint north and south Delta operations, as submitted to CDFW.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall evaluate a wide range of potential approaches to operate the north Delta diversions jointly with existing south Delta export facilities as required by Condition of Approval 10.21.8 (Optimization Study to Inform Joint operations of State Water Project North and South Delta Intakes).

obl-0001.title: Color-match paints for panels and structures directly from the physical color chart, not digital or printed reproductions
obl-0001.trigger: All paints for color panels and structures

locators.excerpt: Refer to https://blmwyomingvisual.anl.gov/mitigation/federal/index.cfm for more information on this technique and other best management practices and techniques for visual screening. a) All paints used for the color panels and structures will be color matched directly from the physical color chart, rather than from any digital or color-reproduced versions of the color chart. b) Paints will be of a dull, flat, or satin finish only.

obl-0002.title: Paint new structures two to three shades darker than the surrounding area, or with a color from the BLM Standard Environmental Colors Chart CC-001 (April 2014), unless an aesthetic design treatment calls for another color

locators.excerpt: New structures that warrant painting will be painted with a shade that is two to three shades darker than the general surrounding area, unless aesthetic design treatments indicate another color selection with the intent to specifically improve aesthetics. Otherwise, colors shall be chosen from the Bureau of Land Management Standard Environmental Colors Chart CC-001: April 2014.

obl-0003.title: Select tower finishes for correct color, durability, and environmental safety

locators.excerpt: In consultation with Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PG&E), SMUD, and other power utility providers on the study area, DWR will require the design of the project’s permanent transmission poles to incorporate the following measures to be consistent with equipment and structures used by these utilities. a) Transmission poles will be power providers standard lattice towers and will be galvanized steel or other required treatment to make the structures visually consistent with other similar towers in the visual landscape. b) Finishes will be selected for their ability to achieve the correct color selection, durability, and environmental safety.

obl-0004.title: Make visible pipelines, guardrails, and non-safety signs of materials or colors that blend with surroundings, with low-sheen, nonreflective surfaces and no glossy paint
obl-0004.trigger: Visible pipelines, guardrails, and non-safety signs

locators.excerpt: DWR will require that visible pipelines, guardrails, and non-safety signs will be of a material or color that helps surfaces to blend better with the surroundings. These elements will be constructed with low- sheen and nonreflective surface materials to reduce potential for glare, and the use of glossy paints or surfaces would be avoided.

obl-0005.title: Apply aesthetic design features such as natural stone texture and integral color to highly visible concrete or shotcrete structures, consistent with technology and building codes
obl-0005.trigger: Concrete or shotcrete structures highly visible to the public
monitorSigns: plain gray concrete wall in public view

locators.excerpt: DWR will require aesthetic design features consistent with technological and building code requirements at concrete or shotcrete structures that are highly visible to the public. These features may include, but not be limited to, mimicking natural material (e.g., stone or rock surfacing) and integral color, in the same theme, to reduce visibility and to better blend with the landscape. v.

obl-0006.title: Site ancillary features such as antennas to minimize visual intrusion

locators.excerpt: In addition, the visual intrusion of ancillary features (e.g., antennas or other equipment) will be minimized through proper siting.

obl-0007.title: Use native Delta plant species as accents and screening to reduce the perceived scale and mass of built features

locators.excerpt: Vegetative accents and screening will be used to aid in a perceived reduction in the scale and mass of the built features, while accentuating the design treatments that will be applied to built features. Plant selection will be species native to the Delta and based on the plants’ abilities to screen built features and provide aesthetic accents. iii.

obl-0008.title: Use a smart watering system that adjusts to site, plant, and weather conditions to avoid overwatering

locators.excerpt: Areas that are irrigated will use a smart watering system that evaluates the existing site conditions and plant material against weather conditions to avoid overwatering of such areas.

obl-0009.title: Seed landscape berms with a native meadow erosion-control seed mix

locators.excerpt: The berms will be seeded with a native meadow erosion- control seed mix and be planted to comply with directions set forth below. a) Plantings will be native and indigenous to the area, and no invasive plant species will be used under any conditions.

obl-0010.title: Build bridges as lattice steel where site conditions can accommodate it
obl-0010.trigger: Bridge crossings where site conditions allow
monitorSigns: concrete bridge where lattice steel feasible

locators.excerpt: DWR will require evaluation of bridge crossing designs using lattice steel, consistent with other bridges in the Delta and implement where site conditions can accommodate a lattice steel structure. Such a structure would be less visually confining than concrete structures, provide better visual access to points beyond, allow light to travel through the structure, and may appear less like a visual barrier within the landscape. vi.

obl-0011.title: Minimize the height of new structures as feasible and consistent with building code

locators.excerpt: The height of new structures will be minimized as feasible and consistent with building code requirements.

obl-0012.title: Use the power provider's standard lattice towers in galvanized steel or other required treatment so they match similar towers nearby

locators.excerpt: In consultation with Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PG&E), SMUD, and other power utility providers on the study area, DWR will require the design of the project’s permanent transmission poles to incorporate the following measures to be consistent with equipment and structures used by these utilities. a) Transmission poles will be power providers standard lattice towers and will be galvanized steel or other required treatment to make the structures visually consistent with other similar towers in the visual landscape. b) Finishes will be selected for their ability to achieve the correct color selection, durability, and environmental safety.

obl-0013.title: Use only dull, flat, or satin paint finishes, of a type chosen for long-term durability

locators.excerpt: Refer to https://blmwyomingvisual.anl.gov/mitigation/federal/index.cfm for more information on this technique and other best management practices and techniques for visual screening. a) All paints used for the color panels and structures will be color matched directly from the physical color chart, rather than from any digital or color-reproduced versions of the color chart. b) Paints will be of a dull, flat, or satin finish only. Appropriate paint type will be selected for the finished structures to ensure long- term durability of the painted surfaces.

obl-0014.title: Maintain the paint color on project structures over time
monitorSigns: chipped or peeling paint on structure

locators.excerpt: c) DWR will maintain the paint color over time.

obl-0015.title: Select colors using color panels at least 3 by 2 feet viewed from key observation points within 1,000 feet under common front and back lighting, choosing for the most prevalent season

locators.excerpt: Because color selection will vary by location, DWR, working with the facility designers, will employ the use of color panels evaluated from key observation points during common lighting conditions (front versus backlighting) to aid in the appropriate color selection. DWR will select colors for the coloring of the most prevalent season. Panels will be a minimum of 3 feet by 2 feet in dimension and will be evaluated from various distances, but within 1,000 feet, to ensure the best possible color selection.

obl-0016.title: Evaluate lattice steel bridge crossing designs consistent with other Delta bridges
monitorSigns: no lattice steel evaluation on file

locators.excerpt: DWR will require evaluation of bridge crossing designs using lattice steel, consistent with other bridges in the Delta and implement where site conditions can accommodate a lattice steel structure.

obl-0017.title: Where riparian vegetation cannot be kept or reestablished, include native-plant landscaping for maximum cover and consider non-vegetative cover such as rock piles, snags, or lightweight faux features.
obl-0017.trigger: Plans for areas where riparian vegetation cannot be maintained
monitorSigns: bare area, no cover in plans

locators.excerpt: Where maintaining and reestablishing the riparian vegetation and canopy is not possible, plans will include landscaping with native plants that will provide the maximum amount of cover and heterogeneity possible and will also consider the use of other non-vegetative options to provide cover and heterogeneity to facilitate wildlife movement such as rock piles, snags, and human-made materials, such as faux rocks and trees that provide cover, yet are lightweight and not load-bearing.

obl-0018.title: Design the landscaping plan to maximize planting zones that need no irrigation, such as native grassland and wildflower meadow seeding
monitorSigns: landscape plan relies on permanent irrigation where meadow feasible

locators.excerpt: Design of the landscaping plan will maximize the use of planting zones that do not need irrigation, such as seeding with a native grassland and wildflower meadow mix, which reduces or eliminates the need for a permanent irrigation system.

obl-0019.title: Evaluate similar local well-designed water conveyance structures, including historic ones, and use them as design precedent for intakes, pumping plants, control structures, fish screens, and bridges so designs complement the landscape, to the extent feasible
monitorSigns: no design precedent evaluation on file

locators.excerpt: DWR will require evaluation of similar, local, well-designed water conveyance structures, including those with historic value and use these features as design precedent to develop designs for the intake facilities, pumping plants, control structures, fish screens, and bridges so that the resultant design will complement the natural landscape, be aesthetically pleasing, and minimize the effects of visual intrusion of project facilities on the landscape, to the extent feasible.

obl-0020.title: Make temporary visual barriers at least 6 feet high

locators.excerpt: The visual barrier will be a minimum of 6 feet high to help maintain the privacy of residents and block long-term ground-level views toward construction activities.

obl-0021.title: Do not install visual barriers within 300 feet of CTS or GGS upland habitat.
monitorSigns: barrier within 300 feet of upland habitat

locators.excerpt: The visual barriers shall not be installed within 300 feet of CTS and GGS upland habitats.

obl-0022.title: Install temporary visual barriers (slatted chain link, windscreen fencing, silt fence, wood or concrete barrier, or similar) to block views of disruptive work areas from residents and recreation areas within 0.25 mile in urban areas or 0.50 mile in rural areas, to the extent feasible
obl-0022.trigger: Construction work areas with direct line of sight from sensitive receptors within those distances
monitorSigns: work area visible from homes with no screen

locators.excerpt: DWR will require installation of temporary visual barriers at the construction work areas with direct line-of-sight from sensitive receptors (i.e., residents and recreational areas). Barriers will be placed to obscure views of work areas where construction activity and equipment would be disruptive and lower the existing visual quality. These efforts will include the following actions and performance standards to be applied to the extent feasible and practicable. The visual barriers will be placed to protect residents and recreational areas that are within 0.25 mile of a project construction site in an urban area and 0.50 mile of a project construction site in a rural area. The visual barrier may include chain link fencing with privacy slats, fencing with windscreen material, silt fence, wood or concrete barrier, or other similar barrier.

obl-0023.title: Build the barrier at least 5 feet high with a continuous surface that light cannot pass through (fence with privacy slats, or concrete barrier with a screen).
obl-0023.trigger: All visual barriers along haul routes

locators.excerpt: The visual barrier will be a minimum of 5 feet high and will provide a continuous surface impenetrable by light. This height may be obtained by installing a temporary structure, such as fencing (e.g., chain link with privacy slats) or a semi-permanent structure, such as a concrete barrier (e.g., a roadway median barrier or architectural concrete wall system) retrofitted with an approved visual screen, if necessary, to meet the required height. ii.

obl-0024.title: Screen substations within 0.25 mile of urban residences or 0.50 mile of rural residences with native Delta plantings
obl-0024.trigger: Substations within those distances of residences
monitorSigns: substation visible from homes, no screening

locators.excerpt: Vegetative accents and screening will be used to aid in screening substations located within 0.25 mile of residences in an urban area or within 0.50 mile of residences in a rural area. Plant selection will be species native to the Delta and based on the plants’ abilities to screen features and provide aesthetic accents. iv.

obl-0025.title: Do not install visual barriers until the biologist has assessed the access road locations.

locators.excerpt: The Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall assess the locations of the identified access roads prior to the installation of any visual barriers.

obl-0026.title: Build landscape berms with tree and shrub plantings in natural, irregular forms, not levee-like, to screen built features

locators.excerpt: Landscape berms, combined with tree and shrub plantings, will be used to help screen built features from existing viewpoints by allowing for additional height. The landscape berms will be constructed to have a more natural form, as opposed to one that is highly regular and levee-like.

obl-0027.title: Plant a species mix of trees, shrubs, and herbaceous understory of varied heights, both evergreen and deciduous

locators.excerpt: If indigenous plantings are not available, DWR will coordinate with the California Department of Fish and Wildlife to use a mutually acceptable plant mix palette. b) The species list will include trees, shrubs, and an herbaceous understory of varying heights, as well as both evergreen and deciduous types. Plant variety will increase the effectiveness of revegetated areas by providing multiple layers, seasonality, diverse habitat, and reduced susceptibility to disease. vi.

obl-0028.title: Use barrier material or color suited to the location and traffic safety, and no glossy materials.
obl-0028.trigger: All visual barriers along haul routes

locators.excerpt: The visual barriers will be of a material or have a color treatment appropriate for the location and traffic safety requirements. The use of glossy materials will be avoided.

obl-0029.title: Install a visual barrier along the identified portions of access routes to block truck headlight spill toward residents.
obl-0029.trigger: Identified access route segments used for nighttime construction trucking

locators.excerpt: DWR will install a visual barrier along portions of access routes where screening would prevent excessive light spill toward residents from truck headlights being used during nighttime construction activities.

obl-0030.title: Screen and shade park-and-ride lots with native Delta plantings
monitorSigns: park-and-ride lot without shade or screening plants

locators.excerpt: Vegetative accents and screening will be used to aid in screening and shading park-and-ride lots. Plant selection will be species native to the Delta and based on the plants’ abilities to screen features and provide aesthetic accents. v.

obl-0031.title: If you install visual barriers along access routes, retrofit them with a CDFW-approved visual screen that blocks light spill.
obl-0031.trigger: Any visual barrier installed along access routes

locators.excerpt: Permittee may install a temporary (e.g., chain link with privacy slats) or semi-permanent (e.g., a roadway median barrier or architectural concrete wall system) barrier retrofitted using a CDFW- approved visual screen along portions of access routes where screening would prevent excessive light spill that could provide a continuous surface impenetrable by light.

obl-0032.title: Assess the locations of identified access roads before any visual barrier is installed.
obl-0032.trigger: Before installing visual barriers along access roads
monitorSigns: barrier installed with no biologist assessment

locators.excerpt: The Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall assess the locations of the identified access roads prior to the installation of any visual barriers.

obl-0033.title: Do not start Covered Activities covered by the package until the HMMPs have been submitted to CDFW and confirmed consistent.
obl-0033.trigger: Before initiating Covered Activities in the phase
monitorSigns: no CDFW confirmation on file at start

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall submit the HMMPs to CDFW as part of the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6.2) for CDFW’s review and confirmation of consistency with this ITP prior to initiating Covered Activities.

obl-0034.title: Do not start any Covered Activity, including preconstruction field investigations or species surveys, until the protocols are approved in writing by CDFW.

locators.excerpt: Protocols shall be finalized and approved in writing by CDFW prior to initiation of any Covered Activity including but not limited to preconstruction field investigation activities or preconstruction species site surveys necessary for Construction Phase Authorization.

obl-0035.title: When nighttime work is proposed, detail in the Construction Phase Authorization Package the activity type, its impact on Covered Species at that site, the measures to reduce impacts, and the justification for working at night.
obl-0035.trigger: Each Construction Phase Authorization Package proposing nighttime work

locators.excerpt: In the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package, Permittee shall detail the type of Covered Activity proposed for nighttime work, assess the impact of the Covered Activity specific to Covered Species within the Project construction site where the nighttime work is being proposed, identify measures that will be implemented to reduce impacts to Covered Species, and provide a justification for the need of nighttime work.

obl-0036.title: Record every Covered Species sighting with GPS, including datum and horizontal accuracy in feet.

locators.excerpt: Covered Species sightings shall be recorded with a GPS (including datum and horizontal accuracy in feet) and the Designated Biologist(s), Fisheries Biologist(S), or Biological Monitor(s) shall report Covered Species observed locations to CDFW within one business day of the observation.

obl-0037.title: Report new kit fox sightings to the CNDDB and send USFWS a copy of the form and a topographic map marking the location.
obl-0037.trigger: After each new kit fox sighting

locators.excerpt: New sightings of kit fox will be reported to the CNDDB. A copy of the reporting form and a topographic map clearly marked with the location of where the kit fox was observed will also be provided to USFWS at the address below.

obl-0038.title: Report any special-status species sightings and any incidental take to CDFW and USFWS by email within 1 working day of discovery
obl-0038.trigger: Within 1 working day of a sighting or take
monitorSigns: take logged, no email to CDFW and USFWS within 1 working day

locators.excerpt: Any sightings and any incidental take will be reported to CDFW and USFWS via email within 1 working day of the discovery.

obl-0039.title: Report all giant garter snake occurrence data from preconstruction surveys to the CNDDB and USFWS.
obl-0039.trigger: Sites where GGS preconstruction surveys are performed

locators.excerpt: For sites where such preconstruction surveys are performed, the surveys will conform to established protocols for giant garter snake surveys and all occurrence data gathered will be reported to the CNDDB and USFWS to add to the understanding of populations and occurrences for the species in the Delta.

obl-0040.title: Submit a completed CNDDB field survey form (or equivalent) to CDFW for each special-status species encountered, within 90 days after the last field visit
obl-0040.trigger: Within 90 days after the last field visit to the site
monitorSigns: species encountered, no CNDDB form within 90 days

locators.excerpt: For each special- status species encountered, the biologist will submit a completed CNDDB field survey form (or equivalent) to CDFW no more than 90 days after completing the last field visit to the project site.

obl-0041.title: Report Covered Species observation locations to CDFW within one business day.
obl-0041.trigger: Within one business day of each observation
monitorSigns: sighting logged, no CDFW report within 1 business day

locators.excerpt: Covered Species sightings shall be recorded with a GPS (including datum and horizontal accuracy in feet) and the Designated Biologist(s), Fisheries Biologist(S), or Biological Monitor(s) shall report Covered Species observed locations to CDFW within one business day of the observation.

obl-0042.title: Include the written MALI incident report in the appropriate monthly compliance report.
obl-0042.trigger: The monthly compliance report covering the transplant
monitorSigns: incident report missing from monthly report

locators.excerpt: The written incident report shall also be included in the appropriate monthly compliance report (see Condition of Approval 10.12).

obl-0043.title: Include each CTS incident report in the Monthly Compliance Report.
obl-0043.trigger: Monthly Compliance Report following a CTS incident
monitorSigns: CTS incident report missing from Monthly Compliance Report

locators.excerpt: The report shall also be included in the Monthly Compliance Report (see Condition of Approval 10.12).

obl-0044.title: Include each written SWHA incident report in the Monthly Compliance Report.
obl-0044.trigger: Monthly Compliance Report following a SWHA incident
monitorSigns: SWHA incident report missing from Monthly Compliance Report

locators.excerpt: The written incident report shall also be included in the Monthly Compliance Report (see Condition of Approval 10.12).

obl-0045.title: Include each written CTS relocation incident report in the Monthly Compliance Report.
obl-0045.trigger: Monthly Compliance Report following a CTS relocation
monitorSigns: relocation incident report missing from Monthly Compliance Report

locators.excerpt: The written incident report shall also be included in the Monthly Compliance Report (see Condition of Approval 10.12).

obl-0046.title: Provide monitoring records to USFWS, CDFW, and NMFS immediately on request, and per permit reporting requirements if requested
monitorSigns: agency records request not answered immediately

locators.excerpt: The biologist(s) will maintain complete records in their possession while conducting monitoring activities and will immediately provide records to USFWS, CDFW, and NMFS upon request. If requested, all monitoring records will be provided to agencies according to the reporting requirements of the relevant permits.

obl-0047.title: Keep an appointed DWR representative as the primary contact for any employee or contractor who may inadvertently take a special-status species.

locators.excerpt: DWR will appoint a representative to be the primary point of contact for any employee or contractor who might inadvertently take a special-status species, or a representative 19 will be identified during the employee education program and the representative’s name and telephone number provided to the fish and wildlife agencies.

obl-0048.title: Send CDFW a written incident report within two business days of the initial notification, covering date and time, disposition, collection location, photographs, cause of take or injury, and other pertinent information.
obl-0048.trigger: Within two business days after the initial notification
monitorSigns: no written report after 2 business days

locators.excerpt: Following initial notification, Permittee shall send CDFW a written incident report within two business days to the CDFW offices listed in the Notices section of this ITP. The report shall include the date and time of the finding or incident, disposition of the CBB, collection location, any photographs, explanation as to cause of take, injury, and any other pertinent information.

obl-0049.title: Record the circumstances of each GGS injury, the procedure followed, and the animal's final disposition in the written incident report.
obl-0049.trigger: Every written incident report for an injured GGS

locators.excerpt: The circumstances of the injury, the procedure followed, and the final disposition of the injured animal shall be documented in the written incident report as described in Condition of Approval 11.68.4).

obl-0050.title: Include the written CBB incident report in the appropriate Monthly Compliance Report.
obl-0050.trigger: The Monthly Compliance Report covering the incident
monitorSigns: incident report missing from monthly report

locators.excerpt: The written incident report shall also be included in the appropriate Monthly Compliance Report (see Condition of Approval 10.12).

obl-0051.title: Follow the injury notice with a written incident report to CDFW as described in Condition 10.16.
obl-0051.trigger: After notifying CDFW of a Covered Species injury

obl-0249.title: Set non-disturbance buffers around active nests found in the survey area, sized by species, status, activity type and duration, line of sight, sensitivity and ambient disturbance (typically 300 to 650 feet for raptors, 50 to 250 feet for other birds).

locators.excerpt: If active nests are found in the survey area, non- disturbance buffers will be established around the nest sites to avoid disturbance or destruction of the nest site until the end of the breeding season (September 1) or until a qualified wildlife biologist determines that the young have fledged and moved out of the work area (this date varies by species). Buffer distances vary by species and conservation status (e.g., listed species and fully protected species may warrant larger buffers than non–special-status species) but typically, these buffer distances are between 300 feet and 650 feet for raptors and between 50 feet and 250 feet for other nesting birds. The extent of the buffers will be determined by the qualified wildlife biologist(s) and will be established by taking into consideration the type and extent of the proposed activity occurring near the nest, the duration and timing of the activity, the line of sight between the nest and the disturbance, the sensitivity and the habituation of the birds and raptors to existing conditions, and the dissimilarity of the proposed activity to ambient levels of noise and other disturbances.

obl-0305.title: Have a qualified archaeologist review all field investigation areas for potential cultural resource impacts.

locators.excerpt: All areas associated with field investigations will be reviewed by a qualified archaeologist to evaluate the potential for impacts, if any, on cultural resources.

obl-0306.title: Evaluate the find and determine an appropriate plan of action before work resumes.

locators.excerpt: Should any unexpected cultural resources be exposed during field investigations, all work will immediately stop in the immediate vicinity (e.g., within 100 feet [30 meters]) of the find until it can be evaluated by a qualified archaeologist and an appropriate plan of action can be determined.

obl-0307.title: Implement feasible avoidance of archaeological resources first in every procedure.

locators.excerpt: The first step in each procedure will be to implement feasible avoidance of archaeological resources.

obl-0308.title: While preparing the ARMP, consult the affiliated Tribes on identification, treatment, post-review discovery, and monitoring procedures, incorporate their input to the greatest extent practicable, and give them the draft ARMP to review and comment on.

draft ARMP not sent to Tribes

locators.excerpt:
DWR will coordinate with the Native American Tribes that participated in consultation on the project to ascertain whether they have standard procedures that may be applicable or other input on the content of the ARMP.

The Tribes will be afforded an opportunity to review and comment on the draft ARMP.

In accordance with (1)(a) of Mitigation Measure CUL-3a, DWR will consult with affiliated Tribes regarding the methods for identification, treatment, post-review discovery, and monitoring during the preparation of the ARMP and incorporate Tribal input into the ARMP to the greatest extent practicable. obl-0310.title: Treat every potentially affected archaeological resource by best practices, choosing from avoidance, minimization, or mitigation.

locators.excerpt: The Archaeological Treatment Procedure will ensure that all archaeological resources potentially affected by the project will be treated according to best practices and professional standards, and that treatment options will include a range of interventions from avoidance and minimization of impacts to mitigation for the loss of the physical resource.

obl-0311.title: Do not demolish or disturb ground where it could affect a built-environment resource until its BETP has been reviewed.

obl-0312.title: Where required, protect historic buildings from construction vehicles, debris, and dust with fencing or debris meshing.

locators.excerpt: Temporary mothballing and fire and intrusion protection based on the National Park Service’s Technical Preservation Brief 31 on mothballing historic buildings (1993) may be needed if the buildings are unoccupied during construction.

obl-0314.title: Survey previously inaccessible impact areas consistently with the 2021 survey, covering direct disturbance, vibration, and setting impacts, using pedestrian survey, photographs, historical research, and interviews.

The scope of the inventory will include the entire area where impacts may occur that were inaccessible or partially inaccessible in the first survey efforts. Such impacts consist of direct disturbance, damage through vibration, or changes to the setting. b. Inventory methods and evaluation will include pedestrian surveys, photographic documentation, historical research using both primary and secondary sources, and interviews and oral histories. d.

obl-0315.title: Field survey all identified resources to determine whether they retain integrity as historical resources.

locators.excerpt: For all identified resources, DWR will review the previous documentation and complete a field survey to determine if the resources retain sufficient integrity as historical resources (CEQA Guidelines § 15064.5(a)).

obl-0316.title: The work must be led or supervised by architectural historians meeting 36 CFR Part 61 standards.

locators.excerpt: Protective treatments against construction vibration may be recommended and would be field checked as needed during construction by a qualified architectural historian with demonstrated experience in conducting monitoring of this nature.

obl-0318.title: Before construction, secure access to all property needed to finish the inventory and make sure all impact areas are surveyed.

locators.excerpt: Before construction, DWR will have access to all property needed to finalize the inventory and evaluation, and DWR will ensure that all areas of impacts will be surveyed.

locators.excerpt: The BETP will be prepared by an architectural historian who meets the Secretary of the Interior’s Standards with demonstrated experience preparing treatment for similar kinds of resources and reviewed by relevant parties prior to any demolition or ground-disturbing activity with potential to affect a built-environment resource.

obl-0320.title: Implement mitigation as specified in each BETP.

locators.excerpt: Property-specific impacts are identified in Appendix 19C, Tables 19C-1 through 19C-4, and mitigation consistent with (c) and (d) below will be implemented in accordance with the specifics developed in the BETP.

obl-0321.title: If a Landscape Treatment Plan is included in a BETP, follow National Park Service (1998) guidance and Secretary of the Interior Standards.

locators.excerpt: For those identified in the assessment as being in poor condition, a Historic Structure Report will be prepared. obl-0327.title: Consult relevant parties, such as SHPO, ACHP, local historical societies, and preservation groups, while preparing each BETP.

Compliance with state law for discoveries occurring on private or state lands requires notification of the county coroner so the coroner may determine if an investigation regarding the cause of death is required.

obl-0334.title: Put the PRC 5097.98(e) protections in place, such as conservation easements and recording the location with the county and CHRIS Information Center.

Techniques may include: a. Providing funding to develop conservation projects that allow Tribes to reintroduce ancestral languages. b. Facilitating access agreements, as appropriate, for restored areas. c. Restoring traditional use areas and restoration of plants and animals affected by the project (see Mitigation Measure TCR-1d for additional information on Tribal involvement of planned restoration activities for mitigation for project impacts). d. Promoting access to areas where Tribes can continue to conduct their ceremonial practices. e. Providing funding for the development of indigenous science by establishing education programs and scholarships; and support of academic programming development in selected academic institutions. f. Supporting co-management partnerships for access to state lands currently not publicly accessible.

locators.excerpt: Artificial burrows will be installed following the methods in Barclay (2008:53–55) and Johnson et al. (2010:4–32), or more current methodology if it becomes available, upon CDFW approval.

obl-0383.title: Do not work inside burrowing owl buffers or no-activity zones.

locators.excerpt: If an active burrow is identified within 500 feet of a work area and work cannot be conducted outside of the nesting season (February 1 through August 31), a qualified biologist will establish a non-disturbance buffer that extends a minimum of 328 feet (200 meters) around the burrow. If burrowing owls are present at the site during the nonbreeding season (September 1 through January 31), a qualified biologist will establish a no- activity zone that extends a minimum of 656 feet (100 meters) around the burrow.

obl-0384.title: Do not break ground or stage until both preconstruction burrowing owl surveys are done.

locators.excerpt: In addition to initial breeding and wintering season surveys, DWR will also require that preconstructions survey be conducted, with one occurring 14 days prior to groundbreaking and/or staging activities and another within 24 hours of these activities.

obl-0385.title: Use signs, stakes and flags that are clearly different from work area markings.

obl-0386.title: Hand excavate burrows to the end of each branch or until the diameter is under 0.5 inch.

obl-0387.title: Only a qualified biologist may set burrowing owl buffers and recommend reduced buffers.

locators.excerpt: If an active burrow is identified within 500 feet of a work area and work cannot be conducted outside of the nesting season (February 1 through August 31), a qualified biologist will establish a non-disturbance buffer that extends a minimum of 328 feet (200 meters) around the burrow. If the appropriate non-disturbance buffer for breeding or nonbreeding burrowing owls cannot be established, a qualified biologist will evaluate site-specific conditions and, in consultation with CDFW, recommend a smaller buffer that still minimizes the potential to disturb the owls (and still allows reproductive success during the breeding season).

obl-0388.title: A biological monitor must be present during all construction inside any reduced burrowing owl buffer.

locators.excerpt: The one-way doors will be left in place for a minimum of 48 hours and be monitored twice daily to ensure that the owls have left the burrow.

locators.excerpt: The extent of non-disturbance buffers will be determined based on Staff Report on time of year and level of disturbance described in the Burrowing Owl Mitigation (California Department of Fish and Game 2012:9) b.

The Designated Biologist(s) shall remove the object immediately after Covered Activities are completed in that work site when the Designated Biologist(s) has determined that potential resumed use of the burrow will not result in harm to the Covered Species.

obl-0396.title: Remove a non-disturbance buffer only after monitoring shows the nest was abandoned or the burrow is no longer in use.

obl-0397.title: Begin breeding and wintering surveys in the year before construction, following the 2012 CDFG Staff Report methods or a CDFW-approved modified method.

locators.excerpt: Surveys will be initiated during the year that precedes construction and will be consistent with the methods described in the Staff Report on Burrowing Owl Mitigation (California Department of Fish and Game 2012), or a modified methodology with written approval from CDFW. b.

locators.excerpt: The Designated Biologist(s) shall monitor to determine vacancy, then block unoccupied burrows (e.g., less than three feet long with dead ends) by installing an object approved in advance, in writing by CDFW, to prevent GGS from entering and using the burrow during Covered Activities.

obl-0399.title: Once owls have left, excavate the burrow by hand.

locators.excerpt: Once the biologist concludes the owls have left the burrow, the burrow will be excavated using hand tools, and a section of flexible plastic pipe (at least 3 inches in diameter) will be inserted into the burrow tunnel during excavation to maintain an escape route for any animals that may be inside the burrow.

obl-0400.title: Before relocating owls, survey all potential burrows in suitable nesting habitat within the project footprint and 75 feet around it for owl use, and excavate those with no owls.
monitorSigns: burrow in 75 ft buffer not surveyed

locators.excerpt: Prior to relocating owls, all potential burrowing owl burrows in suitable nesting habitat within the project footprint and 75 feet (23 meters) around the footprint, will be surveyed for owl use, and excavated if no owls are found.

obl-0401.title: Flag burrows for a 50-foot no-activity buffer, or flag work sites, staging areas and access routes that avoid potentially occupied burrows.

obl-0402.title: If the standard buffer cannot be set, evaluate site conditions (activity type, duration, timing, owl habituation, contrast with background) and recommend a smaller buffer in consultation with CDFW.
obl-0402.trigger: When the standard buffer cannot be established
monitorSigns: reduced buffer with no CDFW consultation

locators.excerpt: If the appropriate non-disturbance buffer for breeding or nonbreeding burrowing owls cannot be established, a qualified biologist will evaluate site-specific conditions and, in consultation with CDFW, recommend a smaller buffer that still minimizes the potential to disturb the owls (and still allows reproductive success during the breeding season). The site- specific buffer will be established by taking into consideration the type and extent of the proposed activity occurring near the occupied burrow, the duration and timing of the activity, the sensitivity and habituation of the owls to existing conditions, and the dissimilarity of the proposed activity to background activities.

obl-0403.title: Excavate formerly occupied burrows by hand where feasible and refill them to prevent reoccupation.
obl-0403.trigger: After owls have left the burrows

locators.excerpt: The formerly occupied burrows will then be excavated. Whenever feasible, based on the location and substrate of burrows, as determined by the qualified biologist, burrows will be excavated using hand tools and refilled to prevent reoccupation.

obl-0407.title: Conduct a preconstruction survey 14 days before groundbreaking or staging to confirm whether owls are still present or newly present.

These surveys will confirm whether owls identified during the initial breeding and wintering season surveys are still present or whether the previously unoccupied site has since become occupied by burrowing owls.

Examples where construction initiation during the nonbreeding season would not be feasible include inclement weather or conflicts with work windows for other terrestrial or aquatic species.

obl-0420.title: Remove rail habitat vegetation carefully with hand tools or equipment approved by the CDFW-approved biologist.

obl-0423.title: Place listening stations along roads, trails, and levees so wetland vegetation is not trampled.

obl-0424.title: Stop broadcasting immediately once a black rail responds.

monitorSigns: no biologist determination on noise walls

obl-0431.trigger: Each black rail survey and detection
monitorSigns: call record missing time or distance

The California black rail call type, location, distance from listening station, and time will be recorded.

obl-0432.title: Only CDFW-approved biologists with black rail survey experience and the qualifications in the CDFW-approved methodology may evaluate habitat and conduct black rail surveys.
obl-0432.trigger: All black rail habitat evaluations and surveys

locators.excerpt: Potentially suitable habitat includes tidal and nontidal seasonal or perennial wetlands at least 2 acres in size with any kind of vegetation types consistent with California black rail use in the Delta (as determined by field evaluations conducted by a CDFW-approved biologist with experience surveying for black rail) over 10 inches high, whether or not the patch in question was mapped as modeled habitat. 1991), or other CDFW-approved survey methodologies that may be developed using new information and best-available science and will be conducted by biologists with the qualifications stipulated in the CDFW-approved methodologies.

obl-0433.title: At each station listen 1 minute, broadcast 1 minute of grr calls and 0.5 minute of ki-ki-doo calls, then listen 3.5 minutes, for 6 minutes total.

The CDFW-approved biologist will then listen for another 3.5 minutes for a total of 6 minutes per station.
