obl-0442.trigger: Occupied least tern nesting habitat during breeding season

locators.excerpt: Activities performed during the California least tern breeding season, in occupied least tern nesting habitat, with USFWS and CDFW approval and under the supervision of a USFWS- and CDFW-approved biologist will be limited to inspection, research, or monitoring.

obl-0443.title: Conduct at least three preconstruction California least tern surveys in all suitable habitat within 500 feet of the construction footprint during the breeding season (April 15 to August 15).
obl-0443.trigger: When suitable nesting habitat was identified in planning-level surveys the year before construction

locators.excerpt: If suitable nesting habitat for California least tern (flat, unvegetated areas near aquatic foraging habitat) is identified during planning-level surveys the year prior to construction, DWR will require that at least three preconstruction estimated by using data on crane use days/acre by habitat type on Staten Island from habitat loss and within the 50 dBA L (1 hour) pile-driving and general construction eq regarding crop habitat needed to be maintained on Staten Island to maintain this surveys for this species will be conducted in all suitable habitat within 500 feet of the construction footprint during the California least tern breeding season (April 15 to August 15).

obl-0444.title: Coordinate with USFWS and CDFW before reducing a least tern nest buffer.
monitorSigns: buffer reduced, no agency coordination logged

locators.excerpt: Reduced buffers may be allowed, through coordination with USFWS and CDFW, if a full-time USFWS- and CDFW- approved biologist is present to monitor the nest and has authority to halt construction if bird behavior indicates continued activities could lead to nest failure.

obl-0445.title: Do not start initial ground disturbance between September 1 and April 30.
obl-0445.trigger: Suitable California red-legged frog habitat, to the extent practicable

locators.excerpt: To the extent practicable, initial ground-disturbing activities will not be conducted between September 1 and April 30, to avoid the wet season which encompasses breeding as well as potential upland migration before and after.

obl-0446.title: Install amphibian exclusion fencing along the construction site perimeter, using material that keeps frogs out, no more than 14 days before construction starts.
obl-0446.trigger: Construction sites with California red-legged frog habitat within 300 feet, installed no more than 14 days before construction starts
monitorSigns: fence installed more than 14 days early

locators.excerpt: When there is California red-legged frog habitat within 300 feet of construction activities, exclusion fencing will be installed along the perimeter of construction sites to protect California red-legged frog habitat and minimize the potential for frogs to enter the construction work area. The perimeter of construction sites will be fenced with fencing material suitable for excluding amphibians by no more than 14 days prior to the start of construction.

obl-0447.title: Work during September 1 to April 30 only in areas already surveyed, initially disturbed, and fenced.
obl-0447.trigger: After initial ground disturbance in CRLF habitat

locators.excerpt: Once the area has been surveyed, initial ground disturbance has occurred, and exclusionary fencing is in place, the seasonal restriction would not apply.

obl-0448.title: Stop all work within at least 10 feet of a California red-legged frog immediately and notify the construction manager and USFWS-approved biologist.
obl-0448.trigger: When a California red-legged frog is found in a construction or restoration area

locators.excerpt: If a California red-legged frog is encountered at any point within a construction or restoration area, activities within a minimum of 10 feet of the individual will cease immediately, the construction manager and USFWS-approved biologist will be notified, and the USFWS-approved biologist will observe and follow within 10 feet of the individual to ensure it has safely left the area.

obl-0449.title: Do not begin ground disturbance, vegetation clearing or fence installation in red-legged frog habitat until the preconstruction survey is done.

locators.excerpt: Preconstruction surveys will be conducted by a USFWS-approved biologist immediately prior to the initiation of any ground-disturbing activities or vegetation clearing, including immediately prior to exclusion fence installation, in areas identified as having suitable California red-legged frog habitat.

obl-0450.title: Only the USFWS-approved biologists named in the approved relocation plan may relocate California red-legged frogs.
monitorSigns: frog moved by biologist not named in plan

locators.excerpt: The relocation plan will contain the name(s) of the USFWS-approved biologist(s) to relocate California red-legged frogs, the method of relocation (if different than described), a map, and a description of the proposed release site(s) outside of exclusion fencing and within 300 feet of the work area or at a distance otherwise agreed to by USFWS, and written permission from the landowner to use their land as a relocation site

obl-0451.title: Only a USFWS-approved biologist may delineate California red-legged frog habitat.

locators.excerpt: When each site is available for surveys, biologist approved by USFWS, will then delineate California red-legged frog habitat at each project site, based on an agreed-upon definition of suitable habitat, including both aquatic and upland habitat.

obl-0452.title: Only a USFWS-approved biologist may conduct the red-legged frog surveys.

locators.excerpt: Preconstruction surveys will be conducted by a USFWS-approved biologist immediately prior to the initiation of any ground-disturbing activities or vegetation clearing, including immediately prior to exclusion fence installation, in areas identified as having suitable California red-legged frog habitat.

obl-0453.title: Observe and follow the frog within 10 feet until it has safely left the area.
obl-0453.trigger: When a California red-legged frog is encountered

locators.excerpt: If a California red-legged frog is encountered at any point within a construction or restoration area, activities within a minimum of 10 feet of the individual will cease immediately, the construction manager and USFWS-approved biologist will be notified, and the USFWS-approved biologist will observe and follow within 10 feet of the individual to ensure it has safely left the area.

obl-0454.title: Delineate California red-legged frog aquatic and upland habitat at each project site using the agreed-upon definition of suitable habitat.
obl-0454.trigger: At each project site, once the site is available for surveys

locators.excerpt: When each site is available for surveys, biologist approved by USFWS, will then delineate California red-legged frog habitat at each project site, based on an agreed-upon definition of suitable habitat, including both aquatic and upland habitat.

obl-0455.title: Conduct preconstruction surveys walking the work site limits and investigating all areas the frog could use for feeding, breeding, sheltering or movement.
obl-0455.trigger: Immediately before ground disturbance, vegetation clearing, or exclusion fence installation in suitable California red-legged frog habitat

locators.excerpt: Preconstruction surveys will be conducted by a USFWS-approved biologist immediately prior to the initiation of any ground-disturbing activities or vegetation clearing, including immediately prior to exclusion fence installation, in areas identified as having suitable California red-legged frog habitat. These surveys will consist of walking the work site limits. The USFWS-approved biologist will investigate all potential areas that could be used by the California red-legged frog for feeding, breeding, sheltering, movement, or other essential behaviors.

obl-0456.title: Survey within 24 hours before exclusion fencing goes in, with 100% visual coverage of the construction site and three-foot buffer.
obl-0456.trigger: Within 24 hours before exclusion fencing installation
monitorSigns: fence installed with survey older than 24 hours

locators.excerpt: Additional GGS surveys shall occur within 24 hours (one calendar day) preceding exclusion fencing installation (see Condition of Approval 11.62) and shall provide 100% visual coverage of the Project construction site and three-foot buffer.

obl-0457.title: Prioritize California red-legged frog land acquisition for lands that connect with existing protected grassland, vernal pool, and alkali seasonal wetland landscapes, including the East San Francisco Bay core recovery area.
monitorSigns: acquired parcel not connected to protected landscapes

locators.excerpt: Land acquisition for California red-legged frog habitat management lands will be prioritized based on the following characteristics. Lands that connect with existing protected grassland, vernal pool complex,  and alkali seasonal wetland complex landscapes, including those in the East San Francisco Bay core recovery area for California red-legged frog.

obl-0458.title: Protect suitable California red-legged frog aquatic and upland habitat to mitigate its loss, prioritizing aquatic breeding and upland habitat in the East San Francisco Bay core recovery area.
obl-0458.trigger: All loss of CRLF aquatic and upland habitat
monitorSigns: protected site outside recovery area, no rationale

locators.excerpt: To mitigate for the loss of California red-legged frog aquatic and upland habitat, DWR will protect suitable habitat. California red-legged frog aquatic breeding and upland habitat will be prioritized for protection within the East San Francisco Bay Recovery Plan for the California Red-Legged core recovery area as described in the Frog (Rana aurora draytonii) (U.S.

obl-0459.title: Notify USFWS of any injured or dead California red-legged frog in the project area, including whether its condition resulted from project activities.
obl-0459.trigger: Within 24 hours of finding an injured or dead CRLF in the project area
monitorSigns: dead frog logged, no USFWS notice within 24 hours
notice missing cause of injury or death

locators.excerpt: Notification to USFWS of an injured or dead California red-legged frog in the project area will be reported within 24 hours and will include details such as whether or not its condition resulted from activities related to the proposed project.

obl-0460.title: Protect and manage in perpetuity all lands protected and restored to compensate for California red-legged frog habitat effects.

locators.excerpt: All lands protected and restored for compensation of effects on California red-legged frog habitat will be protected and managed in perpetuity.

obl-0461.title: Use only rodent control methods consistent with the California tiger salamander 4(d) rule.
monitorSigns: rodent control method not allowed under 4(d) rule

locators.excerpt: In addition, the method of rodent control will comply with those discussed in the 4(d) rule published in the final listing rule for California tiger salamander (69 Federal Register [FR] 47211–47248).

obl-0462.title: Seal overlapping fence sections so CTS cannot be trapped.

locators.excerpt: Fencing that is overlapped to connect different sections of material shall be sealed in a manner that does not allow CTS to become entrapped.

obl-0463.title: Install one-way exit funnels flush to the ground every 150 feet.

locators.excerpt: The fence shall include multiple one-way exit funnels flush to the ground every 150 feet to allow CTS and other species to leave the Project construction site.

obl-0464.title: Build the exclusion barrier with taut fencing on stakes at least 24 inches above ground, buried 6 to 12 inches, with a top climber lip.

locators.excerpt: The barrier shall consist of taut wildlife exclusion fencing supported by stakes at least 24 inches tall above the soil surface and buried to a depth of 6-12 inches below the soil surface; and shall be constructed with a top climber barrier lip so that CTS cannot scale and go over the barrier into the Project construction site.

obl-0465.title: During the CTS active season or within 300 feet of suitable CTS aquatic habitat, stop all work not inside an exclusion barrier, including access road use and SCADA, transmission line and facility maintenance, 30 minutes before sunset and do not restart until 30 minutes after sunrise, using U.S. Naval Observatory times.
obl-0465.trigger: CTS active season or within 300 feet of suitable CTS aquatic habitat
monitorSigns: vehicles on access road at night

locators.excerpt: During the CTS active season or within 300 feet of suitable CTS aquatic habitat, Permittee shall terminate all Covered Activities not encircled by an exclusion barrier, including use and/or construction of access roads for preconstruction activities, SCADA and transmission line construction and maintenance, and facility maintenance no less than 30 minutes before sunset and shall not resume Covered Activities until 30 minutes after sunrise. Permittee shall use sunrise and sunset times established by the U.S. Naval Observatory Astronomical Applications Department for determining when Covered Activities shall terminate and resume.

obl-0466.title: Crews do not excavate or move potential CTS refuge features.

locators.excerpt: All excavation of potential refuge features, including burrows, individual rocks and rock piles, and other accessible features with an entrance diameter of greater than or equal to 0.5 inches, as well as gopher digging piles and mounds, shall be carried out by the Designated Biologist(s).

obl-0467.title: Place refuge cover such as logs, cover boards or leaf litter along both sides of the barrier.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall provide refuge opportunities such as natural cover objects (such as fallen logs and branches), artificial cover boards, or leaf litter along or near both sides of the barrier.

obl-0468.title: Do not begin ground disturbance, vegetation clearing or exclusion fence installation in CTS habitat until the CTS clearance (walking) survey is complete.
obl-0468.trigger: Suitable CTS habitat, before ground disturbance, vegetation clearing or fence installation

locators.excerpt: The Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological monitor(s) shall complete walking surveys of the Project construction site for CTS before the start of any vegetation clearing or ground disturbing Covered Activities (e.g., soil deposition areas; preconstruction activities such as field investigations; SCADA, transmission line, or access road construction, maintenance, or improvement sites; or exclusion fence installation and repair sites) by completing nocturnal walking or cover-board surveys in each of the construction sites located within suitable upland habitat, within or within 1.3 miles from any suitable CTS breeding sites (aquatic habitat), and beneath any woody debris or other potential refugia for CTS.
Prior to initiation of ground disturbing Covered Activities the Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall conduct a CTS survey consistent with Condition of Approval 11.38

Clearance surveys will be conducted by a USFWS- and CDFW-approved biologist immediately prior to the initiation of any ground-disturbing activities or vegetation clearing, including immediately prior to exclusion fence installation, in areas identified as having suitable California tiger salamander habitat.

obl-0469.title: Do not start initial ground disturbance between November 1 and March 31 (April 30 in wet years) in suitable California tiger salamander habitat.
obl-0469.trigger: Areas identified as suitable CTS habitat, to the extent practicable
monitorSigns: initial grading in November to March in CTS habitat

locators.excerpt: To the extent practicable, initial ground-disturbing activities will not be conducted between November 1 and March 31, or extended to April 30 during wet years, in areas identified during the planning stages as providing suitable California tiger salamander habitat, to avoid the period when they are most likely to be moving through upland areas.

obl-0470.title: Install a high-visibility CTS exclusion barrier along the construction footprint perimeter at any site within or 300 feet of suitable CTS habitat, or as CDFW approves.
obl-0470.trigger: Sites within or within 300 feet of suitable CTS habitat

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall install a high visibility exclusion barrier to prevent CTS from dispersing into the Project construction site. Permittee shall place the barrier along the perimeter of the construction footprint for any site within or 300 feet of any suitable CTS upland or aquatic habitat, or as approved by CDFW.

obl-0471.title: Do not restart work at a site after rain until the Designated Biologist has surveyed it.

locators.excerpt: The Designated Biologist(s) shall survey each Project construction site before Covered Activities resume, using the CDFW-approved preconstruction survey protocol (Condition of Approval 11.38).

obl-0472.title: Stop work within 75 feet of a refuge where a CTS or similar salamander retreated, until the Designated Biologist is contacted and on site.
obl-0472.trigger: When a CTS is seen retreating into a refuge on site

locators.excerpt: If Project personnel observe CTS, or a salamander resembling CTS, retreating into an underground burrow, crack or crevice, or under woody debris for refuge within a construction site, Permittee shall prohibit Covered Activities within a 75-foot radius of that refuge (no-activity buffer) until the Designated Biologist(s) is contacted and on-site.

obl-0473.title: Work on paved roads, farm roads, shoulders and similarly disturbed areas where possible.
monitorSigns: work in undisturbed ground when road available

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall conduct Covered Activities within paved roads, farm roads, road shoulders, and similarly disturbed and compacted areas where possible.

obl-0474.title: Drive no faster than 10 mph in suitable CTS habitat before ground clearance, and after clearance within 300 feet of aquatic habitat or 75 feet of a flagged burrow, except where that would unsafely impede traffic.

locators.excerpt: Project-related vehicles shall observe a speed limit of 10 miles per hour within suitable CTS habitat prior to ground clearance. After ground clearance, the speed limit shall be observed within 300 feet of suitable aquatic habitat or 75 feet from a flagged burrow, except on roads where 10 miles per hour would unsafely impede the normal flow of traffic.

obl-0475.title: Mow in rows that do not concentrate animals in the center of the site, only in daytime and dry conditions (no rain in prior 24 hours), and only when the biologist says CTS is unlikely to be aboveground.

locators.excerpt: Mowing shall occur in rows in a pattern that would not concentrate animals in the center of the construction site and shall only occur during the day in dry conditions (no rain within the past 24 hours) when the Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) determines CTS is unlikely to be aboveground.

obl-0476.title: Mow grasses within 24 hours of starting preconstruction surveys in upland habitat where ground disturbance will occur and within the 75-foot boundary.
obl-0476.trigger: When vegetation removal is needed in suitable upland habitat
monitorSigns: mowing not timed with survey start

locators.excerpt: If Covered Activities require the removal or maintenance of vegetation, within suitable upland habitat, Permittee shall mow grasses within 24 hours of initiation of preconstruction surveys (see Condition of Approval 11.42) within suitable upland habitat in each Project construction site where ground disturbance will occur and within the 75-foot boundary.

obl-0477.title: Do not introduce predatory fish (bass, sunfish, bluegill, catfish, mosquitofish, fathead minnows and similar) or amphibians (bullfrogs, barred or Arizona tiger salamanders and similar) within 1.3 miles of suitable CTS aquatic or breeding habitat.
obl-0477.trigger: Within 1.3 miles of suitable CTS aquatic/breeding habitat
monitorSigns: fish released into ditch near breeding pond

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall not introduce predatory fishes (including but not limited to largemouth bass, redear sunfish, bluegill, catfish, mosquitofish, and fathead minnows) or amphibians (including but not limited to bullfrogs, barred tiger salamanders, and Arizona tiger salamanders) within 1.3 miles of suitable aquatic/breeding CTS habitat.

obl-0478.title: Limit ground-disturbing heavy-equipment work in suitable upland and aquatic CTS habitat to July 15 to October 15.
obl-0478.trigger: Ground disturbance in suitable CTS habitat

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall limit ground-disturbing Covered Activities in suitable upland habitat and aquatic habitat involving construction and heavy equipment use (such as excavation, road construction, grading, trenching, pipe and culvert installation) to the period of July 15 to October 15 of each year (dry season).

obl-0479.title: Do not pick up or handle any CTS. Only the Designated Biologist may capture or handle CTS.
obl-0479.trigger: All Project personnel, at all times

locators.excerpt: No Project personnel shall capture and/or handle CTS except the Designated Biologist(s).

obl-0480.title: South of Byron Highway, mark suitable CTS aquatic breeding habitat in work areas (preconstruction, SCADA, transmission line and access road sites) with poly wire or CDFW-approved flagging showing a no-activity buffer of at least 300 feet, and keep all work out of the habitat and buffer.
obl-0480.trigger: Work areas south of Byron Highway, once suitable breeding habitat is identified

locators.excerpt: If the Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) identifies suitable aquatic breeding habitat within the Project Area south of Byron Highway, Permittee shall demarcate a no-activity buffer of at least 300 feet around the suitable aquatic breeding habitat and avoid Covered Activities within the suitable aquatic breeding habitat and no-activity buffer.

South of Byron Highway, Permittee shall delineate suitable CTS aquatic habitat within areas affected by Covered Activities including preconstruction activities, and SCADA, transmission line, and access road construction and maintenance sites with poly wire or other visible flagging approved by CDFW to demarcate a no-activity buffer. of at least 300 feet around suitable breeding habitat.

obl-0481.title: Install amphibian exclusion fencing along the construction site perimeter no more than 14 days before construction (staging, vegetation removal, grading) starts in the area.
obl-0481.trigger: When California tiger salamander habitat is within 300 feet of construction
monitorSigns: fence installed more than 14 days early

locators.excerpt: When there is California tiger salamander habitat within 300 feet of construction activities, exclusion fencing will be installed along the perimeter of construction sites to protect California tiger salamander habitat and minimize the potential for salamanders to enter the construction work area. The perimeter of construction sites within 300 feet of California tiger salamander habitat will be fenced with fencing material suitable for excluding amphibians by no more than 14 days prior to the start of construction activities (e.g., staging, vegetation removal, grading) in a given area.

obl-0482.title: Stop work when the biologist calls a stop for CTS in lit areas, and redirect lights away from burrows.
obl-0482.trigger: When the biologist stops work for CTS

locators.excerpt: If CTS is found aboveground, the Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall have the authority to stop Covered Activities until the light is directed away from the burrows, the CTS individual moves out of the illuminated area, or the CTS individual is relocated away from the illuminated area by the Designated Biologist(s) to a suitable location following the CTS Relocation Plan (Condition of Approval 11.51).

obl-0483.title: Report any CTS found to the Designated Biologist and leave it for the biologist to move.

locators.excerpt: If the Designated Biologist(s), Biological Monitor(s), or any Project personnel discover CTS, the Designated Biologist(s) shall move the animal to a safe location nearby following the CTS Relocation Plan required by Condition of Approval 11.51.

obl-0484.title: Do not disturb a CTS refuge that cannot be avoided until the Designated Biologist has relocated the animal.
obl-0484.trigger: When work cannot avoid a CTS refuge

locators.excerpt: If the Covered Activities cannot avoid the refuge, only the Designated Biologist(s) shall excavate, expose, and relocate the CTS in accordance with Condition of Approval 11.51.

obl-0485.title: Where work cannot avoid breeding habitat or its buffer, work there only July 15 to October 15.
obl-0485.trigger: Work within suitable CTS breeding habitat or buffer
monitorSigns: buffer work outside Jul 15 to Oct 15

locators.excerpt: Where Covered Activities cannot be avoided within the suitable aquatic breeding habitat or no-activity buffer, Permittee shall restrict Covered Activities to the dry season of July 15 – October 15 (Condition of Approval 11.44).

obl-0486.title: Keep geotechnical exploration outside the delineated breeding habitat.

locators.excerpt: DWR will restrict geotechnical exploration to areas outside of the delineated breeding habitat.

obl-0487.title: Do not start work at a site until the preconstruction CTS survey is done.
obl-0487.trigger: Before Covered Activities at each site

locators.excerpt: The Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall conduct CTS surveys following CDFW- approved protocols (Condition of Approval 11.38) within the boundaries of each Project site plus a surrounding 75-foot buffer zone following the 2003 Interim Guidance on Site Assessment and Field Surveys for Determining Presence or a Negative Findings of the California Tiger Salamander 39 prior to the initiation of Covered Activities.

obl-0488.title: Add redirection points at access gates and at least every 100 feet to steer CTS back to habitat.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall design the exclusion barrier to include redirection points at access gates and at no greater than 100-foot intervals (e.g., at least five feet of the fencing perpendicular to the exclusion barrier) to redirect CTS on the outside of the barrier back to intact habitat.

obl-0489.title: Do not start Covered Activities until CDFW has approved the CTS Relocation Plan in writing.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall prepare a CTS Mortality Reduction and Relocation Plan (CTS Relocation Plan) and submit it to CDFW for written approval as part of the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package (see Condition of Approval 6.2) prior to initiating Covered Activities.

obl-0490.title: Implement the site-specific CTS measures agreed with CDFW.
obl-0490.trigger: Where the 300-foot buffer cannot be kept

locators.excerpt: Where suitable aquatic breeding habitat cannot be avoided by 300 feet, Permittee shall notify and coordinate with CDFW to implement site-specific avoidance and minimization measures through the appropriate Phase Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6.2).

obl-0491.title: Do not start earthmoving in an area until the Designated Biologist has flagged the refugia there.
obl-0491.trigger: Before earthmoving in each area of the construction site
monitorSigns: earthmoving with no flagging in place

locators.excerpt: The Designated Biologist(s) shall flag these areas, or other habitat features that are outside of the area for direct ground disturbance within the Project construction site prior to initiation of earthmoving activities in those areas.

obl-0492.title: Work outside the April 1 to October 31 window (May 1 to October 31 in wet years) only in already-disturbed areas where clearance surveys are done and exclusion fencing is in place.
obl-0492.trigger: After initial ground disturbance in CTS habitat

locators.excerpt: Once clearance surveys have been conducted, exclusionary fence is in place, the area has been surveyed, and initial ground disturbance has occurred, work within the disturbed area can occur outside the construction window (defined as April 1 through October 31 or, during wet years, May 1 through October 31).

obl-0493.title: Do not begin earthmoving in an area until burrows and refugia outside the disturbance zone have been flagged at least five days earlier.
obl-0493.trigger: Before earthmoving in each area of the construction site

locators.excerpt: The Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall identify and flag all potential burrows, soil cracks, crevices, or other habitat features that are outside of the area planned for direct disturbance (e.g., grading, excavation, etc.) and within the Project construction site no less than five days prior to earthmoving activities in those areas.

The Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall identify and flag all potential burrows, soil cracks, crevices, or other habitat features that are outside of the area planned for direct disturbance (e.g., grading, excavation, etc.) and within the Project construction site, no less than five days prior to earthmoving activities in those areas.

obl-0494.title: Design the barrier so CTS cannot climb over or get under through burrows or cracks.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall design the barrier to prevent CTS from climbing over it or under it through burrows or cracks.

obl-0495.title: Start before July 15 only if the site has been dry 30 days, the CTS survey is done and exclusion barriers are installed.

locators.excerpt: Covered Activities may begin prior to July 15 if the location in which work will occur has been dry for a minimum of 30 days prior to initiating work, the Designated Biologist(s) has conducted surveys for presence of CTS consistent with Condition of Approval 11.42, and exclusion barriers have been installed.

obl-0496.title: Leave any CTS that cannot move away for the Designated Biologist to capture.
obl-0496.trigger: When anyone finds such a CTS on site

locators.excerpt: If any person discovers a CTS in the Project construction site that cannot move away from Covered Activities on its own, only the CDFW approved Designated Biologist(s) shall capture it using CDFW-approved methodologies.

obl-0497.title: Use signs, stakes, or flags for refugia buffers that look clearly different from work-area markings.
monitorSigns: buffer flagging same color as work-area flagging
refugia stakes confused with survey stakes

locators.excerpt: Signs, stakes, and/or flags shall be clearly distinguishable from markings used to delineate work areas.

obl-0498.title: Do not do non-emergency post-construction work at night in CTS habitat at any time of year unless CDFW authorizes it.
obl-0498.trigger: Post-construction activities in CTS habitat at night
monitorSigns: non-emergency night work in CTS habitat

locators.excerpt: Covered Activities subsequent to construction shall not occur at night for non-emergency work in CTS habitat at any time of the year unless otherwise authorized by CDFW.

obl-0499.title: Tell the Designated Biologist immediately if a CTS is hurt or killed by the work, or is found dead or injured near preconstruction, construction or maintenance areas.
obl-0499.trigger: Any CTS injury, death, or dead or injured CTS found near Project work areas
monitorSigns: dead salamander found, biologist not called
crew moved injured CTS without calling biologist

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall immediately notify the Designated Biologist(s) if a CTS is injured or killed by a Covered Activity, or if a CTS is otherwise found dead or injured within the vicinity of the Project preconstruction activity, construction site, or maintenance area.

obl-0500.title: Avoid suitable CTS habitat delineated under the approved protocols to the greatest extent practicable.
obl-0500.trigger: Covered Activities near delineated CTS habitat

locators.excerpt: To the greatest extent practicable, suitable CTS habitat identified and delineated in accordance with CDFW-approved protocols (Condition of Approval 11.38) shall be completely avoided.

obl-0501.title: Keep CTS clearance work to the smallest area necessary.
obl-0501.trigger: Clearance work that could result in CTS take

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall confine ground disturbance activities that could result in take of CTS (clearance work) to the most minimal area necessary to conduct Covered Activities and shall not initiate clearance work until after exclusion fencing is installed (Condition of Approval 11.43).

obl-0502.title: Tell the Designated Biologist immediately about any CTS or similar salamander seen on the construction site, within 75 feet of it, or on access roads.
obl-0502.trigger: All phases of Covered Activities, whenever a CTS is seen on site, within 75 feet, or on access roads

locators.excerpt: All Project personnel shall inform the Designated Biologist(s) if they encounter CTS, or a salamander resembling CTS, within the Project construction site or 75 feet beyond the Project construction site, or on access roads during, all phases of Covered Activities.
If CTS is found within a construction site or 75 feet beyond the construction site (75-foot boundary), Project personnel shall notify the Designated Biologist(s) immediately.

obl-0503.title: Stop mowing when a CTS is found until the Designated Biologist relocates it per the CTS Relocation Plan.
monitorSigns: mower kept running after CTS found

locators.excerpt: If CTS is found, mowing shall cease until the CTS is relocated by the Designated Biologist(s) only in accordance with the CTS Relocation Plan (Condition of Approval 11.51).

obl-0504.title: Do not disturb known or potential CTS burrows unless they are in direct disturbance areas such as grading or excavation, or pose a risk of direct harm to CTS.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall avoid disturbing any known or potential CTS burrows unless they are in an area of direct disturbance (e.g., grading or excavation areas) or their location poses a risk of direct harm to CTS individuals.

obl-0505.title: Release one CTS per burrow where burrow density allows, and never more than three into an extensive burrow.
monitorSigns: two CTS released in one small burrow
more than three CTS in one burrow system

locators.excerpt: If burrow density allows, the Designated Biologist(s) shall only release one animal per burrow, and shall not exceed the release of a maximum of three individual CTSs into extensive burrows.

obl-0506.title: Release relocated CTS within 300 feet of where it was found, unless CDFW has agreed to another distance.
monitorSigns: release point over 300 ft from capture point
no CDFW agreement for longer distance

If aquatic habitat is identified by the designated biologist(s) within the project area southwest of Byron Highway, DWR will restrict construction activities to beyond 300 feet of breeding habitat, during the breeding season (November 1 through March 31, or extended to April 30 during wet years).

obl-0551.title: If no mitigation bank is used, prioritize California tiger salamander land acquisition for large contiguous grassland, vernal pool, and alkali seasonal wetland landscapes; connectivity to protected landscapes (including East Contra Costa HCP/NCCP lands); grasslands with stock ponds and aquatic breeding features; and lands adjacent or connected to occupied habitat.

monitorSigns: acquired parcel isolated from protected lands
parcel lacks breeding features, no rationale recorded

locators.excerpt: If a mitigation bank is not used, land acquisition for California tiger salamander will be prioritized based on the following characteristics. Large contiguous landscapes that consist of grasslands, vernal pool complex,  and alkali seasonal wetland complex and encompass the range of vegetation, hydrologic, and soil conditions that characterize these communities. Lands that maintain connectivity with protected grassland, vernal pool  complex, and alkali seasonal wetland complex landscapes near proposed construction sites, including connectivity with lands that have been protected or may be protected in the future under the East Contra Costa County Habitat Conservation Plan/Natural Community Conservation Plan. Grasslands containing stock ponds and other aquatic features that provide  aquatic breeding habitat for California tiger salamander. Adjacent or connected to occupied California tiger salamander upland or  aquatic habitat.

Any work within the Colony Active Period shall be subject to approval by CDFW.

obl-0563.title: Do not disturb vegetation or ground in CBB habitat during the spring Queen flight season or the fall Gyne flight season.
obl-0563.trigger: Queen and Gyne Flight Seasons each year
monitorSigns: grading in CBB habitat during queen flight

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall avoid conducting Covered Activities involving vegetation and ground disturbance in CBB habitat during the Queen and Gyne Flight Seasons, when Queens emerge in the spring searching for nest sites, and during the fall flight period when Gynes mate and search for overwintering habitat.

obl-0564.title: Keep a 50-foot no-activity buffer around every avoidable CBB refugium in preconstruction, construction, access road, SCADA and transmission line, and maintenance areas.
obl-0564.trigger: All listed work areas wherever refugia can be avoided
monitorSigns: work within 50 ft of flagged refugium

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall establish a 50-foot radius no-activity buffer around refugia that can be avoided within the Project preconstruction activity area, construction site, access roads, SCADA and transmission line construction areas, and maintenance areas.

obl-0565.title: If you see a CBB or look-alike bee going in or out of a possible nest, stop work within 50 feet until the biologist says the nest is inactive.
obl-0565.trigger: From the sighting until the nest senesces or is no longer in use
monitorSigns: work continued within 50 ft of nest

locators.excerpt: If Project personnel observe CBB or an insect resembling CBB entering or exiting a potential nest, or a CBB nest site, Permittee shall stop Covered Activities within 50 feet of the nest until the nest senesces or becomes inactive and is no longer in use, as determined by the Designated Biologist(s) in consultation with CDFW.

obl-0566.title: Revegetate temporarily disturbed grassland identified as suitable bumble bee habitat with a seed mix including nectar- and pollen-producing plants used by Crotch bumble bee.
obl-0566.trigger: Temporarily disturbed grassland identified by a qualified biologist as suitable habitat

locators.excerpt: Temporarily disturbed grassland identified as suitable bumble bee habitat by a qualified biologist will be revegetated using a seed mix combination that includes nectar- and pollen-producing plants commonly used as a food source by Crotch bumble bee.

obl-0567.title: If you see a CBB or look-alike bee going in or out of a possible nest, stop all work within 50 feet of it until the Designated Biologist is on site.
obl-0567.trigger: From the sighting until the Designated Biologist is contacted and on site
monitorSigns: work continued within 50 ft of nest

locators.excerpt: If Project personnel observe CBB or an insect resembling CBB entering or exiting a potential nest, or a CBB nest site, Permittee shall prohibit Covered Activities within a 50-foot radius of that nest until the Designated Biologist(s) is contacted and on-site (see Condition of Approval 11.98).

obl-0568.title: Keep ground-disturbing work out of the 50-foot no-activity buffer around CBB nests.
obl-0568.trigger: All ground-disturbing Covered Activities near CBB nests

locators.excerpt: Ground disturbing Covered Activities shall avoid CBB nests using the no-activity buffer as described in Condition of Approval 11.98.

obl-0569.title: Keep all work out of the 50-foot non-disturbance buffer around any CBB nest found in the construction, restoration or maintenance area until the biologist says the nest is inactive or work in the area is complete, whichever comes first.
obl-0569.trigger: From nest discovery, where avoidance is feasible, until the nest is inactive or work in the area is complete

locators.excerpt: If a nest is discovered during a CBB survey within the Project construction site or Project maintenance area and avoidance is feasible, a non-disturbance buffer of 50 feet shall be established around the nest until the nest senesces or becomes inactive and is no longer in use, as determined by the Designated Biologist(s) in consultation with CDFW, or until the Covered Activities are complete, whichever is first.

If a nest is discovered within the construction or restoration area, a non- disturbance buffer of 50 feet will be established around the nest until the nest senesces or becomes inactive and is no longer in use, as determined by the qualified biologist or until the project activities in the project area are complete, whichever is first.

obl-0570.title: Do not move or disturb a CBB nest yourself; wait for the Designated Biologist.
obl-0570.trigger: When Covered Activities cannot avoid a CBB nest

locators.excerpt: If the Covered Activities cannot avoid the nest, only the Designated Biologist(s) shall relocate the nest in accordance with Condition of Approval 11.102.

obl-0571.title: Call the Designated Biologist as soon as a possible CBB nest is seen.
obl-0571.trigger: Immediately on seeing a CBB entering or exiting a possible nest

locators.excerpt: If Project personnel observe CBB or an insect resembling CBB entering or exiting a potential nest, or a CBB nest site, Permittee shall prohibit Covered Activities within a 50-foot radius of that nest until the Designated Biologist(s) is contacted and on-site (see Condition of Approval 11.98).

obl-0572.title: Do not begin ground disturbance in a Project Phase until the site-level CBB surveys are done.
obl-0572.trigger: Start of ground disturbance in each Project Phase

locators.excerpt: Prior to initiation of ground disturbing Covered Activities for each Project Phase, site-level surveys shall be conducted consistent with CDFW-approved survey protocols (Condition of Approval 11.38) to determine whether CBB is present within or adjacent to proposed Covered Activities and submitted to CDFW as part of the appropriate Construction Phased Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6.2).

obl-0573.title: Mark each CBB nest buffer with high-visibility fencing, flagging, or similar material and signs, following the buffer zone design plan.
obl-0573.trigger: When a CBB nest buffer is established

locators.excerpt: Utilizing this plan, the buffer shall be delineated using high-visibility fencing, flagging, or similar materials along with appropriate signage and be maintained throughout all weather events.

obl-0574.title: Remove native or non-native flowering vegetation before bloom and before the Colony Active Period begins.
monitorSigns: flowering vegetation still standing in February

locators.excerpt: Native or non-native flowering vegetation removal shall occur prior to bloom and before the Colony Active Period to prevent colonization during the active season.

obl-0575.title: Do not start work in undisturbed CBB habitat until the CBB survey has been done.
obl-0575.trigger: Undisturbed areas of CBB habitat planned for Covered Activities
monitorSigns: work in undisturbed habitat before survey

locators.excerpt: In undisturbed areas of CBB habitat planned for Covered Activities, the Designated Biologist(s) shall perform CDFW-approved CBB survey protocols with assistance from the Biological Monitor(s) (if needed) as described in Condition of Approval 11.38.

obl-0576.title: Disturb or remove only the vegetation needed to complete the work in suitable CBB habitat.
obl-0576.trigger: Covered Activities in suitable CBB habitat

locators.excerpt: Disturbance or removal of vegetation shall be kept to the minimum necessary to complete Covered Activities in suitable CBB habitat.

obl-0577.title: During the CBB overwintering period, avoid ground disturbance in CBB habitat as much as possible, or follow the site-specific phased approach CDFW approved in the Construction Phase Authorization Package.
monitorSigns: digging in CBB habitat in winter outside approved phasing

locators.excerpt: During the overwintering period, Permittee shall avoid ground disturbance activities in CBB habitat to the greatest extent possible or develop a site-specific phased approach to implementation of activities, for CDFW approval as part of the appropriate Project Construction Phase Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6.2).

obl-0578.title: Stay completely out of delineated suitable CBB habitat.
obl-0578.trigger: All Covered Activities near habitat delineated under COA 10.4

locators.excerpt: Identified and delineated suitable CBB habitat in accordance with Condition of Approval 10.4 shall be completely avoided.

obl-0579.title: If flowering vegetation in a restoration temporary impact area must be removed during the Colony Active Period, remove it only where surveys found no foraging CBB and no active nests.
obl-0579.trigger: Temporary impact areas planned for restoration, when vegetation must be removed during bloom
monitorSigns: flowers cleared where bees were foraging

locators.excerpt: If Covered Activities cannot be avoided in temporary impact areas intended for on-site restoration during this time and vegetation needs to be removed during the bloom period for these species, Permittee shall remove flowering vegetation during the Colony Active Period in locations where there are no surveyed foraging CBB or active CBB nests.

obl-0580.title: Keep CBB nest buffer fencing, flagging, and signs in place and intact through all weather.
obl-0580.trigger: For as long as the CBB nest buffer is in place, including through storms

locators.excerpt: Utilizing this plan, the buffer shall be delineated using high-visibility fencing, flagging, or similar materials along with appropriate signage and be maintained throughout all weather events.

obl-0581.title: Survey by meandering transects through the footprint plus a 50-foot buffer where accessible, at least 1 hour after sunrise and 2 hours before sunset (ideally 9 a.m. to 1 p.m.), for the time needed or 30 minutes, whichever is longer.

locators.excerpt: The qualified biologist will perform meandering transects through the planned construction footprint, plus a 50-foot buffer where accessible, at least an hour after sunrise and at least two hours before sunset, though ideally between 9:00 a.m. and 1:00 p.m., to visually survey the area for bumble bee activity. The duration of the survey will be the minimum amount of time necessary to adequately survey the area, or 30 minutes, whichever is longer.

obl-0582.title: Only a CDFW-approved Designated Biologist with bumble bee capture and handling expertise may relocate a CBB nest the work cannot avoid, following COA 11.102.
monitorSigns: nest moved by monitor or crew

locators.excerpt: The CDFW- approved Designated Biologist(s) with appropriate expertise in bumble bee capture and handling shall attempt to relocate the nest to a suitable location outside of the Project construction site following guidance from CDFW.
If the Covered Activities cannot avoid the nest, only the Designated Biologist(s) shall relocate the nest in accordance with Condition of Approval 11.102.

obl-0583.title: Perform CDFW-approved CBB survey protocols in undisturbed CBB habitat planned for Covered Activities.
obl-0583.trigger: Undisturbed areas of CBB habitat planned for Covered Activities
monitorSigns: undisturbed habitat entered with no survey record

locators.excerpt: In undisturbed areas of CBB habitat planned for Covered Activities, the Designated Biologist(s) shall perform CDFW-approved CBB survey protocols with assistance from the Biological Monitor(s) (if needed) as described in Condition of Approval 11.38.

obl-0584.title: Conduct CDFW-approved CBB surveys each year to set the dates of the Queen and Gyne flight seasons and the overwintering period.

locators.excerpt: To determine these time periods each year, the Designated Biologist(s) shall conduct CDFW-approved CBB surveys (Condition of Approval 11.38).

obl-0585.title: Conduct site-level CBB surveys under CDFW-approved protocols to find out whether CBB is present in or next to the planned work.
obl-0585.trigger: Each Project Phase, before ground-disturbing Covered Activities begin
monitorSigns: phase started with no site-level survey

locators.excerpt: Prior to initiation of ground disturbing Covered Activities for each Project Phase, site-level surveys shall be conducted consistent with CDFW-approved survey protocols (Condition of Approval 11.38) to determine whether CBB is present within or adjacent to proposed Covered Activities and submitted to CDFW as part of the appropriate Construction Phased Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6.2).

obl-0586.title: Conduct at least three preconstruction CBB surveys beyond the baseline survey, spaced two to four weeks apart unless CDFW approves otherwise, with the last (clearance) survey within 72 hours before work.
obl-0586.trigger: Each construction site in CBB habitat, before ground disturbance or vegetation removal during the active season (about February 1 to October 31)
monitorSigns: last survey more than 72 hours before work

locators.excerpt: At least three surveys shall be conducted in addition to the baseline preconstruction survey, with each Project construction site survey spaced two to four weeks apart, unless otherwise approved by CDFW, to account for variability in resources and activity, with the last survey taking place within 72 hours prior to construction activity.

A total of three preconstruction surveys will be conducted prior to any ground-disturbing project activities or vegetation removal that will take place during the active season for Crotch bumble bee (approximately February 1 through October 31). Each preconstruction 9 survey will, ideally, be spaced 2 to 4 weeks apart, with the last preconstruction survey (i.e., clearance survey) taking place within 72 hours prior to construction activity.

obl-0587.title: Provide biological construction monitoring as long as needed to ensure the Crotch bumble bee measures are carried out.
obl-0587.trigger: When a Crotch bumble bee nest is found

locators.excerpt: If a Crotch bumble bee nest is found, a qualified biologist will provide biological construction monitoring as long as needed to ensure implementation of applicable measures below.

obl-0588.title: Have a Designated Biologist or Biological Monitor on site once Covered Activities in CBB habitat have begun.
obl-0588.trigger: Every work day once Covered Activities in CBB habitat have begun
monitorSigns: work in CBB habitat with no biologist on site

locators.excerpt: Once Covered Activities within CBB habitat have begun, the Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall be onsite and shall conduct daily visual sweeps of the Project construction site for CBB flight activity at the start of the daily work window and shall intermittently repeat these visual sweeps throughout the daily work window.

obl-0589.title: Repeat the CBB survey in suitable CBB habitat before ground disturbance or other Covered Activities resume after a stop of more than 14 calendar days.
obl-0589.trigger: After work stops for more than 14 calendar days, before it resumes
monitorSigns: work restarted after 14-day stop, no resurvey
work resumed after 3-week gap, no resurvey

locators.excerpt: If Covered Activities stop for more than 14 calendar days, the Designated Biologist(s) with assistance (if needed) from the Biological Monitor(s) shall repeat CBB surveys within suitable CBB habitat, prior to resuming Covered Activities.

if there is a lapse in initial construction disturbance greater than 14 calendar days, an additional CBB survey shall be repeated by the Designated Biologist(s) prior to any ground disturbance activities resuming.

obl-0590.title: Sweep the construction site visually for CBB flight activity at the start of each work day and repeat sweeps through the day.
obl-0590.trigger: Start of each daily work window, then intermittently through it

locators.excerpt: Once Covered Activities within CBB habitat have begun, the Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall be onsite and shall conduct daily visual sweeps of the Project construction site for CBB flight activity at the start of the daily work window and shall intermittently repeat these visual sweeps throughout the daily work window.

obl-0591.title: Repeat the three construction-phase CBB survey efforts each year Covered Activities are expected in or within 50 feet of suitable CBB habitat.
obl-0591.trigger: Each year with Covered Activities in or within 50 feet of suitable CBB habitat
monitorSigns: no surveys this year despite work near habitat
fewer than three surveys this year

locators.excerpt: Survey efforts shall occur each year Covered Activities are expected to occur in or within 50 feet of suitable CBB habitat, since bumble bees have an annual life cycle.

The three survey efforts conducted during the Project construction phase(s) shall occur each year Covered Activities are expected to occur in suitable CBB habitat and shall be reported to CDFW by the Permittee within the Monthly Compliance Reporting (Condition of Approval 10.12) and summarized within each Annual Status Report (Condition of Approval 10.13).

obl-0592.title: Monitor each relocated CBB nest for at least one week, watching for premature absence of bee activity, and determine whether the relocation succeeded.
monitorSigns: no bee activity at relocated nest
no follow-up check of relocated nest

locators.excerpt: To offset the unsuccessful relocation of a nest, as determined by a qualified biologist, suitable habitat will be created, enhanced, or protected, using the mitigation mechanisms described above.

Once relocated, the nest shall be monitored for at least one week by the Designated Biologist(s). If monitoring suggests the nest relocation was successful (i.e., nest is not immediately abandoned following relocation, bees are observed returning to the relocated nest following foraging activities, and the nest is continued to be used at least one week following relocation), no further measures are required.

If monitoring finds nest relocation to be unsuccessful, as determined through premature absence of bee activity, DWR will create or enhance and protect suitable foraging and nesting habitat at a ratio of 1:1 for the lost suitable habitat associated with the nest (i.e., 1 acre of created or enhanced and protected habitat to 1 acre of permanently lost habitat).

obl-0593.title: Watch each buffered CBB nest and decide, in consultation with CDFW, when it has senesced or is no longer in use.
obl-0593.trigger: While a CBB nest buffer is in place and work is stopped near the nest
monitorSigns: buffer released with no CDFW consultation
nest cleared with no CDFW consultation

locators.excerpt: If Project personnel observe CBB or an insect resembling CBB entering or exiting a potential nest, or a CBB nest site, Permittee shall stop Covered Activities within 50 feet of the nest until the nest senesces or becomes inactive and is no longer in use, as determined by the Designated Biologist(s) in consultation with CDFW.

If a nest is discovered during a CBB survey within the Project construction site or Project maintenance area and avoidance is feasible, a non-disturbance buffer of 50 feet shall be established around the nest until the nest senesces or becomes inactive and is no longer in use, as determined by the Designated Biologist(s) in consultation with CDFW, or until the Covered Activities are complete, whichever is first.

obl-0594.title: Flag CBB refugia and other habitat features outside the direct disturbance area before earthmoving begins there.
obl-0594.trigger: Before earthmoving in each area of the construction site

locators.excerpt: The Designated Biologist(s) shall flag these areas, or other habitat features that are outside of the area for direct ground disturbance within the Project construction site prior to initiation of earthmoving activities in those areas.

obl-0595.title: Label each carcass with collection number, species, time and date, location, GPS with datum and error, circumstances of death, collector name and contact, and ITP Number.

locators.excerpt: The label shall be appropriately recorded with a unique identifier (collection number), species name, time and date of collection, collection location, GPS location (including datum and horizontal error in feet), circumstances surrounding death, collector name and contact information (phone number and email), and ITP Number.

obl-0596.title: Survey for foraging CBB and active nests under the CDFW-approved protocol before ground disturbance or vegetation removal in suitable CBB habitat during the colony active period or until flowering vegetation has largely dried.
obl-0596.trigger: Construction and post-construction maintenance, February 1 to October 31 or until flowering vegetation is largely desiccated
monitorSigns: vegetation removed with no pre-disturbance survey

locators.excerpt: During the Project construction and postconstruction maintenance phases, surveys shall be conducted by the Designated Biologist(s) with assistance (if needed) from the Biological Monitor(s) following the CDFW-approved CBB survey protocol (Condition of Approval 11.38) prior to any ground-disturbing Covered Activities or vegetation removal within suitable CBB habitat during the colony active period (February 1 – October 31) or until all flowering vegetation is largely desiccated, to detect foraging CBB and determine if any active nests are within the Project construction site or Project maintenance area.

obl-0597.title: Record each CBB nest location with GPS.
obl-0597.trigger: When a CBB nest is found

locators.excerpt: The nest location shall be recorded with global positioning system (GPS) and be reported to CDFW within 24 hours (one calendar day) of finding the nest.

obl-0598.title: Photograph and salvage each CBB carcass, seal it in a clean labeled plastic bag or vial, and store it frozen for shipment to the CDFW Wildlife Health Lab.
obl-0598.trigger: Whenever a CBB carcass is found

locators.excerpt: The carcass shall be photographed, salvaged, and placed in a labeled, clean plastic, resealable bag or vial and stored in a freezer by the Designated Biologist(s) for shipment to CDFW Wildlife Health Lab.

obl-0599.title: Make every effort to find the active nest when a suspected or confirmed CBB is detected on the construction site.
obl-0599.trigger: After a CBB detection within the construction site
monitorSigns: CBB detected, no nest search logged

locators.excerpt: If a suspected or confirmed CBB individual is detected within the Project construction site, every effort shall be made by the Designated Biologist(s) with assistance (if needed) from the Biological Monitor(s) to find the active nest.

obl-0600.title: Before flowering vegetation is removed during the Colony Active Period, confirm the area has no foraging CBB or active CBB nests.
obl-0600.trigger: Before any flowering vegetation removal during the Colony Active Period

locators.excerpt: If Covered Activities cannot be avoided in temporary impact areas intended for on-site restoration during this time and vegetation needs to be removed during the bloom period for these species, Permittee shall remove flowering vegetation during the Colony Active Period in locations where there are no surveyed foraging CBB or active CBB nests.

obl-0601.title: Relocate an unavoidable CBB nest to suitable habitat outside the construction site and project footprint, following CDFW guidance and the Xerces Society guidelines or the latest CDFW-approved guidelines.
obl-0601.trigger: When a CBB nest cannot be avoided

locators.excerpt: The CDFW- approved Designated Biologist(s) with appropriate expertise in bumble bee capture and handling shall attempt to relocate the nest to a suitable location outside of the Project construction site following guidance from CDFW. Nest relocation efforts shall follow the general guidelines described by The Xerces Society in Bumble Bees: Nesting and Overwintering 47 or the most recently available CDFW-approved guidelines.
A qualified biologist will attempt to relocate the nest to a suitable location outside the project footprint.

obl-0602.title: Survey potential CBB habitat under CDFW-approved protocols to confirm whether overwintering CBB are absent before vegetation removal.
obl-0602.trigger: Before vegetation removal in potential CBB habitat

locators.excerpt: Within potential habitat, Permittee shall avoid removal of vegetation such as woody plants, tall grasses, leaf litter or loose soils until CDFW-approved CBB survey protocols (Condition of Approval 11.38) have been performed by the Designated Biologist(s) and absence of overwintering CBB is confirmed.

obl-0603.title: Report each CBB nest location to CDFW within 24 hours of finding it.
obl-0603.trigger: Within 24 hours (one calendar day) of finding a nest
monitorSigns: nest found, no CDFW report within 24 hours

locators.excerpt: The nest location shall be recorded with global positioning system (GPS) and be reported to CDFW within 24 hours (one calendar day) of finding the nest.

obl-0604.title: Include site management and use restrictions, including on insecticide application per EPA’s Guidance for Assessing Pesticide Risks to Bees, in site protection instruments for Crotch bumble bee habitat.
obl-0604.trigger: Each site protection instrument for Crotch bumble bee habitat

locators.excerpt: Site protection instruments developed to protect Crotch bumble bee habitat would include site management and site use restrictions, including the application of insecticides, as described in U.S. Environmental Protection Agency Guidance for Assessing Pesticide Risks to Bees (U.S. Environmental Protection Agency 2014) (also see Section 3F.4.2.2).

obl-0605.title: Obtain CDFW approval before any work in CBB habitat during the Colony Active Period, after the Designated Biologist has surveyed.
obl-0605.trigger: Before any work during the Colony Active Period
monitorSigns: active-period work started, no CDFW approval on file

locators.excerpt: If feasible, Covered Activities shall avoid vegetation and ground disturbing impacts to CBB and suitable habitat during the Colony Active Period (February 1 – October 31) each year until the expiration of this ITP unless otherwise approved by CDFW after the Designated Biologist(s) has conducted CBB surveys (see Condition of Approval 11.97) consistent with CDFW-approved protocols (Condition of Approval 11.38). Any work within the Colony Active Period shall be subject to approval by CDFW.

obl-0606.title: Notify CDFW within 48 hours of a suspected or confirmed Crotch bumble bee identified during surveys.
monitorSigns: bee detection logged, no CDFW notice within 48 hours

locators.excerpt: If a suspected or confirmed Crotch bumble bee is identified during any of these surveys, the qualified biologist will notify CDFW within 48 hours.

obl-0607.title: Contact CDFW within 24 hours when a CBB nest may be lost to ground disturbance or cannot be avoided, to set next steps.
obl-0607.trigger: Within 24 hours of learning a nest may be lost or cannot be avoided
monitorSigns: unavoidable nest logged, no CDFW contact within 24 hours

locators.excerpt: In the extraordinary case that a nest may be lost because of ground disturbance or if the nest cannot be avoided and will be lost, CDFW shall be contacted immediately (within 24 hours) to determine next steps.

obl-0608.title: When a qualified biologist determines a CBB nest relocation failed, offset it by creating or enhancing and protecting suitable foraging and nesting habitat at 1:1 for the suitable habitat lost with the nest.
obl-0608.trigger: When a nest relocation is determined unsuccessful
monitorSigns: failed relocation logged, no habitat offset

locators.excerpt: To offset the unsuccessful relocation of a nest, as determined by a qualified biologist, suitable habitat will be created, enhanced, or protected, using the mitigation mechanisms described above.

If monitoring finds nest relocation to be unsuccessful, as determined through premature absence of bee activity, DWR will create or enhance and protect suitable foraging and nesting habitat at a ratio of 1:1 for the lost suitable habitat associated with the nest (i.e., 1 acre of created or enhanced and protected habitat to 1 acre of permanently lost habitat).

obl-0609.title: Contact CDFW by telephone and email within 24 hours when a suspected or confirmed CBB is detected on the construction site.
obl-0609.trigger: Within 24 hours of a CBB detection on the construction site
monitorSigns: CBB seen on site, no CDFW call within 24 hours

locators.excerpt: If a suspected or confirmed CBB is detected in the Project construction site, the Designated Representative or Designated Biologist(s) shall contact CDFW by telephone and email within 24 hours.

obl-0610.title: Notify CDFW within 24 hours when a survey finds a suspected or confirmed CBB.
obl-0610.trigger: Within 24 hours of a CBB detection during surveys
monitorSigns: CBB logged on survey, no CDFW notice within 24 hours

locators.excerpt: If a suspected or confirmed CBB is identified during any of these surveys, the Designated Biologist(s) shall notify CDFW within 24 hours.

obl-0611.title: Offset impacts on Crotch bumble bees and their habitat through habitat creation or enhancement, site protection instruments, CDFW-approved bank credits, or a CDFW-approved non-bank site.
obl-0611.trigger: All impacts on Crotch bumble bees and habitat
monitorSigns: impact not offset by any listed mechanism

locators.excerpt: Impacts on Crotch bumble bees and their habitat will be offset either through creation or enhancement of suitable habitat, land preservation through site protection instruments, the purchase of credits through a CDFW-approved mitigation bank, or the creation of non-bank site approved by CDFW.

obl-0612.title: Select and develop Crotch bumble bee mitigation sites with flower-rich natural habitat, grassland, and scrub that include underground cavities for nesting and overwintering, and undisturbed aboveground nesting resources such as leaf litter, wood piles, grass tufts, or rock walls.
obl-0612.trigger: All Crotch bumble bee mitigation sites

locators.excerpt: Mitigation sites will include flower rich natural habitats, grassland, and scrub habitats that include underground cavities (e.g., animal burrows) for nesting and overwintering and aboveground undisturbed areas with nesting resources, such as leaf litter or other complex habitat such as wood piles, tufts of grass, or rock walls for additional overwintering habitat (Xerces Society et al. 2018).

obl-0613.title: Monitor the effectiveness of the delta smelt mitigation over the long term.
obl-0613.trigger: Long term, delta smelt mitigation sites

locators.excerpt: This mitigation measure’s effectiveness will be subject to long-term monitoring

obl-0614.title: Restore tidal habitat for delta smelt, concentrated in the north Delta Arc or other areas deemed appropriate through consultation with USFWS and CDFW.
obl-0614.trigger: All project-related impacts on delta smelt
monitorSigns: restoration outside north Delta Arc without consultation

locators.excerpt: DWR will mitigate potential project-related impacts on delta smelt by restoring tidal habitat, concentrated within the north Delta Arc or other areas deemed appropriate through consultation with USFWS and CDFW.

obl-0615.title: Seal overlapped fence sections so snakes cannot get trapped in the seam.

locators.excerpt: Fencing that is overlapped to connect different sections of material shall be sealed in a manner that does not allow GGS to become entrapped.

obl-0616.title: Work in suitable GGS habitat only during low rainfall (under 0.25 inch per 24 hours) and dry weather (under 40% chance of rain), unless CDFW approves otherwise.
obl-0616.trigger: All Covered Activities within suitable GGS habitat
monitorSigns: working in GGS habitat in rain
work on day with 60% rain forecast

locators.excerpt: The work period for Covered Activities within suitable GGS habitat shall be restricted to periods of low rainfall (less than 0.25 inch per 24-hour period) and periods of dry weather (with less than a 40 percent chance of rain) unless otherwise approved by CDFW.

obl-0617.title: Start construction and clear suitable habitat only between May 1 and October 1; stay out of giant garter snake habitat October 1 to May 1, except inside areas already cleared and fenced.
obl-0617.trigger: Where work does not fully avoid suitable habitat
monitorSigns: clearing in habitat between Oct 1 and May 1
new start in habitat during brumation

locators.excerpt: Initiate construction and clear suitable habitat in the summer months, between May 1 and October 1, and avoid giant garter snake habitat during periods of brumation (between October 1 and May 1). Once a construction site has been cleared and exclusionary fencing is in place, work within the cleared area can occur between October 1 and May 1.

obl-0618.title: Check under vehicles and equipment idle more than 1 hour or parked overnight for giant garter snakes before moving them.
obl-0618.trigger: Before moving any vehicle idle over 1 hour or parked overnight

locators.excerpt: Visually check for giant garter snake under any vehicles or equipment that have been idle for more than 1 hour, or parked overnight, prior to moving the vehicles.

obl-0619.title: If a GGS or look-alike snake is on the road, let it move off on its own, steer around it, or call the biologist to move it.
obl-0619.trigger: Any snake resembling GGS on or crossing a roadway

locators.excerpt: If GGS, or any snake resembling GGS, is found on or traversing a roadway, Project personnel shall allow the snake to safely move off the road on its own, maneuver to avoid striking it, or shall notify the Designated Biologist(s) to move the snake off the road (see Condition of Approval 11.67).

obl-0620.title: Mow in suitable GGS habitat only between July 1 and September 30, and only after the biologist's clearance survey.
obl-0620.trigger: Vegetation removal or maintenance in suitable GGS habitat

locators.excerpt: If Covered Activities require the removal or maintenance of vegetation, Permittee shall limit mowing to occur only between July 1 to September 30 in suitable GGS habitat and after a Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) has performed clearance surveys to ensure absence of GGS.

obl-0621.title: Obey Project speed limits (COA 11.11) in construction sites and on access roads within suitable GGS upland habitat.
obl-0621.trigger: Construction sites and access roads in suitable GGS upland habitat

locators.excerpt: Project-related vehicle traffic shall observe speed limits consistent with Condition of Approval 11.11 in Project construction sites and access roads within suitable GGS upland habitat.

obl-0622.title: Keep a 50-foot no-activity buffer around flagged avoidable burrows at preconstruction, construction, access road, SCADA, transmission line and maintenance sites and the three-foot buffer zone.
obl-0622.trigger: Around flagged burrows at all listed work sites
monitorSigns: equipment within 50 ft of flagged burrow

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall establish a 50-foot radius no-activity buffer around flagged burrows that can be avoided within the preconstruction activity sites, constructions sites, access roads, SCADA and transmission line construction, and maintenance sites, and the three-foot buffer zone.

obl-0623.title: Store equipment in designated staging areas at least 200 feet from giant garter snake aquatic habitat, to the extent practicable.
obl-0623.trigger: Equipment storage near GGS aquatic habitat
monitorSigns: equipment parked within 200 feet of water

locators.excerpt: Store equipment in designated staging area areas at least 200 feet away from giant garter snake aquatic habitat to the extent practicable.

obl-0624.title: Mark suitable GGS aquatic habitat at field investigation, SCADA, transmission line and access road sites with highly visible poly wire or CDFW-approved flagging as a no-disturbance zone.
obl-0624.trigger: Preconstruction field investigation, SCADA, transmission line and access road construction and maintenance sites

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall delineate suitable GGS aquatic habitat within preconstruction field investigations sites and SCADA, transmission line, and access road construction, and maintenance sites with highly visible poly wire or other flagging approved by CDFW to demarcate it as a disturbance-free zone (see Condition of Approval 11.55).

obl-0625.title: Dewater all aquatic giant garter snake habitat between May 1 and October 1 until the biologist confirms it is no longer suitable habitat.
obl-0625.trigger: Aquatic GGS habitat to be disturbed, May 1 to October 1

locators.excerpt: All aquatic giant garter snake habitat will be dewatered between May 1 and October 1 (giant garter snake active season) to the extent that the area is no longer suitable habitat for giant garter snake as determined by the USFWS- and CDFW-approved biologist.

obl-0626.title: Completely avoid identified and delineated giant garter snake habitat, to the greatest extent feasible.
obl-0626.trigger: All work near delineated giant garter snake habitat, to the greatest extent feasible

locators.excerpt: To the greatest extent feasible, and determined by the contractor in coordination with the USFWS- and CDFW-approved biologist, identified and delineated habitat will be completely avoided.

obl-0627.title: If anyone sees a GGS or a look-alike snake retreat into a burrow, crack, crevice or riprap, stop all work within 50 feet of that spot until the biologist is called and on site.
obl-0627.trigger: Any GGS or similar snake seen retreating into refuge within a construction site

locators.excerpt: If Project personnel observe GGS, or any snake resembling GGS, retreating into an underground burrow, crack, or crevice, including rock riprap for refuge within a Project construction site, Permittee shall prohibit Covered Activities within a 50-foot radius of the refuge until the Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) is contacted and is on-site.

obl-0628.title: Do not destroy, modify or block burrows outside the direct ground-disturbance footprint, and leave burrows in temporary disturbance areas intact.
obl-0628.trigger: Outside the direct footprint and in temporary disturbance areas
monitorSigns: burrow collapsed in temporary work area

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall not destroy or modify burrows or exclude GGS from burrows that are beyond the direct footprint of ground disturbance. Burrows in an area of temporary disturbance shall remain intact.

obl-0629.title: Keep vegetation within three feet of the outside of the barrier at 4 to 6 inches using hand tools.
obl-0629.trigger: Outside edge of the exclusion barrier

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall maintain vegetation within three feet of the edge of the exclusion barrier away from the Project construction site at a height that allows visibility of CTS (four to six inches, depending on the terrain and at the discretion of the Designated Biologist(s)) near the barrier, using hand tools to trim or remove vegetation.

obl-0630.title: Drive only existing routes to reach construction sites, and do not cross GGS habitat outside the construction site unless CDFW authorizes it.
obl-0630.trigger: All Project vehicle access during Covered Activities
monitorSigns: vehicle tracks across habitat outside site

locators.excerpt: Project-related vehicles shall access the Project construction site(s) during Covered Activities using existing routes and shall not cross GGS habitat outside of the Project construction site(s) unless otherwise authorized by CDFW.

obl-0631.title: Control vegetation in suitable GGS upland habitat only by mowing.
obl-0631.trigger: Field investigation and line sites in suitable GGS upland habitat
monitorSigns: herbicide or discing in upland habitat

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall only use mowing for vegetation control within suitable GGS upland habitat.

obl-0632.title: Set up Environmentally Sensitive Areas (ESAs) in every construction site to keep construction out of GGS habitat as far as practicable.
monitorSigns: construction site with no ESAs set up

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall establish Environmentally Sensitive Areas (ESAs) in each Project construction site to minimize disturbance of GGS habitat from construction-related activities to the greatest extent practicable.

obl-0633.title: Keep stockpiles, portable equipment, vehicles and supplies away from suitable GGS habitat and ESAs.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall restrict stockpiling of construction materials including portable equipment, vehicles, and supplies away from GGS suitable habitat including any ESAs (see Condition of Approval 11.54).

obl-0634.title: Do not start Covered Activities until CDFW has approved the Phase Authorization Package showing GGS habitat and disturbance areas.
obl-0634.trigger: Before initiation of Covered Activities in each phase

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall identify suitable GGS habitat, locations of proposed surface-disturbing activities, proposed areas for ground disturbance, and habitat removal within the appropriate Phase Authorization Package (Condition of Approval 6.1 and 6.2) for CDFW review and approval prior to initiation of Covered Activities.

obl-0635.title: Do not disturb known or potentially occupied burrows unless they are in the direct ground-disturbance area or their location risks direct harm to GGS.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall avoid disturbing any known or potentially occupied burrows unless they are in an area of direct ground disturbance (e.g., grading areas, excavation areas) or their location poses a risk of direct harm to GGS.

obl-0636.title: If you see a GGS at the pump screen, shut the pump down and call the biologist to move the snake.
obl-0636.trigger: Any GGS seen at the screen during dewatering
monitorSigns: pump kept running with snake at screen
snake on screen, biologist not called

locators.excerpt: If Project personnel see GGS at the screen during dewatering, they shall shut down the pump and contact the Designated Biologist(s) to relocate the snake (see Condition of Approval 11.67).

obl-0637.title: Keep ground disturbance that could harm GGS (clearance work) to the smallest area needed.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall confine ground disturbance that could result in take of GGS (clearance work) to the most minimal area necessary to conduct Covered Activities.

obl-0638.title: Build restored nontidal marsh with still or slow-flowing water over a soil, silt, or mud substrate.

locators.excerpt: Restored nontidal marsh will consist of still or slow-flowing water over a  substrate composed of soil, silt, or mud characteristic of those observed in marshes, sloughs, or irrigation canals.

obl-0639.title: Do not create large areas of deep, perennial open water in the restored marsh.
