obl-0639.trigger: Restored GGS nontidal marsh design and construction

locators.excerpt: Restoration designs will not create large areas of deep, perennial open  water that would support nonnative predatory fish.

obl-0640.title: Place terrestrial features within 200 feet of aquatic foraging areas at all tide levels, with slopes and grading that do not expose largely denuded intertidal mud flats at low tide.
monitorSigns: refuge more than 200 feet from foraging water
bare mudflats exposed at low tide

locators.excerpt: Terrestrial features will be sited within 200 feet of aquatic foraging areas at all tide levels, with slopes and grading designed to avoid exposing largely denuded intertidal mud flats during low tide.

obl-0641.title: Leave vegetation on levees, canal sides and other upland habitat within 200 feet of suitable aquatic features wherever possible.
obl-0641.trigger: Within 200 ft of suitable aquatic features

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall leave vegetation on levees, canal sides, and other upland habitat within 200 feet of suitable aquatic features wherever possible.

obl-0642.title: Do not do field investigations or SCADA, transmission line or access road construction and maintenance in suitable GGS upland habitat from October 2 to April 30, unless CDFW approves.
obl-0642.trigger: Suitable GGS upland habitat, October 2 to April 30
monitorSigns: field investigation in upland habitat in January

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall not conduct preconstruction field investigations and SCADA, transmission line, and access road construction, and maintenance sites in suitable GGS upland habitat during the inactive season from October 2 – April 30 unless otherwise approved by CDFW.

obl-0643.title: Limit dewatering to the immediate construction area and keep it dry for at least 15 consecutive days before excavating or filling.
obl-0643.trigger: Dewatered GGS habitat, before excavation or fill

locators.excerpt: Dewatering will be limited to the immediate construction area and will remain dry for at least 15 consecutive days prior to excavating or filling the dewatered habitat.

obl-0644.title: Stop all work within at least 10 feet of a giant garter snake and notify the construction manager and approved biologist; keep activities stopped until corrective measures are done, the snake will not be harmed, or it has left.
obl-0644.trigger: Immediately when a giant garter snake is found during surveys or construction

locators.excerpt: If a giant garter snake is found in a construction or restoration area, activities within a minimum of 10 feet of the individual will cease immediately, the construction manager and the USFWS- and CDFW-approved biologist will be notified, and the USFWS- and CDFW-approved biologist will observe and follow the individual within 10 feet to ensure it has safely left the area. If a giant garter snake is encountered during surveys or construction, cease activities until appropriate corrective measures have been completed, it has been determined that the giant garter snake will not be harmed, or the giant garter snake has left the work area.

obl-0645.title: Build the fence at least 24 inches above ground with a top climber-barrier lip.

locators.excerpt: Fencing shall extend at least 24 inches above the ground and shall be constructed with a top climber barrier lip so that GGS cannot scale and go over the barrier into the Project construction site.

obl-0646.title: Grade aquatic margins to transition into grassy upland banks with a dense grassy understory, including about 200 feet of high ground above the annual high-water mark.
obl-0646.trigger: Restored GGS marsh margins and shorelines
monitorSigns: no high ground above high-water mark

locators.excerpt: Aquatic margins or shorelines will transition to uplands consisting of  grassy banks, with the dense grassy understory required for sheltering. These margins will consist of approximately 200 feet of high ground or upland habitat above the annual high-water mark to provide cover and refugia from floodwaters during the dormant winter season.

obl-0647.title: Do not catch or handle any GGS or look-alike snake; let snakes in the construction site leave on their own.
obl-0647.trigger: All Project personnel, at all times

locators.excerpt: GGS may only be captured and handled by the CDFW-approved Designated Biologist(s) (see Condition of Approval 9.2.1). GGS encountered in Project construction sites shall be allowed to leave on their own volition.

obl-0648.title: Put up the high-visibility GGS exclusion barrier before ground-disturbing work (staging, vegetation removal) and within 24 hours after preconstruction surveys and burrow excavations are done.
obl-0648.trigger: Before ground disturbance, within 24 hours after surveys and burrow excavation

locators.excerpt: Prior to initiation of ground disturbing Covered Activities (e.g., staging, vegetation removal) and within 24 hours after preconstruction surveys and burrow excavations are completed (see Conditions of Approval 11.56 and 11.62.2), Permittee shall erect a high visibility exclusion barrier to exclude GGS from entering the Project construction site.

obl-0649.title: Work in GGS habitat outside the seasonal window without a separate approval only where initial habitat-removing ground disturbance was done before September 15 and the exclusion barrier is already in place.
obl-0649.trigger: Covered Activities outside the seasonal work restriction
monitorSigns: out-of-season work in site cleared after Sept 15
no exclusion barrier at out-of-season site

locators.excerpt: Permittee may also conduct Covered Activities within suitable GGS habitat outside of the seasonal work restriction if initial ground disturbance removing suitable habitat within a construction site has been conducted prior to September 15 and the construction site already has an exclusion barrier in place (see Condition of Approval 11.62).

obl-0650.title: Restore all temporarily impacted GGS habitat to pre-Project condition or better: remove temporary fill, debris and stockpiles, regrade to the original contour (or an improved contour with CDFW approval), and revegetate with CDFW-approved native species.
obl-0650.trigger: All temporarily impacted GGS habitat after construction

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall restore all temporarily impacted GGS habitat onsite to pre- Project conditions or better by removing temporary fill, construction debris and stockpiled materials, regrading to the pre-existing contour if appropriate or a contour that would improve restoration potential of the site with CDFW consultation and approval, and revegetating upland areas or replanting emergent vegetation in active channels and on banks with CDFW approved and available native plant species (see Revegetation Plan in Condition of Approval 12.3.3).

obl-0651.title: Leave no gaps or holes in the barrier, and design it so GGS cannot climb over or burrow under, except for required vehicle and pedestrian access and one-way exit funnels.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall design the exclusion barrier to prevent GGS from climbing over it or under it through burrows or cracks. Permittee shall ensure there are no gaps or holes in the barrier except for the access areas required for vehicular and pedestrian traffic and one-way exit funnels to allow GGS to move out of the construction site but not reenter.

obl-0652.title: If work in suitable GGS aquatic habitat cannot be avoided, dewater that habitat within the construction site before the work starts.
obl-0652.trigger: Covered Activities in suitable GGS aquatic habitat
monitorSigns: work in wetted habitat without dewatering

locators.excerpt: If Permittee cannot avoid conducting Covered Activities in suitable GGS aquatic habitat, Permittee shall dewater the habitat within the Project construction site prior to starting the Covered Activity.

obl-0653.title: Run the barrier along the construction site perimeter wherever ground disturbance will occur in suitable GGS habitat.
obl-0653.trigger: Construction site perimeter within suitable GGS habitat
monitorSigns: gap in perimeter fence next to habitat

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall place the barrier along the perimeter of the Project construction site within all suitable GGS habitat where ground disturbing activities will occur to isolate activities from suitable GGS upland and aquatic habitat.

obl-0654.title: Notify the Designated Biologist immediately if a GGS or look-alike snake is found in the construction site or within three feet of it.
obl-0654.trigger: Any GGS or similar snake found in or within 3 ft of a construction site
monitorSigns: snake sighting with no call to biologist

locators.excerpt: If a GGS, or a snake resembling GGS, is found on the Project construction site or three feet beyond the construction site, the Designated Biologist(s) shall be notified immediately and shall determine whether the animal should be captured and handled.

obl-0655.title: Once the habitat is deemed free of giant garter snakes, install exclusion fencing around the construction site so no snakes can re-enter before or during construction.
obl-0655.trigger: After the biologist deems the habitat free of snakes, before construction

locators.excerpt: Once habitat is deemed free of giant garter snakes, exclusion fencing will be installed around the construction site so no snakes may reenter prior to or during construction.

obl-0656.title: Keep heavy equipment on existing access roads or outside suitable GGS upland habitat as far as practicable.
obl-0656.trigger: Upland habitat work May 1 to October 1
monitorSigns: heavy equipment off road in habitat

locators.excerpt: For Covered Activities conducted in suitable upland habitat during the active season of May 1 - October 1, Permittee shall implement the following measures to minimize disturbance to Covered Species to the greatest extent possible: • Permittee shall confine movement of heavy equipment to existing access roads or to locations outside of suitable GGS upland habitat to the extent practicable.

obl-0657.title: Grade restored tidal wetlands to provide adjacent terrestrial refuge that stays above the high-water mark.
monitorSigns: refuge areas flooded at high tide

locators.excerpt: Topography of the restored wetlands will be designed to provide adjacent terrestrial refuge persisting above the high-water mark.

obl-0658.title: Mow only with string trimmers (weed whackers) that do not crush burrows or dig into the ground.
obl-0658.trigger: All mowing in suitable GGS habitat, including upland habitat
monitorSigns: tractor mower used without CDFW approval

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall use light mowing equipment limited to string trimers (e.g., weed whackers) that will not crush burrows or impact the ground.

Permittee shall use light mowing equipment limited to string trimmers (e.g., weed whackers) that will not crush burrows or impact the ground. Any request by Permittee to use other mowing equipment shall be subject to CDFW approval (e.g., for locations away from refugia and burrow complexes).

obl-0659.title: Post and keep up ESA signs every 50 feet along the edge of suitable GGS habitat, clearly visible to Project personnel.
obl-0659.trigger: Along the edge of suitable GGS habitat at each ESA

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall also post and maintain signs identifying the ESAs every 50 feet along the edge of suitable GGS habitat and ensure signs are clearly visible and recognizable to Project personnel.

obl-0660.title: Bury the fence at least six inches and compact soil against both sides along its whole length.

locators.excerpt: Fencing shall be buried a minimum of six inches below ground and soil shall be compacted against both sides of the fence for its entire length to prevent animals from passing under the fence.

obl-0661.title: Keep vegetation within three feet on the outside of the barrier fence no taller than six inches, unless CDFW approves otherwise.
obl-0661.trigger: Outside face of the GGS exclusion fence

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall maintain vegetation within three feet on the side of the fence away from the Project construction site, unless otherwise approved by CDFW, at a maximum height of six inches to discourage GGS from using vegetation along the barrier fencing and to increase visibility of GGS near the barrier.

obl-0662.title: Grade restored marsh with varied topography giving a range of depths and emergent, herbaceous aquatic vegetation.

locators.excerpt: The restored marsh will be characterized by a heterogeneous topography providing a range of depths and vegetation profiles consisting of emergent, herbaceous aquatic vegetation that will provide suitable foraging habitat and refuge from predators.

obl-0663.title: Leave vegetation at least six inches tall.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall maintain vegetation at a minimum of six inches

obl-0664.title: Set the barrier at least 10 feet from the edge of aquatic habitat unless CDFW approves otherwise.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall install the exclusion barrier at least 10 feet from the edge of the aquatic habitat unless otherwise approved by CDFW.

obl-0665.title: Include intermittent windows, such as steel grates, in under-crossing culverts for new roads in GGS suitable habitat.
obl-0665.trigger: Under-crossings for new roads in GGS suitable habitat
monitorSigns: culvert with no windows in GGS habitat

locators.excerpt: Culvert under-crossing tunnels shall use “windows” for new roads within GGS suitable habitat as diurnal snakes are less likely to utilize culvert crossings that mimic burrows. Windows may be made of steel grates or other materials and shall be intermittent in placement.

obl-0666.title: Do not use plastic monofilament netting in the barrier.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall not use plastic monofilament netting for the exclusion barrier (see Condition of Approval 11.28).

obl-0667.title: Remove logs, brush piles, and woody debris carefully, and only after the Designated Biologist has inspected them and while the biologist supervises.
obl-0667.trigger: Removal of potential overwintering refugia during the overwintering period
monitorSigns: no biologist on site during removal

locators.excerpt: During this time, removal of fallen logs, brush piles, woody debris, and other potential refugia for overwintering bees shall be done carefully with prior inspection and then supervision from the Designated Biologist(s) with assistance (if needed) from the Biological Monitor(s).

obl-0668.title: Install exclusion fencing along the construction site perimeter, placed based on suitable habitat locations, no more than 14 days before construction starts in that area (staging, vegetation removal, grading).
obl-0668.trigger: Sites with GGS habitat within 200 feet (except open water work sites), no more than 14 days before construction
monitorSigns: fence up more than 14 days early

locators.excerpt: When there is giant garter snake habitat within 200 feet of construction activities, exclusion fencing will be installed along the perimeter of construction sites to protect giant garter snake habitat and minimize the potential for snakes to enter the construction work area. The perimeter of construction sites (except for work sites within areas of open water, like the Sacramento River) within or adjacent to giant garter snake habitat will be fenced with exclusion fencing by no more than 14 days prior to the start of construction activities (e.g., staging, vegetation removal, grading) in a given area. The placement of exclusion fencing will be determined, in part, by the locations of suitable habitat for the species.

obl-0669.title: Do fill, vegetation removal and other ground disturbance within suitable GGS aquatic and upland habitat (within 200 ft of aquatic habitat) only between May 1 and October 1, unless CDFW approves otherwise under COA 11.59.
obl-0669.trigger: Preconstruction, construction and maintenance work in suitable GGS habitat
monitorSigns: grading in GGS habitat in March
fill placed in November with no CDFW approval

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall confine all fill, vegetation removal, and other ground disturbing Covered Activities during preconstruction and construction activities or Project maintenance areas within suitable GGS aquatic and upland habitat (areas within 200 feet of aquatic habitat) to the GGS active period between May 1 and October 1 unless otherwise approved by CDFW per Condition of Approval 11.59.

obl-0670.title: Use taut wildlife exclusion fencing with stakes on the Project side only.

locators.excerpt: Fencing shall consist of taut wildlife exclusion fencing supported by stakes on the Project side only as snakes may be able to climb over the fencing via stakes.

obl-0671.title: Do not do these activities in suitable GGS aquatic habitat.
obl-0671.trigger: Field investigation, SCADA, transmission line and access road work

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall not conduct these Covered Activities in suitable GGS aquatic habitat.

obl-0672.title: Put up ESA fencing around suitable GGS habitat where the biologist directs.
obl-0672.trigger: Suitable GGS habitat in each construction site, as directed by the Designated Biologist
monitorSigns: ESA fence missing where biologist flagged habitat

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall erect ESA fencing around suitable GGS habitat as directed by the Designated Biologist(s).

obl-0673.title: Do not work in suitable GGS habitat before May 1 unless CDFW has given written approval, and then follow any extra measures CDFW requires.
obl-0673.trigger: Covered Activities in suitable GGS habitat during the inactive season before May 1
monitorSigns: GGS habitat work in April with no CDFW approval

locators.excerpt: Permittee may conduct Covered Activities within suitable GGS habitat prior to May 1 during the GGS inactive season only after consultation with and obtaining written approval from CDFW, which approval may require additional measures to minimize and/or avoid potential impacts to GGS during activities prior to May 1.

obl-0674.title: Haul dredged or excavated material off site, or place it only where there are no rodent burrows, riprap or other winter cover for GGS.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall haul any dredged or excavated material off site or place it in areas lacking rodent burrows, riprap, or other materials that might provide dormant period cover for GGS.

obl-0675.title: Where GGS may be overwintering within 200 feet, limit in-channel work to sediment removal, acoustic monitoring and aquatic vegetation removal until the biologist confirms no overwintering GGS.
obl-0675.trigger: Canals or other areas where GGS may overwinter within 200 ft, before absence is confirmed
monitorSigns: bank grading in canal before overwintering survey

locators.excerpt: In-channel work shall be limited to removal of accumulated sediments, acoustic monitoring, and aquatic vegetation removal in canals or other areas where GGS may be overwintering within 200 feet of the activity, until CDFW-approved surveys (Condition of Approval 11.38) have occurred and absence of overwintering GGS has been confirmed by the Designated Biologist(s).

obl-0676.title: Do not do in-channel work during the GGS active season unless CDFW has approved it in writing.
obl-0676.trigger: In-channel work during the GGS active season
monitorSigns: in-channel work in July with no written approval

locators.excerpt: If in-channel work needs to occur within the GGS active season, Permittee shall request written approval by CDFW and have the Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) survey following CDFW-approved protocols (Condition of Approval 11.38) for GGS prior to initiating work and monitor throughout the duration of Covered Activities for GGS.

obl-0677.title: Install one-way exit funnels flush to the ground every 150 feet.

locators.excerpt: The fence shall include multiple one-way exit funnels flush to the ground every 150 feet to allow GGS and other species to leave the Project construction site.

obl-0678.title: Call the Designated Biologist or Biological Monitor when a GGS or look-alike is seen retreating into refuge.
monitorSigns: snake sighting logged, biologist not called

locators.excerpt: If Project personnel observe GGS, or any snake resembling GGS, retreating into an underground burrow, crack, or crevice, including rock riprap for refuge within a Project construction site, Permittee shall prohibit Covered Activities within a 50-foot radius of the refuge until the Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) is contacted and is on-site.

obl-0679.title: Make the upland habitat sunny, with low vegetation and bankside burrows, holes, and crevices for shelter.

locators.excerpt: The upland habitat will have ample exposure to sunlight to facilitate giant  garter snake thermoregulation and will be characterized by low vegetation, bankside burrows, holes, and crevices providing critical shelter for snakes throughout the day.

obl-0680.title: Do not restart work after a qualifying lapse (14+ days Oct 2 to Apr 30, over 12 hours May 1 to Oct 1) until the re-survey is done.
obl-0680.trigger: Restarting Covered Activities after a lapse

locators.excerpt: The survey shall be repeated prior to reinitiating Covered Activities if a lapse in Covered Activities of 14 calendar days or greater occurs at the Project construction site during the aestivation period (October 2 to April 30) or if the lapse in Covered Activities is more than 12 hours during the active season (May 1 to October 1).

obl-0681.title: Do not start any Covered Activities in the GGS active season until the preconstruction survey of the site and buffer is done.
obl-0681.trigger: May 1 to Oct 1, before any Covered Activities at a site

locators.excerpt: The Designated Biologist(s) with assistance (if needed) from the Biological Monitor(s) shall conduct CDFW approved preconstruction surveys (Condition of Approval 11.38) within the boundaries of each Project site and include a three-foot buffer zone around the Project site, prior to initiation of any Covered Activities, including preconstruction activities, during the GGS active season (May 1 to October 1).

obl-0682.title: Follow the Guidelines for the Restoration and/or Replacement of Giant Garter Snake Habitat in the restoration.
monitorSigns: restoration method departs from GGS guidelines

locators.excerpt: The restoration effort shall comply with the Guidelines for the Restoration and/or Replacement of Giant Garter Snake Habitat.

obl-0683.title: Mark suitable GGS upland habitat with flagging or other highly visible markers within these work sites.

locators.excerpt: The Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall delineate suitable upland habitat with flagging or other high-visible markers within the Covered Activity sites.

obl-0684.title: Only the biologists named in the approved relocation plan may relocate giant garter snakes.
monitorSigns: snake moved by biologist not named in plan

locators.excerpt: The relocation plan will contain the name(s) of the biologist(s) to relocate giant garter snakes, the method of relocation (if different than described), a map, and a description of the proposed release site(s) within 300 feet of the work area or at a distance otherwise agreed to by USFWS and CDFW, and written permission from the landowner to use their land as a relocation site.

obl-0685.title: Find and flag every potential burrow in the construction site that can be avoided.

locators.excerpt: The Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall identify and flag all potential burrows within the Project construction site that can be avoided.

obl-0686.title: Repeat GGS surveys every year that Covered Activities will occur in or within three feet of GGS habitat.
obl-0686.trigger: Each year with Covered Activities in or within 3 ft of GGS habitat
monitorSigns: no survey this year in GGS habitat

locators.excerpt: Subsequent survey efforts conducted after submittal of the Construction Phased Authorization Package, shall occur each year Covered Activities are expected to occur in GGS habitat or within three feet of the habitat, or as otherwise approved by CDFW, and shall be reported to CDFW by the Permittee within the Monthly Compliance Reporting (Condition of Approval 10.12) and summarized within each Annual Status Report (Condition of Approval 10.13).
Survey efforts shall occur each year Covered Activities are expected to occur in GGS habitat or within three feet of GGS habitat.

obl-0687.title: If a GGS is seen, follow the GGS Relocation Plan.
obl-0687.trigger: Any GGS observed during the post-dewatering survey
monitorSigns: GGS handled not per Relocation Plan

locators.excerpt: If GGS is observed, the Designated Biologist(s) shall follow the GGS Relocation Plan (Condition of Approval 11.67).

obl-0688.title: After dewatering, survey all suitable GGS aquatic and upland habitat in the potential impact areas of the construction site outside the ESAs.

locators.excerpt: Following dewatering of aquatic habitat, the Designated Biologist(s) shall survey for GGS in all suitable GGS aquatic or upland habitat within the Project construction site that is not within the established ESAs.
Following dewatering of aquatic habitat, all potential impact areas that provide suitable aquatic or upland giant garter snake habitat will be surveyed for giant garter snake by the biologist.

obl-0689.title: Carefully excavate unavoidable burrows, by hand and to the end of each burrow, before any trenching, and relocate any GGS that will not leave on its own per COA 11.67.
obl-0689.trigger: Burrows that cannot be avoided, before trenching

locators.excerpt: Where the Permittee cannot avoid burrows (e.g., within footprint of ground disturbing activities), they shall be carefully excavated prior to any trenching activities and any GGS found during excavation that does not leave of its own volition shall be relocated according to Condition of Approval 11.67. Burrows shall be excavated to the terminus of each burrow.

obl-0690.title: Search along exclusion fences, in pipes, and beneath vehicles before vehicles are moved.
obl-0690.trigger: During construction in giant garter snake areas, before vehicles move

locators.excerpt: The biologist will search along exclusionary fences, in pipes, and beneath vehicles before the vehicles are moved.

obl-0691.title: Expose and identify snakes found in burrows, and relocate any that do not move out of harm's way per the GGS Relocation Plan.
obl-0691.trigger: Any snake found in a burrow during investigation
monitorSigns: snake left in burrow in footprint

locators.excerpt: The Designated Biologist(s) shall attempt to expose and identify any snakes found in burrows and relocate any individuals who do not move out of harm’s way on their own in accordance with the GGS Relocation Plan (Condition of Approval 11.67).

obl-0692.title: Watch burrows that have not been blocked or excavated for emerging GGS.
monitorSigns: open burrow in work area not watched

locators.excerpt: The Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall monitor burrows that have not been blocked or excavated for emerging GGS.

obl-0693.title: Conduct CDFW-approved GGS preconstruction surveys within each Project site plus a three-foot buffer before any Covered Activities, including preconstruction activities, in the active season.
obl-0693.trigger: Before any Covered Activities during the GGS active season (May 1 to Oct 1)
monitorSigns: work started with no preconstruction survey

locators.excerpt: The Designated Biologist(s) with assistance (if needed) from the Biological Monitor(s) shall conduct CDFW approved preconstruction surveys (Condition of Approval 11.38) within the boundaries of each Project site and include a three-foot buffer zone around the Project site, prior to initiation of any Covered Activities, including preconstruction activities, during the GGS active season (May 1 to October 1).

obl-0694.title: A Designated Biologist approved by USFWS and CDFW must be on site for all dewatering, especially when it begins and when the water drops to the intake, to salvage and relocate any GGS that cannot escape the suction.
monitorSigns: dewatering with no biologist on site
biologist absent when water reached intake

locators.excerpt: The Designated Biologist(s) shall be on site during all dewatering activities, particularly when dewatering begins and when the level of water reaches the level of the intake, to salvage and relocate any GGS that cannot swim away from the suction cups and escape on its own.
The USFWS- and CDFW-approved biologist will be on-site during dewatering activities to salvage and relocate any snake that cannot escape on its own.

obl-0695.title: Remove blocking objects as soon as work at the site is done and resumed use will not harm GGS.
obl-0695.trigger: After Covered Activities finish at each work site
monitorSigns: blocking objects left after work done

locators.excerpt: The Designated Biologist(s) shall remove the object immediately after Covered Activities are completed in that work site when they have determined that potential resumed use of the burrow will not result in harm to GGS.

The Designated Biologist(s) shall remove the object immediately after Covered Activities are completed in that work site when they have determined that potential resumed use of the burrow will not result in harm to GGS.

obl-0696.title: Perform a clearance survey to confirm GGS absence before mowing in suitable GGS habitat.
obl-0696.trigger: Before any mowing in suitable GGS habitat
monitorSigns: no clearance survey logged before mowing

locators.excerpt: If Covered Activities require the removal or maintenance of vegetation, Permittee shall limit mowing to occur only between July 1 to September 30 in suitable GGS habitat and after a Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) has performed clearance surveys to ensure absence of GGS.

obl-0697.title: Conduct 2 days of walking clearance surveys within each construction site and a 3-foot band around the exclusion fencing, starting no more than 7 days before ground disturbance, where access allows.
obl-0697.trigger: Active season (May 1 to October 1), within 7 days before ground disturbance

locators.excerpt: Beginning no more than 7 days prior to initiating ground-disturbing activities during the active season (May 1 to October 1), the biologist will conduct 2 days of walking clearance surveys within each construction site and a 3-foot boundary surrounding the exclusion fencing, where access allows.

obl-0698.title: Walk in front of the mower watching for GGS coming out of vegetation or burrows.

locators.excerpt: The Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall walk in front of the mower and monitor for GGS emerging from the vegetation or burrows.

obl-0699.title: Relocate a GGS only if it is directly threatened by imminent work and cannot reach safety on its own, release it as soon as possible, and only to areas named in the Relocation Plan.
monitorSigns: GGS relocated that was not threatened
release site not in Relocation Plan

locators.excerpt: The Designated Biologist(s) shall only relocate GGS if the animal is directly threatened by immediate Covered Activities and the animal is unable to move to a safe area on its own. Relocated GGS shall be released as soon as possible. The Designated Biologist(s) shall only relocate GGS to areas identified in the Relocation Plan.

obl-0700.title: Re-survey before work restarts after a lapse of 14 days or more in the aestivation period (October 2 to April 30) or more than 12 hours in the active season (May 1 to October 1).
obl-0700.trigger: After a lapse in Covered Activities at a construction site, including unfenced areas
monitorSigns: work resumed after lapse with no re-survey
work resumed after lapse without re-survey

locators.excerpt: The survey shall be repeated prior to reinitiating Covered Activities if a lapse in Covered Activities of 14 calendar days or greater occurs at the Project construction site during the aestivation period (October 2 to April 30) or if the lapse in Covered Activities is more than 12 hours during the active season (May 1 to October 1).

This survey of the work area will be repeated if a lapse in construction or dredging activity of 2 weeks or greater occurs during the aestivation period (October 1 to May 1) or if the lapse in construction activity is more than 12 hours during active season (May 1 to October 1).

obl-0701.title: Only a USFWS- and CDFW-approved biological monitor may guide work around giant garter snake habitat.

locators.excerpt: The USFWS- and CDFW-approved biological monitor will help guide access and construction work around wetlands, active rice fields, and other sensitive habitats capable of supporting giant garter snake to minimize habitat disturbance and risk of injuring or killing giant garter snakes.

obl-0702.title: Do not release a GGS taken into captivity unless it has been quarantined and CDFW and USFWS have authorized release.
monitorSigns: captive GGS released without quarantine or authorization

locators.excerpt: If taken into captivity, the individual shall remain in captivity and shall not be released into the wild unless it has been kept in quarantine and the release is authorized by CDFW and USFWS.

obl-0703.title: Immediately bag, label and freeze a recently dead GGS, with time and date, GPS location, circumstances of death if known, and ITP tracking number on the label.
obl-0703.trigger: A GGS found recently dead (no odor or decomposition)
monitorSigns: label missing GPS or ITP number

locators.excerpt: If the GGS is found recently deceased (as evidenced by lack of odor or decomposition), the carcass shall be immediately bagged, labeled, and preserved in a freezer. The label shall include time and date, GPS location, circumstances surrounding death (if known), and ITP tracking number.

obl-0704.title: Delineate giant garter snake aquatic and upland habitat at each project site.
obl-0704.trigger: At each project site, once available for surveys

locators.excerpt: When each site is available for surveys, a USFWS- and CDFW-approved biologist will then delineate giant garter snake habitat at each project site, including both aquatic and upland habitat.

obl-0705.title: Monitor GGS habitat restoration for one year, or until the biologist and CDFW find restoration successful.
obl-0705.trigger: After restoration of temporarily disturbed GGS habitat

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall monitor the restoration for one year or until restoration success is achieved as determined by the Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) and CDFW.

obl-0706.title: Begin the first GGS survey of a construction site, following CDFW-approved protocols, no more than seven days before ground-disturbing work starts there (including soil deposition, preconstruction, SCADA, transmission line, access road and exclusion barrier sites).
obl-0706.trigger: After Construction Phase Authorization Package approval, within 7 days before ground disturbance
monitorSigns: survey more than 7 days before ground disturbance

locators.excerpt: The first Project construction site GGS survey following approval of the appropriate Construction Phase Authorization Package (i.e., after a baseline preconstruction survey(s) has been completed) shall begin no more than seven days prior to initiating ground disturbing Covered Activities and be conducted consistent with CDFW-approved protocols (Condition of Approval 11.38). Ground disturbing activities include soil deposition areas, preconstruction activities, and SCADA, transmission line, or access road construction, maintenance, or improvement sites, and exclusion barrier installation and maintenance.

obl-0707.title: Flag any burrow a GGS or look-alike snake is seen entering or leaving for the no-activity buffer.
obl-0707.trigger: When a GGS or similar snake is seen at a burrow

locators.excerpt: • If GGS, or any snake resembling GGS, is detected retreating into or exiting a burrow, the Designated Biologist(s) shall flag the burrow to be avoided by the no-activity buffer.

obl-0708.title: Observe and follow the snake within 10 feet until it has safely left, setting a larger buffer where heavy equipment or other activities could harm it.
obl-0708.trigger: When a giant garter snake is found in a construction or restoration area
monitorSigns: no larger buffer near heavy equipment

locators.excerpt: If a giant garter snake is found in a construction or restoration area, activities within a minimum of 10 feet of the individual will cease immediately, the construction manager and the USFWS- and CDFW-approved biologist will be notified, and the USFWS- and CDFW-approved biologist will observe and follow the individual within 10 feet to ensure it has safely left the area. A larger protective buffer may be established, depending on site-specific conditions such as the use of heavy equipment, or other activities that may cause harm to the individual, as determined by the USFWS- and CDFW-approved biologist.

obl-0709.title: Determine aquatic and upland habitat suitability using the Appendix 13B, Section 13B.55 definition.
obl-0709.trigger: When determining suitable habitat for giant garter snake

locators.excerpt: Suitability of aquatic and upland habitat characteristics will be determined by the biologist consistent with the description of suitable habitat defined in Appendix 13B, Section 13B.55.

obl-0710.title: After the snake has left, inspect and collapse all burrows within 200 feet of aquatic habitat; collapse burrows on levees only after approval from the relevant agency (e.g., USACE, Reclamation).
obl-0710.trigger: After a giant garter snake has moved out of the work area

locators.excerpt: After the giant garter snake has moved out of the work area, all burrows within 200 feet of aquatic habitat will be inspected and collapsed; burrow collapse on levees will only be conducted following approval from relevant regulatory agencies (e.g., USACE, Reclamation).

obl-0711.title: Monitor for GGS throughout active-season in-channel work.
obl-0711.trigger: Duration of active-season in-channel Covered Activities

locators.excerpt: If in-channel work needs to occur within the GGS active season, Permittee shall request written approval by CDFW and have the Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) survey following CDFW-approved protocols (Condition of Approval 11.38) for GGS prior to initiating work and monitor throughout the duration of Covered Activities for GGS.

obl-0712.title: Only a USFWS- and CDFW-approved biologist may conduct giant garter snake surveys, buffers and relocations.
obl-0712.trigger: All giant garter snake survey and handling work

locators.excerpt: Immediately prior to the initiation of any vegetation clearing, ground-disturbing activities, and exclusion fence installation, the USFWS- and CDFW-approved biologist will conduct clearance surveys of suitable aquatic and upland habitat in the entire work site for the presence of giant garter snakes. If a giant garter snake is found in a construction or restoration area, activities within a minimum of 10 feet of the individual will cease immediately, the construction manager and the USFWS- and CDFW-approved biologist will be notified, and the USFWS- and CDFW-approved biologist will observe and follow the individual within 10 feet to ensure it has safely left the area. If the snake does not move and it is deemed necessary to relocate the animal to prevent harm, as determined by the USFWS- and CDFW-approved biologist in coordination with the construction manager, the snake may be captured and relocated to suitable habitat a minimum of 200 feet outside of the work area in accordance with the relocation plan, prior to resumption of construction activity.

obl-0713.title: Let observed snakes leave the impact area on their own; relocate a snake per the approved relocation plan only if it does not move and relocation is necessary.
obl-0713.trigger: When giant garter snakes are observed after dewatering

locators.excerpt: If giant garter snakes are observed, they will be passively allowed to leave the potential impact area. If the snake does not move of its own accord and it is determined necessary, the snake will be relocated in accordance with the approved relocation plan.

obl-0714.title: Identify and mark all GGS habitat that can reasonably be avoided as ESAs.

monitorSigns: avoidable habitat not marked as ESA

locators.excerpt: In addition, all potential GGS habitat that can be reasonably avoided during construction activities shall be identified as ESAs and shall be marked by the Designated Biologist(s) and/or the Biological Monitor(s).

obl-0715.title: Investigate every burrow in suitable upland habitat outside ESAs, within the construction site and its three-foot boundary, using the CDFW-approved method to tell whether GGS occupy it.
obl-0715.trigger: Construction site and three-foot boundary, suitable upland habitat outside ESAs
monitorSigns: investigation method not per approved protocol

locators.excerpt: Within the Project construction site and three-foot boundary, the Designated Biologist(s) with assistance (if needed) from the Biological Monitor(s) shall investigate all burrows within suitable upland habitat outside of established ESAs using a CDFW-approved methodology (see Condition of Approval 11.62.2) to determine whether the burrows are occupied by GGS.

obl-0716.title: Guide Project access and construction work around ESAs and other sensitive habitat that can support GGS, such as wetlands and active rice fields.
obl-0716.trigger: During Project access and construction near ESAs and sensitive GGS habitat
monitorSigns: route through rice field not reviewed

locators.excerpt: The Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall help guide Project access and construction work around ESAs (e.g., wetlands, active rice fields, and other sensitive habitats capable of supporting GGS) to minimize habitat disturbance and risk of take of GGS.

The USFWS- and CDFW-approved biological monitor will help guide access and construction work around wetlands, active rice fields, and other sensitive habitats capable of supporting giant garter snake to minimize habitat disturbance and risk of injuring or killing giant garter snakes.

obl-0717.title: Confirm burrow vacancy and try to expose and identify any snakes, then block unoccupied burrows only with an object CDFW approved in advance in writing.
obl-0717.trigger: Burrows in the work area during Covered Activities

locators.excerpt: If burrows cannot be avoided by a no-activity buffer and are within suitable upland habitat, Permittee shall monitor to determine vacancy and block burrows for the duration of Covered Activities.

The Designated Biologist shall first monitor to determine vacancy and attempt to expose and identify any snakes found in burrows, then block the entrance of unoccupied burrows (e.g., less than three feet long with dead ends) by installing an object approved in advance in writing by CDFW, to prevent Covered Species from entering and using the burrow during Covered Activities.

obl-0718.title: Conduct CDFW-approved surveys to confirm whether GGS are overwintering near in-channel work.
obl-0718.trigger: Before in-channel work beyond the limited activities, within 200 ft of potential overwintering areas
monitorSigns: no overwintering survey before expanded work

locators.excerpt: In-channel work shall be limited to removal of accumulated sediments, acoustic monitoring, and aquatic vegetation removal in canals or other areas where GGS may be overwintering within 200 feet of the activity, until CDFW-approved surveys (Condition of Approval 11.38) have occurred and absence of overwintering GGS has been confirmed by the Designated Biologist(s).

obl-0719.title: Inspect the area before and during GGS barrier installation, including trenching, vehicle access, fencing, staking and any foot or vehicle traffic in suitable habitat.
obl-0719.trigger: Before and during exclusion barrier installation
monitorSigns: fence trenching with no biologist present

locators.excerpt: The Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall inspect the area prior to and during installation, including trenching, vehicular access, erecting fencing material, installing stakes, and any other activity requiring vehicle or foot traffic in suitable habitat.

obl-0720.title: Let the snake move on its own; if relocation is needed, capture and relocate it to suitable habitat at least 200 feet outside the work area per the relocation plan, before construction resumes.
obl-0720.trigger: When the snake does not move and relocation is determined necessary

locators.excerpt: The snake will be allowed to move of its own volition out of harm’s way. If the snake does not move and it is deemed necessary to relocate the animal to prevent harm, as determined by the USFWS- and CDFW-approved biologist in coordination with the construction manager, the snake may be captured and relocated to suitable habitat a minimum of 200 feet outside of the work area in accordance with the relocation plan, prior to resumption of construction activity.

obl-0721.title: Only the CDFW-approved Designated Biologist may capture and handle GGS.

locators.excerpt: GGS may only be captured and handled by the CDFW-approved Designated Biologist(s) (see Condition of Approval 9.2.1).

obl-0722.title: Immediately take an injured GGS to the CDFW-approved rehabilitation or veterinary facility named in the GGS Relocation Plan.
monitorSigns: taken to facility not in Relocation Plan

locators.excerpt: The Designated Biologist(s) shall immediately take the GGS to a CDFW-approved wildlife rehabilitation or veterinary facility identified in the GGS Relocation Plan (see Condition of Approval 11.67)

obl-0723.title: Immediately take any GGS with major or serious Project-caused injuries to the nearest CDFW-approved rehabilitation or veterinary facility.
obl-0723.trigger: When a GGS has major or serious injuries from Project activities
monitorSigns: seriously injured GGS held on site

locators.excerpt: If it is determined that the GGS individual has major or serious injuries as a result of Project-related activities, the Designated Biologist(s) shall immediately take it to the nearest CDFW-approved wildlife rehabilitation or veterinary facility.

obl-0724.title: Conduct giant garter snake preconstruction surveys to established GGS survey protocols.
obl-0724.trigger: Sites where GGS preconstruction surveys are performed

locators.excerpt: For sites where such preconstruction surveys are performed, the surveys will conform to established protocols for giant garter snake surveys and all occurrence data gathered will be reported to the CNDDB and USFWS to add to the understanding of populations and occurrences for the species in the Delta.

obl-0725.title: Survey for GGS following CDFW-approved protocols before active-season in-channel work begins.

locators.excerpt: If in-channel work needs to occur within the GGS active season, Permittee shall request written approval by CDFW and have the Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) survey following CDFW-approved protocols (Condition of Approval 11.38) for GGS prior to initiating work and monitor throughout the duration of Covered Activities for GGS.

obl-0726.title: Decide whether a GGS needs capture, and keep capture and handling to a minimum.
monitorSigns: GGS captured that could have left on its own

locators.excerpt: If a GGS, or a snake resembling GGS, is found on the Project construction site or three feet beyond the construction site, the Designated Biologist(s) shall be notified immediately and shall determine whether the animal should be captured and handled. The Designated Biologist(s) shall minimize capture and handling to the greatest extent feasible as most reptiles experience stress in response to capture and short-term confinement.

obl-0727.title: If the biologist judges a GGS injury minor or healing and the snake likely to survive, release it immediately as the GGS Relocation Plan directs.
obl-0727.trigger: An injured GGS judged likely to survive
monitorSigns: minor-injury GGS held instead of released

locators.excerpt: If the injury is minor or healing and the snake is likely to survive as determined by the Designated Biologist(s), the snake shall be released immediately in accordance with the GGS Relocation Plan (Condition of Approval 11.67).

obl-0728.title: Salvage and relocate any snake that cannot escape on its own during dewatering.

locators.excerpt: The USFWS- and CDFW-approved biologist will be on-site during dewatering activities to salvage and relocate any snake that cannot escape on its own.

obl-0729.title: Only a USFWS- and CDFW-approved biologist may delineate giant garter snake habitat.

locators.excerpt: When each site is available for surveys, a USFWS- and CDFW-approved biologist will then delineate giant garter snake habitat at each project site, including both aquatic and upland habitat.

obl-0730.title: Survey the exclusion fence and the area inside it immediately before work in delineated habitat when the fencing is found compromised.
obl-0730.trigger: When exclusion fencing is compromised, before work in delineated habitat or any activity that may cause take
monitorSigns: fence breach, no interior survey before work

locators.excerpt: If exclusionary fencing is found to be compromised, a survey of the exclusion fencing and the area inside the fencing will be conducted immediately preceding construction activity that occurs in delineated giant garter snake habitat or in advance of any activity that may result in take of the species.

obl-0731.title: Conduct a clearance survey of all activity areas not protected by exclusion fencing where giant garter snake could be present within 24 hours before construction or dredging with heavy equipment.
obl-0731.trigger: Within 24 hours before heavy-equipment construction or dredging in unfenced areas

locators.excerpt: Within 24 hours prior to construction activities, and dredging, requiring heavy equipment, a USFWS- and CDFW-approved biologist will conduct a preconstruction clearance survey of all the activity area not protected by exclusionary fencing where giant garter snake could be present.

obl-0732.title: Only the Designated Biologist may excavate potential refuge features (burrows, soil cracks, crevices, rocks, rock piles), by hand.
obl-0732.trigger: All excavation of potential GGS refuge features

locators.excerpt: All excavation of potential refuge features, including identified burrows, soil cracks, crevices, individual rocks and rock piles, and other accessible features for GGS, shall be carried out by hand by the Designated Biologist(s).

obl-0733.title: Be present during siting of preconstruction, construction and maintenance sites, ingress and egress, and set-up to guide workers around burrows, cracks and other habitat features until avoidance routes are set.

locators.excerpt: The Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall be present during selection of the preconstruction activity sites, construction sites, and maintenance areas, ingress and egress to these sites, and during set-up activities to guide workers to avoid visible burrows, cracks, crevices, vegetation, or other suitable habitat features until avoidance routes are clearly established.

obl-0734.title: When requesting early-season GGS work, submit the request in writing to CDFW with a justification, NWS evidence that daytime temperatures held between 45°F (±5°F) and 65°F (±3°F) for two weeks, and any other information CDFW requires, 48 hours before construction.
obl-0734.trigger: Each request to work in GGS habitat outside the seasonal window
monitorSigns: request sent without NWS temperature record
evidence sent less than 48 hours before work

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall provide evidence from the National Weather Service that ambient daytime temperature has remained within a minimum range of 45°F (±5°F) and 65°F (±3°F) for two weeks. Permittee shall provide evidence of consistent warm weather to CDFW for approval 48 hours preceding construction activities. Permittee shall submit these requests in writing for review and approval by CDFW. Requests shall include a justification for the request and any additional information CDFW determines necessary.

obl-0735.title: Keep restored nontidal marsh supplied with enough water through the GGS active season (May 1–October 1) for constant cover and food.
monitorSigns: water levels dropped during active season

locators.excerpt: Restored nontidal marsh will be characterized by sufficient water during  the giant garter snake’s active summer season (May 1–October 1) to supply constant, reliable cover and sources of food such as small fish and amphibians.

obl-0736.title: Include each GGS incident report in the Monthly Compliance Report.
obl-0736.trigger: Monthly Compliance Report following a GGS incident
monitorSigns: GGS incident report missing from Monthly Compliance Report

locators.excerpt: The report shall also be included in the Monthly Compliance Report (see Condition of Approval 10.12).

obl-0737.title: Site and keep all protected and restored GGS upland and aquatic habitat at least 2,500 feet from urban areas or areas zoned for urban development.
obl-0737.trigger: Siting and protection of all GGS mitigation, protected and restored habitat
monitorSigns: site within 2,500 feet of urban zoning

locators.excerpt: Protected and restored giant garter snake habitat will be at least 2,500 feet  from urban areas or areas zoned for urban development.
All giant garter snake upland and aquatic habitat will be established at least 2,500 feet from urban areas or areas zoned for urban development.

obl-0738.title: Establish 200-foot buffers between protected GGS habitat and roads, other than roads mainly serving adjacent cultivated land and levees.
obl-0738.trigger: All protected and restored GGS habitat
monitorSigns: public road within 200 feet of protected habitat

locators.excerpt: Incidental injury or mortality of giant garter snakes within protected and  restored habitat will be avoided and minimized by establishing 200-foot buffers between protected giant garter snake habitat and roads (other than those roads primarily used to support adjacent cultivated lands and levees).

obl-0739.title: Block burrows only with an object CDFW has approved in writing in advance.
monitorSigns: blocking object used with no CDFW approval on file

locators.excerpt: Burrows in an area of temporary disturbance shall remain intact and the Designated Biologist(s) shall monitor to determine vacancy, then block the entrance by installing an object approved in advance, in writing by CDFW, to prevent CTS from entering and using the burrow during Covered Activities.

obl-0740.title: For in-kind GGS mitigation sites, provide aquatic and upland habitat of equal or greater quality, character, and location value than the habitat lost.
monitorSigns: mitigation habitat lower quality than habitat lost

locators.excerpt: For in-kind mitigation sites, the aquatic and upland habitat quality, character,  and location must be of equal or greater value than the habitat quality that was lost.

obl-0741.title: Consult CDFW on how to dispose of any GGS specimen.
obl-0741.trigger: Whenever a dead GGS specimen is held
monitorSigns: GGS carcass discarded, no CDFW consult on record

locators.excerpt: CDFW shall be consulted regarding specimen disposal.

obl-0742.title: Place and protect GGS upland mitigation adjacent to protected GGS aquatic habitat.
monitorSigns: upland not adjacent to protected aquatic habitat

locators.excerpt: Giant garter snake upland mitigation will be placed and protected adjacent to  aquatic habitat protected for giant garter snake.

obl-0743.title: Pay all costs of care or treatment for any injured GGS, including seriously injured GGS.
obl-0743.trigger: Any injured GGS taken for care or treatment

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall bear any costs associated with the care or treatment of such injured GGS.
Permittee shall bear any costs associated with the care or treatment of such injured GGS.

obl-0744.title: Use tidal habitat restoration to mitigate GGS tidal aquatic habitat loss only with a design USFWS and CDFW agree provides equal or greater habitat value.
obl-0744.trigger: When tidal restoration is chosen to mitigate GGS tidal aquatic habitat loss
monitorSigns: tidal design built without USFWS/CDFW agreement

locators.excerpt: The loss of tidal aquatic habitat for giant garter snake may be mitigated  through restoration of tidal habitat with a design that provides equal or greater habitat value for the species as agreed upon by USFWS and CDFW.

obl-0745.title: Where delineated giant garter snake habitat cannot be avoided, compensate for its loss with in-kind aquatic and upland habitat.
obl-0745.trigger: Unavoidable loss of delineated GGS habitat

locators.excerpt: Where identified and delineated giant garter snake habitat cannot be avoided, compensation for the loss of the habitat will occur for aquatic and upland habitat, with in-kind habitat type compensation.

obl-0746.title: Report subsequent GGS survey results in the Monthly Compliance Report and summarize them in each Annual Status Report.

monitorSigns: GGS survey missing from monthly report
Annual Status Report lacks GGS survey summary

locators.excerpt: Subsequent survey efforts conducted after submittal of the Construction Phased Authorization Package, shall occur each year Covered Activities are expected to occur in GGS habitat or within three feet of the habitat, or as otherwise approved by CDFW, and shall be reported to CDFW by the Permittee within the Monthly Compliance Reporting (Condition of Approval 10.12) and summarized within each Annual Status Report (Condition of Approval 10.13).

obl-0747.title: Include each written GGS relocation incident report in the Monthly Compliance Report.
obl-0747.trigger: Monthly Compliance Report following a GGS relocation
monitorSigns: relocation report missing from Monthly Compliance Report

locators.excerpt: The written incident report shall also be included in the Monthly Compliance Report (see Condition of Approval 10.12).

obl-0748.title: Make sure alternative aquatic habitat remains available when dewatering GGS habitat.
obl-0748.trigger: Before and during dewatering of GGS aquatic habitat
monitorSigns: no alternative water nearby during dewatering

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall limit dewatering to the immediate Project construction site and shall ensure that alternative aquatic habitat is available.

obl-0749.title: Keep GGS upland habitat within 200 feet of protected aquatic habitat unless USFWS and CDFW agree a larger distance is appropriate.
monitorSigns: upland more than 200 feet from water, no agency agreement

locators.excerpt: The upland habitat will not exceed 200 feet from protected aquatic habitat (unless research shows a larger distance is appropriate and USFWS and CDFW agree).

Helicopters will not be used between 45 minutes before sunset to 45 minutes after sunrise.

obl-0759.title: Keep combined pile-driving and general construction noise at or below 50 dBA Leq (1 hour) at the nearest roost sites at night (1 hour before sunset to 1 hour after sunrise) by daytime-only work, siting night work, relocating cultivated roosts, or noise barriers.

night pile driving near flooded roost

locators.excerpt: Avoid pile driving and general construction-related noise effects on known permanent and temporary roost sites as described below. Activities within 0.75 mile of known roost sites will reduce pile driving and general construction noise during nighttime hours (from 1 hour before sunset to 1 hour after sunrise) such that pile-driving and general construction noise levels do not exceed a combined 50 dBA L eq (1 hour) at the nearest temporary or permanent roost sites during periods when the roost sites are available (flooded). This can be accomplished by limiting construction activities that could result in pile-driving and general construction noise levels above 50 dBA L (1 eq hour) at the roost site to day time only (from 1 hour after sunrise to 1 hour before sunset); siting nighttime project activities to ensure that pile-driving and general construction noise levels do not exceed a combined 50 dBA L (1 hour) at the roost site; relocating cultivated eq land roost sites as described above; and/or installing noise barriers between roost sites within the 50 dBA L (1 hour) contour and the eq pile-driving and general construction noise source areas, such that construction noise levels at the roost site do not exceed 50 dBA L (1 eq hour).

Potential den. a. Any subterranean hole within the species’ range that has entrances of appropriate dimensions for which available evidence is sufficient to conclude that it is being used or has been used by a San Joaquin kit fox.
