locators.excerpt: Permittee shall delineate TRBL roosting sites with different materials than those used to delineate the Project construction site and maintain the fencing or markings throughout all weather events.

obl-0952.title: Do no nighttime construction (45 minutes before sunset to 45 minutes after sunrise) inside the 300-foot buffer around a tricolored blackbird roost.
monitorSigns: night work within 300 ft of roost

locators.excerpt: DWR will not conduct nighttime construction (45 minutes before sunset to 45 minutes after sunrise) within a 300-foot non-disturbance buffer surrounding the roost site.

obl-0953.title: Mark the TRBL roost buffer clearly with fencing or other high-visibility marking.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall clearly delineate the buffered area using fencing or other high visibility marking.

obl-0954.title: Reduce a TRBL colony buffer (to no less than 300 feet) and work inside it only with CDFW written approval, and only where dense forest, buildings, topography or installed sound curtains shield the colony.
monitorSigns: buffer reduced with no written approval
reduced buffer with no CDFW approval

locators.excerpt: The no-activity buffer zone may be reduced to a minimum of 300 feet, with written approval from CDFW, in areas with dense forest, buildings, or other features between the Covered Activities and the breeding colony; where there is topographic relief to protect the colony from excessive noise or visual disturbance; or where sound curtains have been installed.

The non-disturbance buffer may be reduced to a minimum of 300 feet (91 meters), with written approval from CDFW, in areas with dense forest, buildings, or other features between the construction and the breeding colony, where there is sufficient topographic relief to protect the colony from excessive noise or visual disturbance; or where sound curtains have been installed.

obl-0955.title: Install the additional protective measures agreed, such as a larger buffer, delayed work, relocated staging, or rerouted access.
obl-0955.trigger: After CDFW consultation on colony disruption

locators.excerpt: Additional protective measures may include, but are not limited to, increasing the size of the buffer, delaying construction until the colony is finished breeding and chicks have left the nest site, temporarily relocating staging areas, and temporarily rerouting access to the construction site.

obl-0956.title: Do not land or take off helicopters within 500 feet of any TRBL breeding colony or occupied roost, unless CDFW has approved a reduced buffer in writing where dense forest, buildings or terrain shield it.
obl-0956.trigger: All helicopter landings and take-offs near TRBL colonies or occupied roosts
monitorSigns: landing inside 500 ft with no written CDFW approval
reduced buffer used with open line of sight to roost
helicopter landed within 500 ft of colony

locators.excerpt:
Permittee shall ensure helicopters do not land or take off within 500 feet of any breeding colony or occupied roost site.

This buffer may be modified in areas with dense forest, buildings, or other features between the helicopter landing/take-off site and the occupied roost site; where there is sufficient topographic relief to protect the roost site from excessive noise or disturbance; and as approved in writing by CDFW.

DWR will ensure helicopters do not land or take off within 500 feet (152 meters) of any breeding colony. This buffer may be modified in areas with dense forest, buildings, or other features between the helicopter landing/take- off site and the breeding colony, where there is sufficient topographic relief to protect the breeding colony from excessive noise or disturbance; and as approved in writing by CDFW.

obl-0957.title: When the biologist finds work is disrupting roosting TRBL, put added protective measures in place and keep them until behavior normalizes.
obl-0957.trigger: After the biologist finds roost disruption
monitorSigns: no added measures after disruption reported

locators.excerpt: If the Designated Biologist(s) determines that Covered Activities are disrupting roosting activity and TRBL are exhibiting agitated behaviors, Permittee shall put additional protective measures in place until TRBL behavior normalizes.

obl-0958.title: Put in the no-activity buffers or sound curtains set with CDFW when TRBL colonize habitat next to active work.
obl-0958.trigger: After CDFW consultation on a colony that formed after work started

locators.excerpt: If TRBL colonizes habitat adjacent to Covered Activities after they have been initiated, Permittee shall reduce the disturbance through establishment of no-activity buffers or sound curtains as determined in consultation with CDFW.

If tricolored blackbird colonizes habitat within 1,300 feet of construction after construction has been initiated, DWR will reduce disturbance through establishment of non-disturbance buffers and/or sound curtains, as determined in consultation with CDFW.

obl-0959.title: Mark TRBL colonies with different materials than the construction site boundary, and keep the markings up through all weather.
monitorSigns: colony marked same as site boundary

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall delineate TRBL colonies with different materials than those used to delineate the Project construction site and maintain the fencing or markings through all weather events.

obl-0960.title: Keep seasonal buffer zones, consistent with Mitigation Measure BIO-33, around restored tricolored blackbird nesting habitat.
obl-0960.trigger: Restored tricolored blackbird nesting habitat during the nesting season

locators.excerpt: Establish seasonal buffer zones (consistent with buffers described in Chapter 13, Mitigation Measure BIO-33) around restored tricolored blackbird nesting habitat to reduce disturbance and improve foraging habitat for tricolored blackbirds.

obl-0961.title: Do not touch an occupied TRBL roost during the nonbreeding season (September 16 to February 28).

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall prohibit physical contact with an occupied roost site during the nonbreeding season (September 16 – February 28).

obl-0962.title: When working by helicopter within 200 horizontal or 150 vertical feet of a colony or occupied roost, fly no more than three minutes at a time, no more than twice a day, with at least four hours between sessions.
obl-0962.trigger: Helicopter work within 200 horizontal or 150 vertical feet of a TRBL colony or occupied roost
monitorSigns: helicopter over colony more than 3 minutes
second pass less than 4 hours after first

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall only operate helicopters at these distances from the breeding colony or occupied roost site for up to three minutes in duration, no more than twice per day, with a minimum of four hours between helicopter activities.
DWR will only operate helicopters at these distances from the breeding colony for up to 3 minutes in duration, once or twice per day, with a minimum of 4 hours between helicopter activities.

obl-0963.title: Do not work within a TRBL roosting site.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall not conduct Covered Activities within the roosting site.

obl-0964.title: Keep disturbing activities stopped until additional protective measures are in place, unless the colony's behavior normalizes on its own.

locators.excerpt: Stop construction activities that are resulting in the disturbance until additional protective measures are implemented, unless tricolored blackbird breeding behavior normalizes on its own. b.

obl-0965.title: Keep construction away from suitable tricolored blackbird nesting habitat within 1,300 feet, to the extent feasible.
monitorSigns: work within 1,300 ft of nesting habitat with no feasibility call

locators.excerpt: DWR will ensure construction avoids suitable nesting habitat within 1,300 feet, to the extent feasible as determined by the construction manager in coordination with the CDFW-approved biologist.

obl-0966.title: Do no work inside a no-activity or nest disturbance buffer around a TRBL nest, breeding colony or occupied roost.
obl-0966.trigger: Whenever a TRBL no-activity or nest disturbance buffer is in place

locators.excerpt: Work within the nest disturbance buffer shall not be permitted.
Permittee shall prohibit conduct of Covered Activities within no-activity buffers established for breeding colonies or occupied roost sites (see Conditions of Approval 11.85 and 11.87).

obl-0967.title: Burn, mow, or graze bulrush/cattail stands every 2 to 5 years, or at an interval CDFW agrees to, to remove dead growth.
obl-0967.trigger: Bulrush/cattail stands in managed nesting habitat
monitorSigns: no treatment in more than 5 years

locators.excerpt: Burn, mow, or graze bulrush/cattail vegetation every 2 to 5 years, or an  appropriate interval necessary and agreed to by CDFW to remove dead growth and encourage the development of new vegetative structure.

obl-0968.title: Do not string SCADA or transmission line by helicopter within 200 horizontal or 150 vertical feet of a TRBL colony or occupied roost unless the helicopter is small enough to cause only a 15 to 18 mph downdraft at up to 150 feet.
obl-0968.trigger: All helicopter line stringing near breeding colonies or occupied roosts
monitorSigns: large helicopter stringing line near colony

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall not use helicopters to string SCADA or transmission lines within 200 horizontal feet or 150 vertical feet of breeding colonies or occupied roost sites unless the helicopter is small enough to only cause a down draft of 15 to 18 miles per hour at up to 150 feet.

obl-0969.title: Do no construction inside the 1,300-foot non-disturbance buffer around a detected colony and its habitat during the breeding season (March 15 to July 31).

locators.excerpt: If nesting habitat cannot be avoided and a tricolored blackbird breeding colony is detected, DWR will ensure construction does not occur within a 1,300-foot diameter non-disturbance buffer surrounding the colony and associated habitat during the breeding season (March 15 through July 31).

obl-0970.title: Within 1,300 feet of an occupied TRBL breeding colony or roost, work only from 45 minutes after sunrise to 45 minutes before sunset, unless CDFW approves otherwise.
obl-0970.trigger: Covered Activities within 1,300 ft of an occupied TRBL colony or roost

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall restrict Covered Activities to 45 minutes after sunrise and 45 minutes before sunset when Covered Activities occur within 1,300 feet of a breeding colony or roost site occupied by TRBL, unless otherwise approved by CDFW.

obl-0971.title: Do not start nighttime construction within 300 feet of roosting habitat until the preconstruction roost surveys are complete.

locators.excerpt: Prior to initiation of nighttime construction activities (45 minutes before sunset to 45 minutes after sunrise) within 300 feet of a construction site, the CDFW-approved biologist(s) will conduct preconstruction surveys to establish the existence and use of roosting habitat by tricolored blackbird.

obl-0972.title: Tell the Designated Biologist immediately if a TRBL is hurt or killed by the work, or if you find a dead or injured TRBL near the work.
obl-0972.trigger: Immediately on take, or on finding a dead or injured TRBL near preconstruction, construction, or maintenance areas
monitorSigns: dead bird found, biologist not called

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall immediately notify the Designated Biologist(s) if TRBL is taken by a Covered Activity, or if a TRBL is otherwise found dead or injured within the vicinity of the Project preconstruction activity, construction site, or maintenance area.

obl-0973.title: Where an active TRBL nest is within the site or 1,300 feet of work and cannot be avoided, do no work inside the 1,300-foot no-activity buffer around the colony and its habitat during the breeding season (March 1 to September 15) until young fledge, or as CDFW approves.
obl-0973.trigger: Active TRBL colonies in or within 1,300 ft of Covered Activities, breeding season

locators.excerpt: If active nests are found within the Project construction sites or within 1,300 feet of any Covered Activity and cannot be avoided, Permittee shall ensure that Covered Activities do not occur within a 1,300-foot diameter no-activity buffer zone surrounding the colony and associated suitable habitat during the breeding season (March 1 – September 15), until the young have fledged, or when approved by CDFW.

obl-0974.title: Work only on Project sites outside the flagged TRBL habitat.
obl-0974.trigger: All Covered Activities at sites with delineated TRBL habitat

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall restrict these Covered Activities to Project Sites outside of the delineated habitat.

obl-0975.title: Manage protected or restored nesting habitat for young, lush bulrush/cattail stands and prevent senescence, or for other CDFW-agreed nesting substrate.
obl-0975.trigger: Protected or restored tricolored blackbird nesting habitat

locators.excerpt: Protected or restored nesting habitat will be managed to provide young, lush stands of bulrush/cattail emergent vegetation and prevent vegetation senescence; or other nesting substrate determined to be location and use appropriate and agreed to by CDFW.

obl-0976.title: Do not fly larger helicopters or run longer helicopter work periods near TRBL until the CDFW-set buffer is in place.
obl-0976.trigger: Larger helicopters or longer work periods near TRBL colonies or roosts
monitorSigns: larger helicopter operating before buffer set
long helicopter session with no buffer

locators.excerpt: For larger helicopters or longer work periods, Permittee shall consult with CDFW to establish the appropriate buffer needed.

obl-0977.title: Do not set up break, rest, or meeting areas next to or inside TRBL nest or roost buffers.
obl-0977.trigger: All break, rest, and meeting areas, whenever TRBL no-activity buffers are in place

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall not designate any employee break, rest, or meeting areas adjacent to or within the no-activity nest and roosting buffers.

obl-0978.title: Do not touch a TRBL breeding colony during the breeding season (March 1 to September 15), from nest site selection until the chicks fledge or the colony is inactive.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall prohibit physical contact with a breeding colony during the breeding season (March 1 – September 15) from the time of nest site selection until after the chicks have fledged or colony is no longer active, as determined by a Designated Biologist(s) and approved by CDFW.

obl-0979.title: Do not touch, handle, or move TRBL; leave it to the Designated Biologist.

locators.excerpt: Only the CDFW-approved Designated Biologist(s) with appropriate expertise in handling blackbirds shall handle and relocate TRBL.

obl-0980.title: Minimize insecticide use during the spring growing season until tricolored blackbird nestlings have fledged or it is documented that no nearby nesting is occurring.
obl-0980.trigger: Cultivated lands managed as high- to very high-value tricolored blackbird foraging habitat, spring growing season
monitorSigns: insecticide sprayed in spring with nesting nearby

locators.excerpt: On cultivated lands managed as high- to very high-value foraging habitat for tricolored blackbirds, insecticide use will be minimized to the greatest extent practicable during the spring growing season until tricolored blackbird nestlings have fledged or it is documented that no nearby nesting is occurring. This is to ensure that an abundant insect prey population is available to support egg development and feeding of the young, as well as to minimize the risk of pesticide toxicity effects.

obl-0981.title: Avoid suitable TRBL roosting habitat and a 300-foot buffer around it as far as practicable.
obl-0981.trigger: All Covered Activities near suitable roosting habitat
monitorSigns: work within 300 ft of suitable roost habitat

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall ensure Covered Activities avoid suitable roosting habitat and a surrounding buffer area of 300 feet to the extent practicable.

obl-0982.title: Do not start construction in a work area until the preconstruction colony surveys are done.
obl-0982.trigger: Before construction in each work area

locators.excerpt: Prior to initiation of construction in a given work area and within 1,300 feet (396 meters) of the work area, the CDFW-approved biologist(s) will conduct preconstruction surveys to evaluate the presence of tricolored blackbird breeding colonies and suitable nesting habitat.

obl-0983.title: Keep large continuous bulrush/cattail stands at least 30 to 45 feet wide.

locators.excerpt: Maintain large continuous stands of bulrush/cattail that are at least 30 to 45  feet wide to provide adequate space for breeding as well as protection from predators.

obl-0984.title: Within 1,300 feet of an occupied colony, work only from 45 minutes after sunrise to 45 minutes before sunset, to the extent feasible.
obl-0984.trigger: Construction within 1,300 feet of an occupied breeding colony

locators.excerpt: DWR will restrict construction to 45 minutes after sunrise to 45 minutes before sunset if occurring within 1,300 feet (396 meters) of a breeding colony occupied by tricolored blackbird to the extent feasible, as determined by the contractor in coordination with the CDFW-approved biologist.

obl-0985.title: Change the roost buffer only where forest, buildings, topography, or sound curtains shield the roost and CDFW has approved it in writing.
obl-0985.trigger: When a modified roost buffer is proposed
monitorSigns: modified buffer with no CDFW approval

locators.excerpt: The non- disturbance buffer may be modified in areas with dense forest, buildings, or other features between the nighttime construction and the occupied roost site; where there is sufficient topographic relief to protect the roost site from excessive noise or visual disturbance; or where sound curtains are installed, as approved in writing by CDFW.

obl-0986.title: Mark the buffer clearly with fencing or other high-visibility marking.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall clearly delineate the buffered area using fencing or other high visibility marking.

obl-0987.title: Where conditions permit, establish stands of emergent vegetation, native blackberry, or other native vegetation along ditches and canals as tricolored blackbird nesting substrate.
obl-0987.trigger: Ditches and canals where conditions permit

locators.excerpt: Where conditions permit, stands of emergent vegetation, native blackberry, or other native vegetation will be established along ditches and canals to provide suitable nesting substrate for tricolored blackbird.

obl-0988.title: Stay in your vehicle while inside a TRBL no-activity breeding or roosting buffer when TRBL are present.
obl-0988.trigger: Inside an established TRBL no-activity buffer while TRBL are present
monitorSigns: worker out of vehicle inside buffer
door open, crew on foot in buffer

locators.excerpt: Project personnel shall not exit vehicles when inside the established no-activity buffer for breeding or roosting when TRBL are present (see Conditions of Approval 11.85 and 11.87).

obl-0989.title: Do the loudest work only in the windows set with the biologist and CDFW.
obl-0989.trigger: Loud or disruptive Covered Activities near TRBL

locators.excerpt: To the maximum extent feasible, Permittee shall coordinate with the Designated Biologist(s) and CDFW to time the loudest or otherwise most disruptive Covered Activities outside periods where the TRBL, their nests/colony, their eggs, or their young are most vulnerable to disturbance.

obl-0990.title: Watch TRBL nests and colonies for abandonment, abandoned nestlings, distress, or abnormal nesting behavior.
obl-0990.trigger: Throughout monitoring of active TRBL nests and colonies
monitorSigns: adults off nest, did not return

locators.excerpt: The Designated Biologist(s) shall immediately notify CDFW (within 24 hours) if TRBL abandon their nests or nestlings are abandoned, or nesting or roosting colonies exhibit distress and/or abnormal nesting behavior.

obl-0991.title: Train Project personnel, within the education program, on TRBL avoidance procedures, buffer zones, and what to do if a TRBL flies into an active construction site.
obl-0991.trigger: As part of the worker education program (COA 9.4)

locators.excerpt: The Designated Biologist(s) shall train Project personnel on the required avoidance procedures, buffer zones, and protocols in the event that a TRBL flies into an active Project construction site (i.e., outside the buffer zone), as part of the education program described in Condition of Approval 9.4.

obl-0992.title: If work starts in the breeding season, do three surveys within 15 days of starting, one within three days of ground disturbance at the site and within 1,300 feet.
obl-0992.trigger: Covered Activities initiated during the breeding season
monitorSigns: no survey within 3 days of start

locators.excerpt: If Covered Activities are initiated during the breeding season, the Designated Biologist(s) with assistance (if needed) from the Biological Monitor(s) shall conduct three surveys within 15 days of commencement of Covered Activities, with one survey occurring within three days of initiating ground-disturbing Covered Activities within the Project site and 1,300 feet from the Project site.

obl-0993.title: Re-check suitable roost sites within 300 feet that were unoccupied at preconstruction surveys to see whether TRBL later occupy them.
obl-0993.trigger: During Covered Activities, per the approved roosting protocol
monitorSigns: no follow-up check of unoccupied roosts

locators.excerpt: The Designated Biologist(s) with assistance (if needed) from the Biological Monitor(s) shall check suitable roost sites within 300 feet of Project sites that are not occupied at the time of preconstruction surveys in accordance with the roosting survey protocol approved by CDFW (Condition of Approval 11.38), to determine whether TRBL later occupies the roost site.

obl-0994.title: Survey for tricolored blackbird roosting habitat use before nighttime construction within 300 feet, in the nonbreeding season (August 1 to March 14) one year before and again in the year of construction.
obl-0994.trigger: Before nighttime construction within 300 feet of a site

locators.excerpt: Prior to initiation of nighttime construction activities (45 minutes before sunset to 45 minutes after sunrise) within 300 feet of a construction site, the CDFW-approved biologist(s) will conduct preconstruction surveys to establish the existence and use of roosting habitat by tricolored blackbird. Surveys will be conducted during the nonbreeding season (August 1 through March 14) 1 year prior and then the year of construction to establish use of roosting habitat.

obl-0995.title: Only CDFW-approved Designated Biologists with blackbird handling expertise may handle or relocate TRBL.
obl-0995.trigger: Any handling or relocation of TRBL
monitorSigns: monitor without blackbird expertise moving birds

locators.excerpt: Only the CDFW-approved Designated Biologist(s) with appropriate expertise in handling blackbirds shall handle and relocate TRBL.

obl-0996.title: Mark occupied TRBL roost sites with flagging or other visible markings.

locators.excerpt: The Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor shall delineate occupied roost sites with flagging or visible markings consistent with Condition of Approval 11.90.
The CDFW-approved biologist(s) will delineate occupied roost sites with flagging or other visible markings.

obl-0997.title: Survey the construction site or maintenance area and within 300 feet for TRBL roosting before work, including nighttime construction and postconstruction maintenance.
obl-0997.trigger: Before Covered Activities at each site
monitorSigns: no roost survey before night work

locators.excerpt: Prior to initiation of Covered Activities, including nighttime construction and postconstruction maintenance activities, in a Project construction site or Project maintenance area and within 300 feet of a Project site, the Designated Biologist(s) with assistance (if needed) from the Biological Monitor(s) shall conduct preconstruction surveys to establish the existence and use of roosting habitat by TRBL.

obl-0998.title: Before each Project phase, assess TRBL habitat per CDFW-approved protocols to find existing or potential nesting or foraging sites in the Project site and, where feasible, within three miles.
obl-0998.trigger: Before Covered Activities in each Project Phase
monitorSigns: no habitat assessment before phase start

locators.excerpt: Prior to the commencement of Covered Activities for each Project Phase, the Designated Biologist(s) shall conduct a habitat assessment consistent with CDFW-approved protocols (Condition of Approval 11.38) to determine if existing or potential nesting or foraging sites are present within the Project site and include areas within three miles of Project sites, where feasible.

obl-0999.title: During night construction, check suitable unoccupied roost sites within 300 feet each day through the nonbreeding season, per the approved protocol.
obl-0999.trigger: Nights with construction in the nonbreeding season

locators.excerpt: During nighttime construction activities (45 minutes before sunset to 45 minutes after sunrise), the CDFW-approved biologist(s) will check suitable roost sites within 300 feet of construction areas that are not occupied at the time of preconstruction surveys each day throughout the nonbreeding season, in accordance with the roosting survey protocol approved by CDFW, to determine whether tricolored blackbird later occupy the roost site.

obl-1000.title: Stop construction when it is disrupting a colony.
obl-1000.trigger: When construction disrupts a tricolored blackbird colony

locators.excerpt: If the Designated Biologist(s) determines that construction is causing a disruption to the colony, the CDFW-approved biologist(s) will have the authority to stop construction and will notify DWR immediately. Stop construction activities that are resulting in the disturbance until additional protective measures are implemented, unless tricolored blackbird breeding behavior normalizes on its own. b.

obl-1001.title: Mark suitable TRBL nesting habitat and breeding colonies with flagging or other visible marking.
obl-1001.trigger: Each identified colony and nesting habitat area near work

locators.excerpt: The Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall delineate suitable nesting habitat and breeding colonies with flagging or other visible marking.
The CDFW-approved biologist(s) will delineate suitable nesting habitat and breeding colonies with flagging or other visible marking.

obl-1002.title: Keep monitoring and make sure additional measures remain in place until the biologist determines behavior has normalized.
obl-1002.trigger: While additional protective measures are in place

locators.excerpt: Continue monitoring and ensure additional protective measures will remain in place for the duration of construction. c. Maintain additional protective measures until the CDFW-approved biologist determines tricolored blackbird behavior has normalized and continue monitoring.

obl-1003.title: Flag or otherwise highly visibly mark suitable TRBL nesting and roosting habitat and its buffers at preconstruction, staging, SCADA, transmission line, and access road construction and maintenance sites.
obl-1003.trigger: At Project sites for preconstruction activities, staging areas, SCADA, transmission line, and access road construction and maintenance sites

locators.excerpt: The Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall delineate suitable nesting and roosting habitat and buffers with flagging or other highly visible marking at Project sites for preconstruction activities, construction staging areas, SCADA, transmission line, and access road construction and maintenance sites.

obl-1004.title: Survey within 1,300 feet of each work area for tricolored blackbird colonies and suitable nesting habitat monthly from March through July, one year before and again in the year of construction.
obl-1004.trigger: Before construction in a given work area

locators.excerpt: Prior to initiation of construction in a given work area and within 1,300 feet (396 meters) of the work area, the CDFW-approved biologist(s) will conduct preconstruction surveys to evaluate the presence of tricolored blackbird breeding colonies and suitable nesting habitat. Surveys will be conducted during the breeding season (March 15 through July 31) 1 year prior to, and then again in the year of, construction. During each year, surveys will be conducted monthly in March, April, May, June, and July.

obl-1005.title: If construction starts in the nonbreeding season, do three surveys within 15 days before work, one within three days before start.
obl-1005.trigger: Construction initiated during the nonbreeding season
monitorSigns: no survey within 3 days of start

locators.excerpt: If construction is initiated at a site during the nonbreeding season, the Designated Biologist(s) with assistance (if needed) from the Biological Monitor(s) shall conduct three surveys within 15 days prior to the Covered Activities, with one of the surveys occurring within three days prior to the start of the Covered Activity.

obl-1006.title: Treat a roost used by large mixed blackbird flocks as occupied by TRBL unless TRBL absence can be clearly confirmed.
obl-1006.trigger: Roost surveys with large mixed blackbird flocks
monitorSigns: mixed flock roost recorded as unoccupied without confirming absence
mixed flock roost treated as unoccupied

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall consider roosting habitat occupied by large mixed blackbird flocks to be occupied by TRBL if the Designated Biologist(s) cannot clearly identify TRBL absence within the flock.

DWR will consider roosting habitat occupied by large mixed blackbird flocks to be occupied by tricolored blackbird if the CDFW- approved biologist(s) cannot clearly identify tricolored blackbird presence within the flock.

obl-1007.title: Document whether tricolored blackbirds are nesting nearby and when nestlings have fledged.
obl-1007.trigger: Spring growing season near managed foraging lands

locators.excerpt: On cultivated lands managed as high- to very high-value foraging habitat for tricolored blackbirds, insecticide use will be minimized to the greatest extent practicable during the spring growing season until tricolored blackbird nestlings have fledged or it is documented that no nearby nesting is occurring.

obl-1008.title: Complete the baseline assessment during the breeding season (March 1 to September 15) before work starts.

locators.excerpt: The preconstruction (i.e., baseline) assessment shall be completed during the breeding season (March 1 – September 15) prior to implementation of Covered Activities.

obl-1009.title: Monitor occupied roosts within the 300-foot no-activity buffer daily for at least four hours, or until no longer occupied, per the CDFW-approved TRBL protocol, to confirm work is not disrupting them.
obl-1009.trigger: Occupied roost sites within the 300-ft buffer

locators.excerpt: Occupied roost sites that are within the 300 feet no-activity buffer (Condition of Approval 11.87) shall be monitored daily by the Designated Biologist(s), with assistance (if needed) from the Biological Monitor(s), for at least four hours each day or until the roost site is no longer occupied and consistent with CDFW-approved TRBL survey protocol (Condition of Approval 11.38) to verify that Covered Activities are not disrupting roosting TRBL.

obl-1010.title: Survey the Project site and within 1,300 feet for TRBL breeding colonies and suitable nesting habitat before work, unless CDFW approves otherwise.
obl-1010.trigger: Before Covered Activities at a Project site

locators.excerpt: Prior to the initiation of Covered Activities in a Project site and within 1,300 feet of the Project site unless otherwise approved by CDFW, the Designated Biologist(s) with assistance (if needed) from the Biological Monitor(s) shall conduct preconstruction surveys to evaluate the presence of TRBL breeding colonies and suitable nesting habitat.

obl-1011.title: Watch for TRBL agitation showing that work is disrupting roosting.
obl-1011.trigger: During Covered Activities near occupied roosts

locators.excerpt: If the Designated Biologist(s) determines that Covered Activities are disrupting roosting activity and TRBL are exhibiting agitated behaviors, Permittee shall put additional protective measures in place until TRBL behavior normalizes.

obl-1012.title: Survey for TRBL each year Covered Activities are expected in TRBL habitat during construction or maintenance.
obl-1012.trigger: Each year with Covered Activities in TRBL habitat

locators.excerpt: Subsequent survey efforts conducted during the Project construction phase(s) or maintenance shall occur each year Covered Activities are expected to occur in TRBL habitat and shall be reported to CDFW by the Permittee within the Monthly Compliance Reporting (Condition of Approval 10.12) and summarized within each Annual Status Report (Condition of Approval 10.13).

obl-1013.title: Notify DWR immediately when construction is stopped for colony disruption.

locators.excerpt: If the Designated Biologist(s) determines that construction is causing a disruption to the colony, the CDFW-approved biologist(s) will have the authority to stop construction and will notify DWR immediately.

obl-1014.title: Monitor any nesting TRBL colony in the site or within 1,300 feet of work at least six hours a day throughout the nesting season, to confirm work is not disrupting it and to determine when young have fledged, unless CDFW approves otherwise.
obl-1014.trigger: Nesting TRBL within the site or 1,300 ft of Covered Activities, nesting season

locators.excerpt: If nesting TRBL is present within the Project construction site or within 1,300 feet of any Project- related Covered Activity, the Designated Biologist(s) with assistance (if needed) from the Biological Monitor(s) shall monitor the colony daily for at least six hours per day throughout the nesting season to verify the Covered Activities are not disrupting the colony and to determine when the young have fledged, unless otherwise approved by CDFW.

obl-1015.title: Survey each preconstruction, SCADA, transmission line, access road, construction and maintenance site for suitable TRBL nesting and roosting habitat, using CDFW-approved protocols.
obl-1015.trigger: Before initiation of any Covered Activities at each site
monitorSigns: site with no TRBL habitat survey before work

locators.excerpt: The Designated Biologist(s) with assistance (if needed) from the Biological Monitor(s) shall conduct CDFW approved TRBL survey protocols (Condition of Approval 11.38) to identify the presence of suitable nesting habitat and roosting habitat, within each preconstruction activity site, SCADA, transmission line and access road site, construction site, and maintenance area, prior to initiation of any Covered Activities.

obl-1016.title: Determine when the chicks have fledged or the colony is no longer active, for CDFW approval.
monitorSigns: contact restriction lifted without fledging determination

obl-1240.trigger: When hauling is the chosen method
monitorSigns: debris on site more than 24 hours

locators.excerpt: (2) Debris shall be immediately hauled off-site for disposal within 24 hours to avoid GGS from colonizing debris piles.

obl-1241.title: Do not disc or till upland vegetation.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall not disc or till upland vegetation as disking is more hazardous to GGS that are underground than mowing.

obl-1242.title: Haul cleared vegetation off site immediately, or pile it at least 200 feet from Covered Species habitat and leave it undisturbed.
monitorSigns: vegetation pile within 200 feet of habitat

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall immediately haul vegetative material off site for disposal or place the material in piles at least 200 feet from Covered Species habitat to be left undisturbed.

obl-1243.title: Do not remove vegetation inside established no-disturbance buffers.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall not remove vegetation within established Covered Species no-disturbance buffers.

obl-1244.title: Trim vegetation marked for protection only with hand string trimmers, and only as needed for access or facility maintenance.

locators.excerpt: Vegetation marked for protection may only be trimmed with hand tools limited to string trimmers (e.g., weed whackers) to the extent necessary to gain access to work sites or for facility maintenance, to minimize potential of crushing burrows or impacting the ground.

obl-1245.title: Disturb or remove only the vegetation needed to do the work.

locators.excerpt: Disturbance or removal of vegetation shall be kept to the minimum necessary to complete Covered Activities.

obl-1246.title: Set mower blades no lower than four inches unless CDFW approves otherwise in writing.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall set mower blade heights to no lower than four inches, unless otherwise approved by CDFW in writing (See Condition of Approval 11.18).

obl-1247.title: Do not remove vegetation in avoidable burrows, burrow complexes or refugia, to the greatest extent practicable.
obl-1247.trigger: Vegetation work near burrows and refugia

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall not remove vegetation within avoidable burrows, burrow complexes, and suitable refugia to the greatest extent practicable.

obl-1248.title: Watch for fossorial Covered Species during vegetation management.

locators.excerpt: The Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor shall be on site during vegetation management activities to monitor for any fossorial Covered Species.

obl-1249.title: Where curbs are needed for safety or runoff, design and build them so Covered Species can walk over them.
obl-1249.trigger: Curbs on roads within Covered Species habitat
monitorSigns: vertical curb too high to cross

locators.excerpt: If curbs are necessary for safety and/or surface runoff, Permittee shall design and construct them to allow Covered Species to walk over them.

obl-1250.title: Post wildlife crossing and extra caution signs in both directions on all access roads that overlap CTS and GGS aquatic and upland habitat.
obl-1250.trigger: Access roads overlapping CTS and GGS habitat, during construction, operations and maintenance

locators.excerpt: Wildlife crossing signs and signage requiring extra caution shall be posted in both directions on all Project access roads that overlap with CTS and GGS aquatic and upland habitat during Project construction, operations, and maintenance.

obl-1251.title: Build the crossings (culverts or bridges) on Brushy Creek, Italian Slough, Mountain House Creek, and the unnamed channels at Byron Highway and Mountain House Road to the required frog-passage performance standards.
obl-1251.trigger: Design and construction of crossings at the named creeks and channels
monitorSigns: culvert does not match approved performance standards

locators.excerpt: DWR will design and construct crossings (i.e., culverts or bridges) on Brushy Creek, Italian Slough, Mountain House Creek, and the unnamed channels crossing Byron Highway and Mountain House Road that meet the following performance standards.

obl-1252.title: Where median barriers cannot be avoided for public safety, fit them with small ground-level openings for amphibian passage.
obl-1252.trigger: Median barriers required for public safety

locators.excerpt: If median barriers cannot be avoided due to public safety concerns, barriers will be outfitted with small openings at ground level to allow amphibian passage.

obl-1253.title: Include wildlife crossings where the Byron Highway intersection and Armstrong Road extension cross Brushy Creek, spanning the banks as far as possible and designed for California red-legged frog, western pond turtle, and other wildlife.
obl-1253.trigger: Byron Highway / Armstrong Road work under Alternatives 1, 2a-2c, 3, 4a-4c

locators.excerpt: The new intersection for Byron Highway and the extension of Armstrong Road (Alternatives 1, 2a, 2b, 2c, 3, 4a, 4b, and 4c) will include wildlife crossing structures where the new road intersects with Brushy Creek. The wildlife crossing structure will span the banks of the channel to the maximum extent possible and will incorporate design elements to facilitate movement and connectivity of California red-legged frog, western pond turtle, and other aquatic, semi-aquatic, and terrestrial wildlife species inhabiting the area.

obl-1254.title: Do not install curbs on new or widened access road segments, to the extent practicable.
obl-1254.trigger: New and widened access road segments, to the extent practicable
monitorSigns: curb installed on new access road segment

locators.excerpt: New and widened access road segments will avoid installing curbs, to the extent practicable.

obl-1255.title: Build road culvert under-crossings of concrete with a natural sand, dirt, or gravel bottom, unless CDFW approves otherwise for site constraints.

locators.excerpt: Unless otherwise approved by CDFW due to site-specific constraints, Permittee shall construct road culvert under-crossings using concrete with a natural substrate bottom such as sand, dirt, or gravel.

obl-1256.title: Where curbs must be installed, build them with sloping sides under 30 degrees so amphibians can cross.
obl-1256.trigger: Any curb that must be installed on new or widened access roads

locators.excerpt: If curbs must be installed, curbs will be designed with sloping sides less than 30 degrees (Clevenger and Huijser 2011:156) to allow amphibian movement across the road.

obl-1257.title: Keep habitat connectivity along riparian banks and corridors at levees, intakes, and other facilities during operations.

locators.excerpt: Contiguous habitat connectivity along riparian banks and riparian corridors will be maintained during operations to maintain connectivity at riparian banks and corridors at levees, intakes, and other facilities located along/within riparian banks and corridors.

obl-1258.title: Keep steel grate windows out of vehicle wheel paths.

locators.excerpt: Steel grate windows shall not be placed directly in vehicle wheel pathways, as this would produce a “flashing” of light to dark for the species using the culvert under- crossing and would dissuade the use of the culvert tunnel.

obl-1259.title: Post wildlife crossing signs in both directions on new or widened access roads that overlap special-status wildlife habitat.
obl-1259.trigger: New or widened access roads in special-status wildlife habitat, to the extent practicable

locators.excerpt: Wildlife crossing signs will be posted in both directions on new or widened access roads that overlap with habitat for special-status wildlife, to the extent practicable.

obl-1260.title: Keep habitat connectivity along riparian banks and corridors at levees, intakes, and other facilities during construction, to the extent feasible.
obl-1260.trigger: During construction along riparian banks and corridors

locators.excerpt: Contiguous habitat connectivity along riparian banks and corridors will be maintained during construction, to the extent feasible, to maintain connectivity at riparian banks and corridors at levees, intakes, and other facilities located along or within riparian banks and corridors.

obl-1261.title: Make under-crossing culverts at least six inches in size.

locators.excerpt: A minimum under-crossing culvert size of six inches shall be used to ensure Covered Species and other wildlife may move across active roadways.

obl-1262.title: Post caution signs for giant garter snakes basking on cool days and California tiger salamander and California red-legged frog moving on rainy nights
obl-1262.trigger: Construction access roads in those species' habitat

locators.excerpt: Signage would be provided for extra caution to be used on cool days when giant garter snake may be basking on roads and on rainy nights when California tiger salamander and California red-legged frog are most likely to be moving between breeding and upland habitats.

obl-1263.title: Build roads in Covered Species habitat without steep curbs, berms, dikes, or median barriers that keep animals from crossing or leaving the road.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall construct roadways that are within Covered Species habitat such that there are no steep curbs, berms, dikes, or median barriers (e.g., k-cuts) that could prevent Covered Species from crossing or exiting the roadway.

obl-1264.title: Do not install median barriers (k-rails) on new or widened access road segments, to the extent practicable.
obl-1264.trigger: New and widened access road segments, to the extent practicable

locators.excerpt: New and widened access road segments will avoid installing median barriers (i.e., k-rails), to the extent practicable.

obl-1265.title: Install wildlife fencing where applicable to keep wildlife off roads and facilities, placed so wildlife can move along riparian corridors.

locators.excerpt: Design will include wildlife fencing where applicable to prevent wildlife access to roads and facilities. Fencing will also be designed and placed in a manner that facilitates wildlife movement through or between the riparian banks and corridors during constriction.

obl-1266.title: Under Alternatives 1, 2a, 2b, and 2c, upgrade the SR 12 culvert (Barrier ID W031) to a dedicated wildlife crossing that spans the channel banks as far as possible and is designed for giant garter snake, western pond turtle, mink, river otter, beaver, and other reptiles and mammals.

locators.excerpt: As part of project access road improvement planning, design, and construction, under Alternatives 1, 2a, 2b, and 2c, the project will upgrade the existing culvert on SR 12 (identified by CDFW [2020d:11] as a priority barrier to wildlife movement in the region; Barrier ID W031) to a dedicated wildlife crossing structure to facilitate movement of both aquatic and terrestrial wildlife. The wildlife crossing structure will span the banks of the channel to the maximum extent possible and will incorporate design elements to facilitate movement and connectivity of giant garter snake, western pond turtle, mink, river otter, beaver, other reptiles, and mammals inhabiting the area. This mitigation is only applicable to Alternatives 1, 2a, 2b, and 2c to mitigate for the impacts of widening SR 12.

obl-1267.title: Operations monitoring must be overseen by an agency-approved biologist experienced in connectivity ecology, road ecology, and wildlife crossings.

locators.excerpt: An agency-approved biologist with demonstrated understanding of monitoring and adaptive management techniques used in the field of connectivity ecology, road ecology, and wildlife crossings will oversee operations monitoring of new wildlife crossings, connectivity enhancement measures (e.g., amphibian- friendly roads and curbs), new and modified roadways, and all project elements with potential to affect wildlife connectivity (e.g., project elements along riparian banks).

obl-1268.title: Monitor new wildlife crossings, connectivity features, new and modified roads, and other elements affecting connectivity for at least 5 years across multiple seasons, targeting all wildlife connectivity groups and listed species, using cameras, tracking, and roadkill surveys where access allows.

locators.excerpt: Monitoring will occur for at least 5 years using best practices in the field and will be compiled to inform adaptive management strategies, which may be needed to ensure intended connectivity function and value are being achieved. Monitoring techniques may include wildlife camera monitoring, wildlife tracking, and roadkill monitoring. Monitoring will be conducted over multiple seasons and include considerations and methodologies targeting species across all WCGs as well as listed species. Monitoring will be conducted from locations where access allows.

obl-1269.title: Compile monitoring results to inform adaptive management needed to achieve intended connectivity function.
obl-1269.trigger: During and after the monitoring period

locators.excerpt: Monitoring will occur for at least 5 years using best practices in the field and will be compiled to inform adaptive management strategies, which may be needed to ensure intended connectivity function and value are being achieved.

obl-1270.title: DWR must determine feasibility and develop and oversee connectivity and fencing design with a biologist qualified in wildlife crossing planning, and manage it with the qualified biologist during construction phasing.
obl-1270.trigger: Connectivity and fencing design and construction phasing

locators.excerpt: Feasibility will be determined and design and maintenance of habitat contiguity and fencing will be developed and overseen by DWR in coordination with a biologist qualified and experienced in wildlife crossing planning and design and will be managed in coordination with the qualified biologist during construction phasing.

obl-1271.title: Develop connectivity, revegetation, and fencing design with a biologist qualified in wildlife crossing planning.

locators.excerpt: Design of habitat contiguity, revegetation, and fencing will be developed by DWR in coordination with a biologist qualified and experienced in wildlife crossing planning and design.

obl-1272.title: Do not trench through burrows that cannot be avoided until the biologist has hand excavated them.
obl-1272.trigger: Before trenching where burrows cannot be avoided

locators.excerpt: When the Permittee cannot avoid burrows in areas of direct ground disturbance or in a location posing a risk of direct harm to CTS, they shall be hand excavated by the Designated Biologist(s) prior to trenching activities (see condition of Approval 11.49.2) and any CTS found during excavation shall be relocated according to the CTS Relocation Plan (see Condition of Approval 11.51).

Where the Permittee cannot avoid burrows (e.g., within footprint of ground disturbing activities), they shall be carefully excavated prior to any trenching activities and any GGS found during excavation that does not leave of its own volition shall be relocated according to Condition of Approval 11.67.

obl-1273.title: Stop all work that could harm a Covered Species until the animal leaves the site on its own.
obl-1273.trigger: Whenever a Covered Species is in or near the Project site

locators.excerpt: All Covered Activities with potential to take Covered Species shall cease until the animal moves from the Project site on its own accord.

obl-1274.title: Leave any wildlife in the maintenance area alone and let it move away on its own.
obl-1274.trigger: When wildlife is encountered in the maintenance area

locators.excerpt: Any wildlife that is encountered within the maintenance area will be avoided and allowed to move out of harm’s way of its own accord. g.

obl-1275.title: Tell the biologist or biological monitor right away if you see a Covered Species in or near the site.
obl-1275.trigger: Any Covered Species encounter in or near the Project site

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall direct all workers to inform the Designated Biologist(s), Fisheries Biologist(s), or Biological Monitor(s) if they encounter any Covered Species within or near the Project site.

obl-1276.title: If a special-status species is encountered, divert work away from it or stop work until it leaves on its own or is relocated by a qualified biologist, per the species' measures
obl-1276.trigger: Whenever a special-status species is encountered, including during dewatering

locators.excerpt: If a special-status species is encountered during construction work, including  dewatering, generally construction activities should be diverted away from the animal or, depending upon the conditions and specification in the relevant environmental documents and permits, work will cease until it moves out of the work area on its own or is relocated by a qualified biologist, following the species- specific mitigation measures appearing in the environmental documents and relevant permits.

obl-1277.title: Follow the biological monitor's recommendations for protecting a special-status species found in the work area
obl-1277.trigger: When the monitor reports a special-status species in the work area
monitorSigns: work continued next to species against monitor advice

locators.excerpt: If a special-status species is observed in an active work area, the biological monitors will immediately provide the construction manager and contractor with its location and recommendations to address the species’ presence and steps necessary to ensure the protection of the species consistent with permits and authorizations.

obl-1278.title: Do not capture or handle trapped or injured wildlife; leave it for the Designated or Fisheries Biologist.
obl-1278.trigger: Any trapped or injured special-status wildlife

locators.excerpt: Capture and relocation of trapped or injured special-status wildlife may only be performed by the Designated Biologist(s) and Fisheries Biologist(s).

obl-1279.title: Insert flexible plastic pipe at least 3 inches across into burrows during excavation to keep an escape route open.

locators.excerpt: Sections of flexible plastic pipe (at least 3 inches in diameter) will be inserted into burrows during excavation to maintain an escape route for any animals inside the burrow. Once the biologist concludes the owls have left the burrow, the burrow will be excavated using hand tools, and a section of flexible plastic pipe (at least 3 inches in diameter) will be inserted into the burrow tunnel during excavation to maintain an escape route for any animals that may be inside the burrow.

obl-1280.title: Follow the Declining Amphibian Population Task Force Fieldwork Code of Practice or current guidance when handling special-status amphibians
obl-1280.trigger: Capture and handling of special-status amphibians

locators.excerpt: When capturing and handing special-status amphibians, the biologists will follow the Declining Amphibian Population Task Force’s Fieldwork Code of Practice (U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service n.d.) or the most current applicable guidance.

obl-1281.title: When a Covered Species inside a fenced construction site cannot leave on its own, move it outside the construction area following its species-specific relocation plan.
obl-1281.trigger: Covered Species trapped inside fenced construction sites

locators.excerpt: If the animal is found within a fenced Project construction site and cannot move of its own volition, the Designated Biologist(s) shall move the animal outside of the area of construction according to their species-specific relocation or transplantation plans described in this ITP for each Covered Species.

obl-1282.title: Exclusion devices may be installed only by or under supervision of an experienced biologist.

locators.excerpt: Exclusionary devices will only be installed by or under the supervision of an experienced biologist. d.

obl-1283.title: If a special-status species is seen in an active work area, immediately give the construction manager and contractor its location and recommendations to protect it
obl-1283.trigger: Immediately on observing a special-status species in an active work area
monitorSigns: species observed, construction manager not informed

locators.excerpt: If a special-status species is observed in an active work area, the biological monitors will immediately provide the construction manager and contractor with its location and recommendations to address the species’ presence and steps necessary to ensure the protection of the species consistent with permits and authorizations.

obl-1284.title: Handle special-status fish and wildlife only with hands free of soaps, oils, lotions, repellents, solvents and other chemicals; use non-latex nitrile or hypoallergenic gloves if not single use.
obl-1284.trigger: All handling of special-status fish and wildlife

locators.excerpt: The Designated Biologist(s) shall ensure their hands are free of soaps, oils, creams, lotions, insect repellants, solvents or other potentially harmful chemicals and if not single use, nitrile or other hypo-allergenic gloves (non-latex) will be used for handling special-status fish or wildlife.

Any person who captures and handles special- status species will ensure their hands are free of soaps, oils, creams, lotions, insect repellents, solvents or other potentially harmful chemicals and if not single use, nitrile or other hypo-allergenic gloves (non-latex) will be used for handling special- status fish or wildlife.

obl-1285.title: Only personnel with USFWS and CDFW handling approvals may capture and relocate trapped or injured special-status wildlife
obl-1285.trigger: Any capture or relocation of special-status wildlife

locators.excerpt: Capture and relocation of trapped or injured special-status wildlife can only be  performed by personnel with appropriate USFWS and CDFW handling approvals.

obl-1286.title: Thoroughly inspect debris piles before they are removed.

locators.excerpt: Debris piles shall be kept to a minimum and removed regularly after thorough inspection by the Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s).

obl-1287.title: Release captured special-status animals into a safe aquatic environment as close as possible to where they were captured
monitorSigns: animal released far from capture point

locators.excerpt: To avoid transferring diseases or pathogens between aquatic habitats during the course of surveys or the capture and handling of special-status fish or wildlife species, all species captured and handled will be released in a safe, aquatic environment as close to the point of capture as possible.

obl-1288.title: Keep capture and relocation records with start and end times, species, time and finder and condition, capture and release locations, photographs, measurements where harmless, actions taken, and other pertinent information.

locators.excerpt: The Designated Biologist(s) shall maintain monitoring records that include, but are not limited to: (1) the beginning and ending time the capture and relocation effort, (2) a statement identifying the Covered Species encountered, (3) the time of discovery, by whom, and the condition of the Covered Species, (4) the capture and release locations of each Covered Species individual, (5) photographs of each Covered Species individual, (6) measurements of each Covered Species individual if doing so will not cause undue stress or harm, (7) a description of all actions taken, and (8) any other pertinent information.

obl-1289.title: Inspect fallen logs, brush piles, woody debris, and other overwintering refugia before removal, and supervise their removal.
obl-1289.trigger: Any removal of potential overwintering refugia during the overwintering period
monitorSigns: refugia removed with no prior inspection

locators.excerpt: During this time, removal of fallen logs, brush piles, woody debris, and other potential refugia for overwintering bees shall be done carefully with prior inspection and then supervision from the Designated Biologist(s) with assistance (if needed) from the Biological Monitor(s).

obl-1290.title: Capture and handle special-status fish and wildlife using the most recent standard methods and species-specific authorizations
obl-1290.trigger: All capture and handling of special-status species

locators.excerpt: The most recent available standard methods for species capture and handling, as  well as species specific authorizations, will be used to capture and handle special- status fish or wildlife species.

obl-1291.title: Keep captive amphibians cool, moist, and aerated, such as in a dark bucket with a damp sponge
monitorSigns: amphibian in hot or dry container

locators.excerpt: While in captivity, individual amphibians will be kept in a cool, moist, aerated environment such as a dark (e.g., green or brown) bucket containing a damp sponge.

obl-1292.title: Only the Designated Biologist(s) and Fisheries Biologist(s) may capture and relocate trapped or injured special-status wildlife.
obl-1292.trigger: All capture and relocation of special-status wildlife

locators.excerpt: Capture and relocation of trapped or injured special-status wildlife may only be performed by the Designated Biologist(s) and Fisheries Biologist(s).

obl-1293.title: Immediately take any Covered Species injured by Covered Activities to a CDFW-approved wildlife rehabilitation or veterinary facility suited to that individual.
obl-1293.trigger: Any Covered Species injured by Covered Activities

locators.excerpt: If a Covered Species is injured as a result of Covered Activities, the Designated Biologist shall immediately take it to a CDFW-approved wildlife rehabilitation or veterinary facility specific to the injured individual.

obl-1294.title: A professional biologist with USFWS and CDFW handling approvals must direct any capture and handling of special-status species
obl-1294.trigger: All capture and handling of special-status species
monitorSigns: capture with no approved biologist present

locators.excerpt: A professional biologist, with appropriate USFWS and CDFW handling approvals, will be responsible for and direct any efforts to capture and handle special-status species.

obl-1295.title: Direct all workers to tell the Designated Biologist, Fisheries Biologist, or Biological Monitor whenever they encounter a Covered Species.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall direct all workers to inform the Designated Biologist(s), Fisheries Biologist(s), or Biological Monitor(s) if they encounter any Covered Species within or near the Project site.

obl-1296.title: Pay any costs of care or treatment for injured Covered Species.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall bear any costs associated with the care or treatment of such injured Covered Species.

obl-1297.title: Do not use plastic monofilament netting or similar material anywhere on site, including exclusion fencing, buffers, ESAs and erosion control.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall prohibit the use of plastic monofilament netting (erosion control matting) or similar material on the Project Site for exclusionary fencing, non-disturbance buffers, environmentally sensitive areas (ESAs), erosion control (see Condition of Approval 11.27), or any other purpose, to avoid entanglement hazards to Covered Species.

obl-1298.title: Before shaft construction, place biologist-approved exclusion barriers around vertical shaft openings to keep wildlife out (e.g., chain link for foxes, exclusion barriers for amphibians and reptiles).
obl-1298.trigger: Shaft excavation sites, before shaft construction

locators.excerpt: Prior to shaft construction, the Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall ensure that vertical shafts have suitable exclusion barriers placed around the shaft opening to prohibit entry of Covered Species into the shaft.

Shaft excavation sites are exempt from this measure because it would not be feasible to place a ramp into a vertical shaft. Rather than a vertical ramp inside the shaft, suitable barriers, approved by a qualified biologist prior to construction at the shaft site (e.g. chain link fence for large wildlife such as foxes and appropriate exclusion barriers for amphibians and reptiles), will be placed around the shaft opening to prohibit entry of wildlife into the shaft.

obl-1299.title: At the close of each working day, cover excavations, steep-walled holes, pumps, and trenches deeper than six inches with plywood or similar sealed with rock bags, or give them earthfill or plank escape ramps no steeper than 30 degrees.
obl-1299.trigger: Close of each working day, excavations deeper than six inches other than shafts, in areas wildlife may occupy

locators.excerpt: The Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall ensure that all excavated areas, steep- walled holes, pumps, or trenches more than six inches deep, with the exception of shaft excavation, will be covered at the close of each working day with plywood or similar material and shall ensure the cover is sealed with rock bags or other methods to prevent animals from reentering or provided with one or more escape ramps constructed of earth fill or wooden planks at no more than a 30° angle.

To prevent inadvertent entrapment of special-status wildlife during construction in  areas that may be occupied by wildlife at risk for entrapment, all excavated, steep- walled holes or trenches more than 6 inches deep, with the exception of shaft excavation, will be covered at the close of each working day with plywood or similar material or will be provided with one or more escape ramps constructed of earthfill or wooden planks at no more than a 30° angle.

obl-1300.title: If a Covered Species or other animal is found in a pit, hole, or trench, move work away from it and contact the Designated Biologist.
obl-1300.trigger: Any animal found in an excavation

locators.excerpt: If a Covered Species or other animal is encountered in excavated pits, holes, or trenches during Covered Activities, Permittee shall divert Covered Activities away from the Covered Species until Project personnel contact the Designated Biologist(s).

obl-1301.title: Cap the ends of all pipes and culverts stored in the open
obl-1301.trigger: All pipes and culverts stored in the open

locators.excerpt: All pipes and culverts stored in the open will have their ends capped.

obl-1302.title: Do not fill or cover holes or trenches unless the biologist or monitor is present.
obl-1302.trigger: Filling or covering holes and trenches

locators.excerpt: Before such holes or trenches are filled, the Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall thoroughly inspect them for trapped animals and be present when holes or trenches are being covered or filled to ensure there is no entrapment of Covered Species and that the cover is secure.

obl-1303.title: Do not bury, cap, use, or move stored pipes and culverts until the biologist or monitor has inspected them.

locators.excerpt: All pipes, culverts, and similar structures with a diameter of 0.25 inches or greater that are stored in Project construction sites for one or more overnight periods shall be thoroughly inspected by the Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) for Covered Species prior to the initiation of any Covered Activity and when these materials are subsequently buried, capped, or otherwise used or moved in any way.

obl-1304.title: Do not move parked vehicles or equipment until the biologist or monitor has checked under and around them.
obl-1304.trigger: Before moving vehicles and equipment during initial ground disturbance

locators.excerpt: The Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall also check any potential hiding places in the Project construction site, such as cracks, crevices, or cavities; stockpiles that have been left for more than 24 hours where cracks or crevices may have formed; and under or around vehicles and equipment before they are moved.

obl-1305.title: Do not use plastic monofilament netting or netting with bound or stitched cross joints (straw wattles, fiber rolls, erosion blankets) for erosion control; fiber rolls and erosion mesh must be loose-weave, not fused or welded at the intersections.
obl-1305.trigger: All erosion control materials in the Project Area

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall not use plastic monofilament netting or similar material such as nylon or netting with cross joins that are bound or stitched (such as straw wattles, fiber rolls, or erosion-control blankets) in the Project Area for erosion control to avoid entanglement, strangling, or entrapment of Covered Species.

Erosion control may not use netting made with plastic monofilament or similar materials or netting with cross joints that are bound or stitched (such as straw wattles, fiber rolls, or erosion control blankets), which could trap wildlife including snakes or birds. Fiber rolls or erosion-control mesh shall be made of loose-weave mesh that is not fused at the intersections of the weave, or other products without welded weaves.

obl-1306.title: Let the animal escape or be relocated by the Designated Biologist before moving, capping, burying, or using the structure.

locators.excerpt: If Project personnel detect Covered Species or other wildlife within a pipe, culvert, debris pile, or similar structure, they shall notify the Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) and allow the animal to safely escape or be relocated by the Designated Biologist(s) outside of the Project construction site before moving, capping, burying, or utilizing the structure.

obl-1307.title: Do not start equipment or move materials left overnight until the biologist or monitor has inspected them.

locators.excerpt: All construction equipment, or construction materials left overnight in areas that may be occupied by wildlife shall be inspected by the Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) prior to initiation of any Covered Activity within a Project construction site, to prevent inadvertent entrapment of Covered Species during construction.

obl-1308.title: Install wildlife fencing where applicable to keep wildlife out of dangerous construction areas, placed so wildlife can still move along riparian corridors.
obl-1308.trigger: Construction areas such as roads and facilities near riparian corridors

locators.excerpt: Design will include wildlife fencing where applicable to prevent wildlife access to construction areas that may be dangerous for wildlife, such as roads and other facilities. Fencing will also be designed and placed in a manner that facilitates wildlife movement through or between the riparian banks and corridors during constriction.

obl-1309.title: Repair damaged exclusion fence within 24 hours of finding the damage.
obl-1309.trigger: Within 24 hours of discovering fence damage
monitorSigns: fence damage open more than 24 hours

locators.excerpt: Repairs to the exclusion fence will be made within 24 hours of discovery of damage.

obl-1310.title: If you find wildlife in a pipe, culvert, debris pile, or similar structure, tell the Designated Biologist or Biological Monitor.
obl-1310.trigger: Any wildlife found in a stored structure

locators.excerpt: If Project personnel detect Covered Species or other wildlife within a pipe, culvert, debris pile, or similar structure, they shall notify the Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) and allow the animal to safely escape or be relocated by the Designated Biologist(s) outside of the Project construction site before moving, capping, burying, or utilizing the structure.

obl-1311.title: Once the animal has left or been relocated, cap the structure ends securely right after inspection, under biologist or monitor supervision.

locators.excerpt: Conduct tree removal between September 15 and October 31 to the maximum extent practicable, which corresponds to a time period when bats would not likely have entered winter hibernation and would not be caring for flightless young. If weather conditions remain conducive to regular bat activity beyond October 31, later tree removal may be considered in consultation with CDFW. f.

Eviction will take place during weather and temperature conditions conducive to bat activity (a warm night when nighttime lows are not less than 45°F and during dry weather conditions). v.

obl-1483.title: Conduct at least one daytime inspection in January or February for hibernacula, using a fiber-optic probe in crevices where needed.

locators.excerpt: At least one daytime site inspection should be conducted in January or February to determine if winter hibernacula or overwintering habitat for bats are present. Crevice-roosting species typically roost deep in crevices in the winter, and they may not be visible during winter inspections. Therefore, visual surveys, in combination with the use of an extendable fiber-optic camera probe to view inside crevices may be required for some bridges, overpasses, or structures.

obl-1484.title: Survey under the entire structure where practicable and record habitat type, roosting features, bat sign by feature, roost dimensions, and a sketch of features and activity.

locators.excerpt: Survey under the entire bridge or overpass, as practicable. b. Identify the type of habitat present (e.g., day and night-roosting habitat). c. Describe the features that provide the roosting habitat (e.g., expansion joints, hinges, closure pours). d. Describe signs of bat use with respect to each habitat feature, if present. e. Include a sketch of the structure showing the locations of suitable habitat features and bat activity in each feature, based on sign or visual detection. Estimate dimensions (i.e., length, width, depth) of each roost habitat type.

obl-1485.title: Monitor occupied roosts within 300 feet of night construction daily, starting 45 minutes before sunset, for at least 4 hours or until unoccupied.

High-value habitat features (e.g., large tree cavities, basal hollows, loose or peeling bark, larger snags, palm trees with intact thatch) will be identified and the area around these features searched for bats and bat sign (e.g., guano, culled insect parts, staining). Riparian woodland, orchards, and stands of mature broadleaf trees should be considered potential habitat for solitary foliage-roosting bat species.

obl-1488.title: Biologists must carry out or oversee eviction tasks.

obl-1490.title: The assessment must be done by a qualified biologist with knowledge of California bats, habitat identification experience, and full-spectrum acoustic experience.

obl-1491.title: About 2 years before surface construction or demolition on a bridge, overpass, or structure, conduct a daytime search for bat sign on and under it, listening with a bat detector, in weather that allows a thorough look.
obl-1491.trigger: About 2 years before surface construction at each structure

locators.excerpt: Approximately 2 years prior to surface construction, including demolition, beginning on a bridge, overpass or a structure, a qualified biologist, with knowledge of the natural history of California bats, experience identifying habitat, and experience using full-spectrum acoustic equipment, will conduct a daytime search for bat sign (e.g., guano, urine staining, culled insect parts) on or underneath the bridge, overpass, or structure. Biologists conducting daytime surveys will listen for audible social calls through the use of bat detector, which converts ultrasonic echolocation emissions into frequencies audible to humans in real-time. This field assessment can be performed during any time of year, provided that weather conditions or local flooding do not affect the biologist’s ability to do a thorough evaluation.

obl-1492.title: If bat sign is found, do evening emergence surveys from half an hour before sunset to 1 to 2 hours after, on at least 2 nights in the construction season, using the bridge emergence methods.

obl-1497.title: In the maternity season (generally March 1 to August 31, timing set by the biologist), do a daytime inspection for bats and high-use areas, plus a night roost inspection 2 to 3 hours after sunset if special-status species are suspected.

While daytime inspections are usually sufficient to determine the presence of night-roosting habitat, nighttime roost inspections (2 to 3 hours after sunset) will be conducted if special-status species are suspected to occur. ii.

obl-1498.title: Photograph the structure with a scaled high-resolution camera: signage, side view of span, abutments, soffit, joints, hinges, closure pours, piers, weep holes, and every type of guano and staining.

locators.excerpt: Use the preferred method of documenting conditions in the survey area, including evidence of bats: a digital camera capable of capturing high- resolution images that provide scale. At a minimum, the photographs should document the bridge or overpass signage (with identification number, post mile, and bridge or overpass name [if applicable]); a right-angle (i.e., side perspective) view showing the entire span; the abutments and any details associated with potential roosting habitat; representative images of the soffit, expansion joints, hinges, and closure pours; how the piers support the deck; representative weep holes documenting the presence or absence of screens; and images of various bat sign, such as urine staining and guano on the structure. g. obl-1504.title: Follow up with a dusk emergence count on a warm (lows 45 F or above), dry night from about 15 minutes before to 1 hour after sunset, with surveyors on non-overlapping stations where exits are backlit, using night vision if possible.

locators.excerpt: Conduct a follow-up dusk emergence count survey. Dusk emergence count surveys should be conducted on a warm night when nighttime lows are not less than 45°F and during dry weather conditions. Surveys should be conducted from approximately 15 minutes before sunset to 1 hour after sunset. Prior to any dusk emergence count, the biologist should understand the primary locations where bats are day roosting so these locations can be targeted during the emergence count. Depending on the locations and number of roost exit points, multiple surveyors may be needed. Surveyors should each be assigned a specific area that does not overlap with other surveyors’ locations. Surveyors should station themselves such that roost exit points are backlit by the sky. If possible, night-vision goggles should be used to assist in the counting. iii.
