obl-1640.title: Continuously monitor hydroacoustics during pile driving, drilled shaft construction, riprap placement and dredging, with at least two calibrated hydrophones per site placed at least 1 meter deep, one at 10 meters and one at the SEL cumulative limit distance, following Caltrans 2020 guidance.

locators.excerpt: The underwater sound abatement plan shall include a requirement for continual hydroacoustic monitoring of in-water Covered Activities, including: impact or vibratory pile driving, drilled shaft (also known as castin-drilled hole piles) construction, riprap placement, and dredging. During in- water Covered Activities, conducted in the Construction Work Window (Condition of Approval 11.31.2), Permittee shall implement the CDFW-approved underwater sound abatement plan to verify that any sound transmitted to the water column is below the applicable and interim underwater noise thresholds established for injury of fish provided in California Department of Transportation 2020 Technical Guidance for the Assessment of Hydroacoustic Effects of Pile Driving on Fish 36 at 10 meters from source: • Injury threshold for fish of all sizes includes a peak sound pressure level (SPL) of 206 dB relative to 1 micropascal; • Injury threshold for fish less than 2 grams is 183 dB relative to 1 micropascal cumulative sound exposure level (SEL cumulative ); and • Injury threshold for fish greater than or equal to 2 grams is 187 dB relative to 1 micropascal SEL cumulative . Procedures for hydroacoustic monitoring shall be consistent with the California Department of Transportation 2020 Technical Guidance for the Assessment of Hydroacoustic Effects of Pile Driving on Fish. Hydroacoustic monitoring shall at a minimum consist of two hydrophones used at each site to monitor in-water Covered Activities. Hydrophones shall be calibrated prior to deployment and maintained with best management practices. All hydrophones shall be placed at least 1 meter below the water surface, preferably at mid-depth in the water column, and will have a direct line of acoustic transmission through the water column to the in-water Covered Activity. The first hydrophone shall be positioned at 10 meters from the site. The second hydrophone shall be positioned at or near the proposed SEL cumulative limit to measure whether threshold distances are met.

locators.excerpt: Diversions shall not reduce Sacramento River bypass flows to less than 10,000 cfs. • Sacramento River flow at Freeport above 15,000 cfs: Diversions shall not exceed 2,000 cfs plus 80% of Sacramento River flow at Freeport above 15,000 cfs.

obl-1805.title: Do not let diversions drop bypass flow below 10,000 cfs.
obl-1805.trigger: June after the off-ramp, after 15 consecutive days of bypass flow above 20,000 cfs, Freeport flow 10,900 to 15,000 cfs

locators.excerpt: Diversions shall not reduce Sacramento River bypass flows to less than 10,000 cfs. • Sacramento River flow at Freeport above 15,000 cfs: Diversions shall not exceed 2,000 cfs plus 80% of Sacramento River flow at Freeport above 15,000 cfs.

obl-1806.title: In June, keep operating to COA 11.111 criteria until the salmon presence off-ramp criteria are met, then shift to the COA 11.111.1 June criteria.
monitorSigns: did not shift after off-ramp declared

locators.excerpt: Condition of Approval 11.111 allows for risk assessments and real-time decision-making when flows in the Sacramento River are between 20,000 – 35,000 cfs (December – February) or above 35,000 cfs. • June: o Before salmon presence off-ramp (Condition of Approval 11.111.6): Default operations shall adhere to operating criteria described in Condition of Approval 11.111. o After a salmon presence offramp (Condition of Approval 11.111.6): Default operations shall adhere to June operations criteria in Condition of Approval 11.111.1.

After June 1 default operations as described in Condition of Approval 11.111.2 shall shift from Condition of Approval 11.111 to Condition of Approval 11.111.1 when the following criteria have been met, pursuant to the collaborative decision- making process in Condition of Approval 11.111.5: o 95% of CHNWR and CHNSR have exited the Delta past Chipps Island as determined through Condition of Approval 11.111.5; o Daily mean water temperature at Prisoner’s Point (CDEC station PPT) is > 22.2 o C for seven days (does not have to be consecutive) in June.

obl-1807.title: Keep total north Delta diversions at or below 10% of the 25-hour running average Sacramento River flow.
obl-1807.trigger: Flow dominated: 25-hour running average Sacramento River flow above 35,000 cfs

locators.excerpt: Flow Dominated: When the 25-hour running average Sacramento River flow is maintained above 35,000 cfs, the Sacramento River near Hood is flow dominated. • Total Project diversions from the north Delta intakes shall not exceed ten percent (10 %) of the 25-hour running average Sacramento River flow at any time.

obl-1808.title: With Freeport flow above 20,000 cfs, do not let diversions drop bypass flow below 17,180 cfs.
obl-1808.trigger: June after the off-ramp, Freeport flow above 20,000 cfs

locators.excerpt: In June, after the operating criteria (Condition of Approval 11.111) end as determined by Condition of Approval 11.111.6, allowable NDDs shall be subject to the following criteria. Sacramento River bypass flow shall be measured using the gage required by Condition of Approval 10.20.1: • Sacramento River flow at Freeport between 10,900 cfs – 15,000 cfs: Diversions shall not exceed 900 cfs. • Sacramento River flow at Freeport between 15,000 – 17,000 cfs: Diversions shall not exceed 6% of the Sacramento River flow at Freeport. • Sacramento River flow at Freeport between 17,000 – 20,000 cfs: Diversions shall not exceed 1,020 cfs plus 40% of Sacramento River flow above 17,000 cfs. • Sacramento River flow at Freeport above 20,000 cfs: Diversions shall not reduce Sacramento River bypass flows to less than 17,180 cfs.

obl-1809.title: Do not divert from the north Delta intakes while the Delta Cross Channel Gates are open.
obl-1809.trigger: All flow conditions: tidally dominated, transitional and flow dominated

locators.excerpt: Tidally Dominated: When the 25-hour running average Sacramento River flow is below 20,000 cfs, the Sacramento River near Hood is tidally dominated. • Permittee shall not divert from the north Delta intakes while the Delta Cross Channel Gates are open.

Transitional: When the 25-hour running average Sacramento River flow is maintained above 20,000 cfs, but less than 35,000 cfs, the Sacramento River near Hood is transitional. • Permittee shall not divert from the north Delta intakes while the Delta Cross Channel Gates are open.

Flow Dominated: When the 25-hour running average Sacramento River flow is maintained above 35,000 cfs, the Sacramento River near Hood is flow dominated. • Permittee shall not divert from the north Delta intakes while the Delta Cross Channel Gates are open. •

obl-1810.title: Divert between 6% and 10% of the 25-hour average flow only when approved through COA 11.111.5 after a risk assessment shows the biological criteria will not be exceeded.
obl-1810.trigger: Transitional conditions, when diversions above 6% are proposed
monitorSigns: higher rate with no risk assessment

locators.excerpt: Total north Delta intake diversions may take between 6% - 10% of the 25-hour running average Sacramento River flow, if approved through Condition of Approval 11.111.5 in response to a risk assessment (Condition of Approval 11.111.3), demonstrating that increased diversions will not cause Covered Fish Species Biological Criteria to be exceeded (Conditions of Approval 11.115, 11.116, and 11.117).

obl-1811.title: Divert only while an instantaneous bypass flow of 10,000 cfs is maintained below intake C.
monitorSigns: instantaneous bypass under 10,000 cfs while diverting

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall not divert from the north Delta intakes unless an instantaneous bypass of Sacramento River flow of 10,000 cfs is maintained below the north Delta intake C.

obl-1812.title: Limit shifting of exports from south to north Delta facilities by the D-1641 E/I ratio, the operating criteria of COA 11.109, 11.111, 11.112, and 11.114, keeping combined south Delta diversions above 3,000 cfs, or keeping total SWP diversions at or below 7,180 cfs except for carriage water savings.
monitorSigns: south Delta exports at or below 3,000 cfs after shift

locators.excerpt: Shifting of exports from south Delta export facilities to north Delta export facilities during balanced conditions shall be limited by the following: • Export/inflow (E/I) ratio in D-1641; • Operating criteria described in Conditions of Approval 11.109, 11.111, 11.112, and 11.114; • Maintaining combined SWP and CVP south Delta diversions greater than 3,000 cfs; or • Maintaining total combined SWP diversion at the south Delta and north Delta diversions less than or equal to 7,180 cfs, excluding exceptions for carriage water savings.

obl-1813.title: From December through May, operate by default to COA 11.111 operating criteria.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall implement operating criteria according to the following annual schedule: • November: Based on real-time operations as described in Conditions of Approval 11.111.3 and 11.111.5, if CDFW determines it is necessary based on an assessment of risk to Covered Fish Species, relative to the Covered Fish Species Biological Criteria (Conditions of Approval 11.115, 11.116, and 11.117), Permittee shall adhere to operating criteria described in Condition of Approval 11.111. • December – May: Default operations shall adhere to operating criteria described in Condition of Approval 11.111.

obl-1814.title: Meet all velocity requirements and diversion criteria of COA 11.109, 11.111, 11.112, 11.113, and 11.114 during Phase 2.
monitorSigns: velocity or diversion criterion exceeded in Phase 2

locators.excerpt: During Phase 2 Operations, Permittee shall adhere to all velocity requirements and diversion criteria described in Conditions of Approval 11.109, 11.111, 11.112, 11.113, and 11.114.

obl-1815.title: Do not divert from the north Delta intakes from March 1 through May 31.
obl-1815.trigger: Tidally dominated conditions, March 1 to May 31
monitorSigns: diversion in April under tidal conditions

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall not divert from the north Delta intakes from March 1 through May 31.

obl-1816.title: With Freeport flow between 10,900 and 15,000 cfs, keep diversions at or below 900 cfs plus 50% of flow above 11,000 cfs.
obl-1816.trigger: June after the off-ramp, after 15 consecutive days of bypass flow above 20,000 cfs
monitorSigns: diversion over the 900 cfs plus 50% cap

locators.excerpt: After 15 consecutive days of Sacramento River bypass flow above 20,000 cfs, as measured using the gage required by Condition of Approval 10.20.1, allowable north Delta diversions shall be subject to the following criteria: • Sacramento River flow at Freeport between 10,900 – 15,000 cfs: Diversions shall not exceed 900 cfs plus 50% of the Sacramento River flow at Freeport above 11,000 cfs.

obl-1817.title: Divert between 10% and 12% of the 25-hour average flow only when approved through COA 11.111.5 after a risk assessment shows the biological criteria will not be exceeded.
obl-1817.trigger: Flow dominated conditions, when diversions above 10% are proposed
monitorSigns: diversion above 10% with no approved risk assessment

locators.excerpt: Total north Delta intake diversions may take between 10% - 12% of the 25-hour running average Sacramento River flow, if approved through Condition of Approval 11.111.5 in response to a risk assessment (Condition of Approval 11.111.3), demonstrating that increased diversions will not cause Covered Fish Species Biological Criteria to be exceeded (Conditions of Approval 11.115, 11.116, and 11.117).

obl-1818.title: Meet all velocity requirements and diversion criteria of COA 11.109 and 11.111 during Phase 1.
monitorSigns: velocity or diversion criterion exceeded in Phase 1

locators.excerpt: During Phase 1 Operations, Permittee shall adhere to all velocity requirements and diversion criteria described in Conditions of Approval 11.109 and 11.111.

obl-1819.title: With Freeport flow between 10,900 and 15,000 cfs, keep diversions at or below 900 cfs.
obl-1819.trigger: June after the off-ramp, Freeport flow 10,900 to 15,000 cfs

locators.excerpt: In June, after the operating criteria (Condition of Approval 11.111) end as determined by Condition of Approval 11.111.6, allowable NDDs shall be subject to the following criteria. Sacramento River bypass flow shall be measured using the gage required by Condition of Approval 10.20.1: • Sacramento River flow at Freeport between 10,900 cfs – 15,000 cfs: Diversions shall not exceed 900 cfs. • Sacramento River flow at Freeport between 15,000 – 17,000 cfs: Diversions shall not exceed 6% of the Sacramento River flow at Freeport. • Sacramento River flow at Freeport between 17,000 – 20,000 cfs: Diversions shall not exceed 1,020 cfs plus 40% of Sacramento River flow above 17,000 cfs. • Sacramento River flow at Freeport above 20,000 cfs: Diversions shall not reduce Sacramento River bypass flows to less than 17,180 cfs.

obl-1820.title: In October, divert only while a 3-day average bypass of 7,000 cfs is maintained downstream of intake C.

locators.excerpt: October 1 - October 31: o Permittee shall not divert from the north Delta intakes unless a 3-day average bypass of Sacramento River flow of 7,000 cfs is maintained downstream of the north Delta Intake C at the gage required by Condition of Approval 10.20.1.

obl-1821.title: Do not divert any water through the north Delta intakes during the Bethany Reservoir Pumping Plant Contractor's Test.
obl-1821.trigger: During the Bethany Reservoir Pumping Plant Contractor's Test

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall not divert any water through the north Delta intakes while it is conducting the Bethany Reservoir Pumping Plant Contractor’s Test (see Section 19.2.1 in the Project Description).

obl-1822.title: Do not change upstream reservoir operations to move additional stored water through the north Delta intakes.
monitorSigns: reservoir release increased to feed north Delta intakes

locators.excerpt: SWP upstream facilities will continue to be operated to meet regulatory, environmental, and contractual obligations consistent with existing SWP operations (as of the date of issuance of this ITP) and Permittee shall not change upstream reservoir operations to move additional stored water through the north Delta intakes.

obl-1823.title: Do not divert at the north Delta intakes when combined south Delta exports are at or below 3,000 cfs.
obl-1823.trigger: Balanced conditions declared while the CVP and SWP are withdrawing from storage
monitorSigns: NDD running with south Delta exports at 3,000 cfs or less

locators.excerpt: When balanced conditions are declared, consistent with COA, and the CVP and SWP are collectively withdrawing water from storage, Permittee shall not conduct diversions at the north Delta intakes when combined south Delta exports are less than or equal to 3,000 cfs.

obl-1824.title: From November 1 to July 30, divert only while an instantaneous bypass of 10,000 cfs is maintained downstream of intake C at the COA 10.20.1 gage.
monitorSigns: instantaneous bypass under 10,000 cfs while diverting

locators.excerpt: November 1 – July 30: The following criteria within Condition of Approval 11.111 shall be implemented from November 1 – July 30 without exception: o Permittee shall not divert from the north Delta intakes unless an instantaneous bypass of Sacramento River flow of 10,000 cfs is maintained downstream of the north Delta intake C at the gage required by Condition of Approval 10.20.1. o Permittee shall not divert from the north Delta intakes unless a minimum bypass 25- hour running average Sacramento River flow of 6,000 cfs is maintained downstream of the north Delta Intake C at the gage required by Condition of Approval 10.20.1. • August 1 – September 30: •

obl-1825.title: Limit combined SWP diversions at the south Delta facilities and north Delta intakes to the amount allowed under COA 11.114.

locators.excerpt: To accomplish this, Permittee shall limit combined SWP water diversions at the existing south Delta facilities and the north Delta intakes to the amount allowed under Condition of Approval 11.114.

obl-1826.title: In November, follow COA 11.111 operating criteria when CDFW determines it is necessary from the risk assessment.
obl-1826.trigger: November, when CDFW determines it is necessary
monitorSigns: November CDFW determination, criteria not applied

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall implement operating criteria according to the following annual schedule: • November: Based on real-time operations as described in Conditions of Approval 11.111.3 and 11.111.5, if CDFW determines it is necessary based on an assessment of risk to Covered Fish Species, relative to the Covered Fish Species Biological Criteria (Conditions of Approval 11.115, 11.116, and 11.117), Permittee shall adhere to operating criteria described in Condition of Approval 11.111. • December – May: Default operations shall adhere to operating criteria described in Condition of Approval 11.111.

obl-1827.title: Do not make additional stored water releases from Lake Oroville or other upstream reservoirs for south Delta exports, except for carriage water savings, flood control, or instream flow requirements not needed for in-Delta regulatory requirements.
monitorSigns: added release for export with no listed exception

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall not make additional stored water releases, beyond those possible or required as of the date of issuance of this ITP without the use of the Project, from the Lake Oroville Complex, or any other of its existing upstream reservoirs for the purpose of south Delta SWP exports, except: • A shift in exports from south Delta facilities to the north Delta intakes that results in a carriage water savings (Condition of Approval 11.113); or • Upstream releases for flood control; or • Upstream releases required to meet instream flow requirements that are not needed to meet in-Delta regulatory requirements.

obl-1828.title: Divert no more than 3% of the 25-hour running average flow from March 1 through May 31.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall not divert more than 3% of the 25-hour running average Sacramento River flow from the north Delta intakes from March 1 through May 31.

obl-1829.title: From August 1 to September 30, divert only while a 3-day average bypass of 5,000 cfs is maintained downstream of intake C.

locators.excerpt: • o Permittee shall not divert from the north Delta intakes unless a 3-day average bypass of Sacramento River flow of 5,000 cfs is maintained downstream of the north Delta Intake C at the gage required by Condition of Approval 10.20.1.

obl-1830.title: With Freeport flow between 15,000 and 17,000 cfs, keep diversions at or below 6% of Freeport flow.
obl-1830.trigger: June after the off-ramp, Freeport flow 15,000 to 17,000 cfs

locators.excerpt: In June, after the operating criteria (Condition of Approval 11.111) end as determined by Condition of Approval 11.111.6, allowable NDDs shall be subject to the following criteria. Sacramento River bypass flow shall be measured using the gage required by Condition of Approval 10.20.1: • Sacramento River flow at Freeport between 10,900 cfs – 15,000 cfs: Diversions shall not exceed 900 cfs. • Sacramento River flow at Freeport between 15,000 – 17,000 cfs: Diversions shall not exceed 6% of the Sacramento River flow at Freeport. • Sacramento River flow at Freeport between 17,000 – 20,000 cfs: Diversions shall not exceed 1,020 cfs plus 40% of Sacramento River flow above 17,000 cfs. • Sacramento River flow at Freeport above 20,000 cfs: Diversions shall not reduce Sacramento River bypass flows to less than 17,180 cfs.

obl-1831.title: After the June off-ramp and in July, follow COA 11.111 criteria when CDFW determines it is necessary from the risk assessment.
obl-1831.trigger: June after the off-ramp and July, when CDFW determines it is necessary

locators.excerpt: Based on real-time operations as described in Conditions of Approval 11.111.3 and 11.111.5, if CDFW determines it is necessary based on an assessment of risk to Covered Fish Species relative to the Covered Fish Species Biological Criteria (Conditions of Approval 11.115, 11.116, and 11.117), Permittee shall adhere to Diversion Criteria described in Condition of Approval 11.111. • July: Based on real-time operations as described in Conditions of Approval 11.111.3 and 11.111.5, if CDFW determines it is necessary based on an assessment of risk to Covered Fish Species, relative to the Covered Fish Species Biological Criteria (Conditions of Approval 11.115, 11.116, and 11.117), Permittee shall adhere to operating criteria described in Condition of Approval 11.111.

obl-1832.title: Keep total north Delta diversions at or below 6% of instantaneous Sacramento River flow.

locators.excerpt: Total Project diversions from the north Delta intakes shall not exceed six percent (6%) of the Sacramento River instantaneous flow.

obl-1833.title: Keep total SWP diversions from south and north Delta intakes at or below 10,350 cfs daily average.
monitorSigns: daily average SWP diversion over 10,350 cfs

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall operate the north Delta intakes at all times to ensure that total SWP diversions from both south and north Delta intakes do not exceed 10,350 cfs on a daily average.

obl-1834.title: From November 1 to July 30, divert only while a 25-hour running average bypass of 6,000 cfs is maintained downstream of intake C at the COA 10.20.1 gage.

locators.excerpt: November 1 – July 30: The following criteria within Condition of Approval 11.111 shall be implemented from November 1 – July 30 without exception: o Permittee shall not divert from the north Delta intakes unless an instantaneous bypass of Sacramento River flow of 10,000 cfs is maintained downstream of the north Delta intake C at the gage required by Condition of Approval 10.20.1. o Permittee shall not divert from the north Delta intakes unless a minimum bypass 25- hour running average Sacramento River flow of 6,000 cfs is maintained downstream of the north Delta Intake C at the gage required by Condition of Approval 10.20.1. • August 1 – September 30: •

obl-1835.title: Keep total north Delta diversions at or below 6% of the 25-hour running average flow unless a higher rate is approved through COA 11.111.5.

locators.excerpt: Total Project diversions from the north Delta intakes shall not exceed six percent (6%) of the 25-hour running average Sacramento River flow at any time, unless otherwise approved through Condition of Approval 11.111.5.

obl-1836.title: With Freeport flow between 17,000 and 20,000 cfs, keep diversions at or below 1,020 cfs plus 40% of flow above 17,000 cfs.
obl-1836.trigger: June after the off-ramp, Freeport flow 17,000 to 20,000 cfs
monitorSigns: diversion over the 1,020 cfs plus 40% cap

locators.excerpt: In June, after the operating criteria (Condition of Approval 11.111) end as determined by Condition of Approval 11.111.6, allowable NDDs shall be subject to the following criteria. Sacramento River bypass flow shall be measured using the gage required by Condition of Approval 10.20.1: • Sacramento River flow at Freeport between 10,900 cfs – 15,000 cfs: Diversions shall not exceed 900 cfs. • Sacramento River flow at Freeport between 15,000 – 17,000 cfs: Diversions shall not exceed 6% of the Sacramento River flow at Freeport. • Sacramento River flow at Freeport between 17,000 – 20,000 cfs: Diversions shall not exceed 1,020 cfs plus 40% of Sacramento River flow above 17,000 cfs. • Sacramento River flow at Freeport above 20,000 cfs: Diversions shall not reduce Sacramento River bypass flows to less than 17,180 cfs.

obl-1837.title: Divert only while a 25-hour running average bypass flow of at least 6,000 cfs is maintained downstream of intake C.

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall not divert from the north Delta intakes unless a minimum bypass 25-hour running average Sacramento River flow of 6,000 cfs is maintained downstream of the north Delta intake C.

obl-1838.title: Measure Freeport flow with the 25-hour running average of USGS gage 11447650 and bypass flow with the COA 10.20.1 gage for June criteria.
obl-1838.trigger: June, after the salmon presence off-ramp
monitorSigns: instantaneous value used instead of 25-hour average

locators.excerpt: Sacramento River flow at Freeport shall be measured using the 25-hour running average of USGS Gage Number 11447650. Sacramento River bypass flow shall be measured using the gage required by Condition of Approval 10.20.1: • Sacramento River flow at Freeport between 10,900 cfs – 15,000 cfs: Diversions shall not exceed 900 cfs. • Sacramento River flow at Freeport between 15,000 – 17,000 cfs: Diversions shall not exceed 6% of the Sacramento River flow at Freeport. • Sacramento River flow at Freeport between 17,000 – 20,000 cfs: Diversions shall not exceed 1,020 cfs plus 40% of Sacramento River flow above 17,000 cfs. • Sacramento River flow at Freeport above 20,000 cfs: Diversions shall not reduce Sacramento River bypass flows to less than 17,180 cfs.

obl-1839.title: Measure Sacramento River flow with the gage required by COA 10.20.1.
obl-1839.trigger: All flow determinations for diversion criteria
monitorSigns: flow taken from a different gage

locators.excerpt: Sacramento River flow shall be measured using the gage required by Condition of Approval 10.20.1.

obl-1840.title: Close the gate behind any screen unit at intake B or C that is not fully functional, and do not divert through it.
obl-1840.trigger: At all times at north Delta intakes B and C

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall close the gate behind a screen unit and not divert water through that screen unit at north Delta intake B or C at any time unless the screen unit is fully functional.

obl-1841.title: Divert at north Delta intakes B and C only when the fish screens are operating to the CDFW 2000 and NMFS 2023 screening criteria.
obl-1841.trigger: All diversions at north Delta intakes B and C
monitorSigns: diverting with screen out of criteria

locators.excerpt: To minimize impingement and entrainment of Covered Fish Species, Permittee shall only divert when the north Delta intake B and C fish screens are operating according to the CDFW 2000 Fish Screening Criteria and the NMFS 2023 Anadromous Salmonid Passage Design Manual.

obl-1842.title: Keep approach velocity at or below 0.2 feet per second across each fish screen.
obl-1842.trigger: All diversions at the north Delta intakes
monitorSigns: Va reading over 0.2 fps on a screen

locators.excerpt: 50, 51 In order to comply with CDFW and NMFS fish screening criteria, Permittee shall operate the north Delta intakes not to exceed the maximum uniform approach velocity (V a ) of 0.2 feet per second across the wetted surface of each individual fish screen.

obl-1843.title: Spread diversions across as many intakes and screens as possible, opening more screens than the minimum, to keep local approach velocity low.
obl-1843.trigger: During all diversions at the north Delta intakes
monitorSigns: high local Va at one screen

locators.excerpt: During diversions at the north Delta intakes, Permittee shall minimize localized V a by spreading the diversion as much as possible across intakes and fish screens, and by opening more fish screens than would be minimally required to meet the V a criterion.

obl-1844.title: Keep sweeping velocity at or above 0.4 feet per second across each fish screen.
obl-1844.trigger: All diversions at the north Delta intakes

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall operate the north Delta intakes to maintain a minimum uniform V s of 0.4 feet per second across the wetted surface of each individual fish screen.

obl-1845.title: Run regular hydraulic testing of north Delta intake fish screens under COA 10.27 to confirm approach and sweeping velocities meet the limits.
monitorSigns: test results missing Va or Vs

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall conduct regular hydraulic testing in accordance with Condition of Approval 10.27 (Hydraulic Testing for Velocity Requirements) to ensure compliance with V a and V s requirements identified in this Condition of Approval.

obl-1846.title: Ensure Phase 1 and Phase 2 operations do not entrain juvenile CHNWR or CHNSR into the north Delta intakes.
monitorSigns: juvenile salmon found behind intake screens

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall ensure that Phase 1 and Phase 2 operations do not result in entrainment of juvenile CHNWR or CHNSR into the north Delta intakes.

obl-1847.title: Notify CDFW in writing within one business day if fish screens are not operational at either north Delta intake.
obl-1847.trigger: Within one business day of screens becoming non-operational
monitorSigns: screen outage logged, no written CDFW notice within 1 business day

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall notify CDFW within one business day in writing if the fish screens are not operational at either north Delta intake.

obl-1848.title: Operate to the decision reached by WOMT representatives or the alternative agreed by the Directors.
obl-1848.trigger: Once a resolution or Director consensus is reached

locators.excerpt: If a resolution is reached, Permittee shall operate consistent with the decision regarding Project operations made by Permittee and CDFW WOMT representatives. If consensus is reached, Permittee shall implement the alternative action.

obl-1849.title: If the Directors cannot agree and CDFW issues a written operational decision, implement it.
obl-1849.trigger: When the CDFW Director requires a written operational decision

locators.excerpt: If the Directors do not reach a resolution on operations, the CDFW Director may require Permittee to implement an operational decision provided by CDFW in writing. Permittee shall implement CDFW’s operational decision.

obl-1850.title: Share all available biological, abiotic, and operational information through the NDDMT to inform discussions between the Permittee and CDFW WOMT representatives.

locators.excerpt: The NDDMT shall share and discuss all available biological, abiotic, and operational information to inform discussions among Permittee and CDFW WOMT representatives as established in the 2024 ITP.

obl-1851.title: Give CDFW all raw data and modeling used by the NDDMT within ten days of a request.
obl-1851.trigger: Within ten days of a CDFW request
monitorSigns: CDFW data request open past 10 days

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall make all raw data and modeling utilized as part of NDDMT available to CDFW within ten days of a request.

obl-1852.title: Have the NDDMT begin risk assessments the last week of October and meet weekly through November.
obl-1852.trigger: Last week of October through November
monitorSigns: no risk assessment started late October

locators.excerpt: The NDDMT shall begin to conduct risk assessments the last week of October, to look ahead to conditions starting in November, and meet weekly throughout November.

obl-1853.title: Keep Phase 1 Operations to one calendar year unless CDFW approves an extension, and never let Phase 1 and Phase 2 together run past two calendar years.
monitorSigns: Phase 1 past one year with no CDFW extension
Phase 1 and 2 combined over two years

locators.excerpt: Phase 1 Operations are authorized for no more than one calendar year. Permittee may extend the time period of Phase 1 Operations with CDFW approval but shall not extend the total duration of Phase 1 and Phase 2 Operations beyond two calendar years.

obl-1854.title: Convene weekly NDDMT meetings in July to conduct risk assessments.
obl-1854.trigger: Each week of July during Phase 1 and Phase 2 operations
monitorSigns: July week with no NDDMT meeting

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall convene weekly NDDMT meetings in July to conduct risk assessments.

obl-1855.title: Use new science, modeling, and data to inform real-time risk assessments of operations on Covered Fish Species.

locators.excerpt: This new science, modeling, and data shall be used to inform real-time assessments of risk of impacts of Project operations on Covered Fish Species and the potential to exceed biological criteria.

obl-1856.title: Determine through the COA 11.111.5 process when 95% of CHNWR and CHNSR have passed Chipps Island and Prisoner's Point daily mean temperature has exceeded 22.2 C on seven June days.
monitorSigns: off-ramp declared without the 95% exit finding
fewer than seven days over 22.2 C

locators.excerpt: After June 1 default operations as described in Condition of Approval 11.111.2 shall shift from Condition of Approval 11.111 to Condition of Approval 11.111.1 when the following criteria have been met, pursuant to the collaborative decision- making process in Condition of Approval 11.111.5: o 95% of CHNWR and CHNSR have exited the Delta past Chipps Island as determined through Condition of Approval 11.111.5; o Daily mean water temperature at Prisoner’s Point (CDEC station PPT) is > 22.2 o C for seven days (does not have to be consecutive) in June.

obl-1857.title: Begin sharing real-time operations data with CDFW under the approved process when Phase 1 Operations start.
obl-1857.trigger: From the initiation of Phase 1 Operations
monitorSigns: Phase 1 started, no data shared with CDFW

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall begin implementation of the information sharing process with CDFW upon initiation of Phase 1 Operations.

obl-1858.title: If WOMT representatives cannot agree, have the DWR Director confer with the CDFW Director on an alternative action.
obl-1858.trigger: When WOMT representatives do not reach a resolution

locators.excerpt: If Permittee and CDFW WOMT representatives do not reach a resolution, the Director of DWR shall confer with the Director of CDFW to determine if there is an alternative action that will be mutually agreeable.

obl-1859.title: Monitor and manage Project operations in close coordination with CDFW staff during Phase 1 and Phase 2.
monitorSigns: operating changes with no CDFW coordination record

locators.excerpt: Permittee shall monitor and manage Project operations in close coordination with CDFW staff during Phase 1 and Phase 2 operations as described in Condition of Approval 11.110.

obl-1860.title: Change risk assessment data sources or modeling only to match best available science and with CDFW approval.
obl-1860.trigger: Whenever a listed data source or model is changed

obl-1991.title: Use watertight forms and containment structures for raw concrete, wash water and other contaminants so they cannot enter surface waters or sensitive habitats.

locators.excerpt: The SPCCPs shall include, but not be limited to, the following: procedures for routine handling of products; discharge or drainage controls such as secondary containment and procedures for discharge control; countermeasures for discharge discovery, response, and cleanup; methods of disposal or recovered materials; personnel training in emergency response and spill containment techniques; storage of petroleum products in non-leaking containers at impervious storage sites from which an accidental spills cannot escape; storage of concrete, wash water, and other contaminants in watertight containment structures; storing and maintaining spill containment materials such as absorbent pads, pillows, socks, booms, and other spill containment materials in non-leaking sealed containers at the hazardous materials storage sites until transport to an appropriate disposal facility; using spills containment materials under transfer areas when transferring oil or other hazardous materials from trucks to storage containers; daily inspection of equipment for oil, grease, and other petroleum products if equipment is in contact with water; cleaning of external petroleum products off of equipment prior to its contact to water; use of oil- absorbent booms for equipment used in or adjacent to water; containment of contaminants in staging areas designed so that should an accidental spill occur, contaminants do not drain toward receiving waters or storm drain inlets; and staging of all stationary equipment in appropriate staging areas and positioned over drip pans.

The erosion and sediment control plan(s) shall include best management practices such as: physical erosion control stabilization (see Condition of Approval 11.27); maintaining emergency erosion control supplies at all times during construction and replacing used emergency materials within 48 hours; minimal disturbance of the terrain and natural land features; diverting runoff away from steep, denuded slopes or other critical areas with barriers, berms, ditches, or other facilities; retaining trees and vegetation where practicable to stabilize hillsides, retain moisture, and reduce erosion; limiting ground disturbance to areas of proven stability; using sequence clearing of native vegetation and soil disturbance to minimize overall time of soil disturbance; implementing construction management and site inspections before, during, and after rain events; scheduling measures to mitigate erosion from rainfall events, runoff, or flooding at construction sites; installing runoff and drainage control features (e.g., berms and swales, slope drains); installing wind erosion control features (e.g., application of hydraulic mulch or bonded fiber matrix); and use of watertight forms and other containment structures to prevent spills or discharge of raw concrete, wash water, and other contaminants from entering surface waters and other sensitive habitats.

obl-1992.title: Collect and direct surface runoff at non-erosive velocities to common drainage courses for storage and reuse.

locators.excerpt: Sediment control measures shall include measures to retain sediment transported by on-site run-on or runoff; collect and direct surface runoff at non-erosive velocities to common drainage courses for storage and reuse; use sediment and turbidity areas where ground disturbance is adjacent to surface waters or wetlands; prevent mud tracking; and deposit or store excavated materials away from drainage courses and keep them covered when stored over five days or within 48 hours of a forecasted rain event.

obl-1993.title: Control all non-stormwater discharges during construction
monitorSigns: water flowing off site in dry weather

locators.excerpt: Control all non-stormwater discharges during construction.

obl-1994.title: Implement each SWPPP throughout construction under the supervision of a Qualified SWPPP Practitioner
obl-1994.trigger: Throughout the construction period at each site

locators.excerpt: In accordance with this environmental commitment, DWR will require the preparation and implementation of stormwater pollution prevention plans (SWPPPs) to control short-term and long-term effects associated with construction-generated stormwater runoff. The SWPPPs will include all the necessary state requirements regarding construction-generated stormwater collection, detention, treatment, and discharge that will be in place throughout the construction period. For the alternative selected, a series of separate but related SWPPPs will be prepared by a Qualified SWPPP Developer (QSD) and will be implemented under the supervision of a Qualified SWPPP Practitioner (for each construction site and/or each construction contract).

obl-1995.title: Do not let non-stormwater discharges, such as vehicle washing, street cleaning or applying erodible landscape material during rain, reach surface waters.

locators.excerpt: The SWPPP shall include measures that address erosion and sediment control (Condition of Approval 11.26), management of construction materials, waste management measures, water pollution control measures, site dewatering and pipeline testing, accidental spill prevention and response, hazardous materials management plan (Condition of Approval 11.21), site inspection and monitoring, and measures to prevent non-stormwater discharges from reaching surface waters. Non-stormwater discharge examples include washing vehicles, cleaning streets, or applying erodible landscape material during rain.

obl-1996.title: Wash vehicles so no wash water reaches surface waters

locators.excerpt: Wash vehicles in such a manner as to prevent non-stormwater discharges to surface waters.

obl-1997.title: Do not let rinse or wash water run off or be disposed of off site

locators.excerpt: Prevent off-site disposal or runoff of any rinse or wash waters.

obl-1998.title: Design and implement low-impact development measures that disperse and reduce runoff, such as vegetated buffer strips, bioswales, cisterns, and detention basins
monitorSigns: paved area draining directly to waterway

locators.excerpt: Design and implement low-impact development (LID) measures that disperse and reduce runoff by using such features as vegetated buffer strips between paved areas that catch and infiltrate runoff, bioswales, cisterns, and detention basins.

obl-1999.title: Provide concrete and truck washout facilities with appropriately sized storage, treatment, and disposal

locators.excerpt: Implement concrete and truck washout facilities and appropriately sized storage, treatment, and disposal practices.

obl-2000.title: Inspect each drainage area visually at least quarterly for authorized and unauthorized non-stormwater discharges and their sources
monitorSigns: dry-weather flow not traced to source

locators.excerpt: Conduct minimum quarterly visual inspections of each drainage area for the presence of (or indications of prior) unauthorized and authorized non- stormwater discharges and their sources.

obl-2001.title: At least 2 business days before each qualifying rain event (0.5 inch or more), visually inspect drainage areas for spills, leaks, and pollutant sources; all BMPs for proper implementation; and storage and containment areas for leaks and adequate freeboard
obl-2001.trigger: 48 hours before each anticipated qualifying rain event
monitorSigns: BMP not per SWPPP before storm

locators.excerpt: At least 2 business days (48 hours) prior to each anticipated qualifying rain event (a rain event producing 0.5 inch or more of precipitation), visually inspect: (a) stormwater drainage areas to identify any spills, leaks, or uncontrolled pollutant sources; (b) all BMPs to identify whether they have been properly implemented in accordance with the SWPPP; and (c) stormwater storage and containment areas to detect leaks and require maintenance of adequate freeboard. iii.

obl-2002.title: At Risk Level 2 and 3 sites, sample and analyze stormwater discharges at every offsite discharge point, at least three samples per day for pH and turbidity during qualifying rain events
obl-2002.trigger: Risk Level 2 and 3 sites, during qualifying rain events

locators.excerpt: Perform sampling and analysis of stormwater discharges to characterize discharges associated with construction activity from the entire disturbed area at all discharge points where stormwater is discharged offsite. iii. At a minimum, collect and analyze a minimum of three samples per day for pH and turbidity during qualifying rain events. Perform all of the same visual inspection, monitoring, and maintenance measure specified for Risk Level 1 and Risk Level 2 sites. ii.

obl-2003.title: When an active treatment system is deployed, collect effluent samples and measurements from the discharge pipe or a representative location
obl-2003.trigger: Wherever an active treatment system is in use

locators.excerpt: When an active treatment system is deployed on the site or a portion of the site, collect active treatment system effluent samples and measurements from the discharge pipe or another location representative of the nature of the discharge.

obl-2004.title: At Risk Level 3 sites disturbing 30 acres or more and discharging directly to receiving waters, conduct a benthic macroinvertebrate bioassessment of the receiving waters before and after construction begins; if construction starts outside an index period, participate in the State's Surface Water Ambient Monitoring Program instead
obl-2004.trigger: Risk Level 3 sites of 30 acres or more with direct discharge; before and after construction begins
monitorSigns: outside index period, no SWAMP participation

locators.excerpt: If disturbing 30 acres or more of the landscape and discharging directly into receiving waters, conduct a benthic macroinvertebrate bioassessment of receiving waters prior to and after commencement of construction activities to determine if significant degradation to the receiving water’s biota has occurred. However, if commencement of construction is outside of an index period (i.e., the period of time during which bioassessment samples must be collected to produce results suitable for assessing the biological integrity of streams and rivers) for the site location, the discharger will participate in the State of California’s Surface Water Ambient Monitoring Program.

obl-2005.title: At Risk Level 3 sites, if a pH or turbidity numeric effluent limitation is exceeded with direct discharge to receiving waters, sample the receiving waters for all parameters monitored in the discharge
obl-2005.trigger: Risk Level 3 sites, after an NEL exceedance with direct discharge
monitorSigns: NEL exceeded, receiving water not sampled

locators.excerpt: In the event that a numeric effluent limitation (NEL) of the CGP (i.e., pH and turbidity) is exceeded and has a direct discharge into receiving waters, the discharger will subsequently sample receiving waters for all parameter(s) monitored in the discharge.

obl-2006.title: Visually observe stormwater discharges at all discharge locations within 2 business days after each qualifying rain event
obl-2006.trigger: Within 48 hours after each qualifying rain event

locators.excerpt: Visually observe stormwater discharges at all discharge locations within two business days (48 hours) after each qualifying rain event and identify additional BMPs as necessary, and revise the SWPPP accordingly. iv.
Develop and implement a written site-specific Construction Site Monitoring Program (CSMP).

obl-2008.title: All construction-site stormwater inspection, maintenance, repair, and sampling must be performed or supervised by a Qualified SWPPP Practitioner (QSP) representing the discharger
obl-2008.trigger: All stormwater inspection, maintenance, repair, and sampling activities

locators.excerpt: Require that all inspection, maintenance, repair, and sampling activities at the construction site will be performed or supervised by a QSP representing the discharger.

obl-2009.title: Collect one or more effluent samples whenever a breach, malfunction, leak, or spill seen during inspection could discharge pollutants to surface water, whether visible or not
obl-2009.trigger: When such a breach, leak, or spill is observed during visual inspection

locators.excerpt: Collect one or more samples of construction site effluent during any breach, malfunction, leakage, or spill observed within the construction site during a visual inspection that could result in the discharge of pollutants to surface waters whether visually detectable or not.

obl-2010.title: If any effluent sample exceeds a NAL at a Risk Level 2 site, submit all storm event sampling results to the State Water Board within 10 days after the storm ends; provide an NAL Exceedance Report if the Regional Board requires one
obl-2010.trigger: Within 10 days after the storm event in which a NAL was exceeded
monitorSigns: NAL exceedance, results not submitted within 10 days
Regional Board request for exceedance report unanswered

locators.excerpt: In the event that any effluent sample exceeds an applicable NAL, Risk Level 2 dischargers will submit all storm event sampling results to the State Water Board no later than 10 days after the conclusion of the storm event. The Regional Boards have the authority to require the submittal of an NAL Exceedance Report, which includes a description of the current BMPs associated with the effluent sample that exceeded the NAL and the proposed corrective actions taken.

obl-2011.title: Upload the forms and records the SWPPP specifies to SMARTS, including quarterly non-stormwater inspection reports and annual compliance reports.
obl-2011.trigger: On the schedule the SWPPP specifies, quarterly and annually
monitorSigns: quarterly inspection report not uploaded to SMARTS
annual compliance report missing in SMARTS

locators.excerpt: The SWPPP shall also specify the forms and records that must be uploaded to the State Water Board online [Stormwater Multiple Application and Report Tracking System (SMARTS)] at https://smarts.waterboards.ca.gov, such as quarterly non-stormwater inspection and annual compliance reports.
The SWPPP will also specify the forms and records that must be uploaded to the State Water Board online SMARTS, such as quarterly non-stormwater inspection and annual compliance reports.

obl-2012.title: For Risk Level 3 components, report to the State Water Board when effluent monitoring shows daily average runoff pH outside 6.0 to 9.0 or daily average turbidity above 500 NTU
obl-2012.trigger: Risk Level 3 components, when effluent monitoring shows the exceedance
monitorSigns: pH or turbidity exceedance logged, no State Water Board report

locators.excerpt: Additionally, if a given construction component is Risk Level 3, for that component DWR will report to the State Water Board when effluent monitoring indicates that daily average runoff pH is outside the range of 6.0 to 9.0 or the daily average turbidity is greater than 500 NTUs.

obl-2013.title: At Risk Level 3 sites, after an NEL exceedance, submit all storm event sampling results to the State and Regional Water Boards through SMARTS within 5 days after the storm ends
obl-2013.trigger: Within 5 days after the storm event with an NEL exceedance
monitorSigns: NEL exceedance, no SMARTS upload within 5 days

locators.excerpt: An exceedance of an NEL is considered a violation of the CGP, and the discharger must electronically submit all storm event sampling results to the State and Regional Water Boards via Stormwater Multiple Application and Report Tracking System (SMARTS) no later than 5 days after the conclusion of the storm event.

obl-2014.title: Identify additional BMPs and revise the SWPPP when post-storm observations show they are needed
obl-2014.trigger: After post-storm observation finds a need
monitorSigns: post-storm problem logged, SWPPP not revised

locators.excerpt: Visually observe stormwater discharges at all discharge locations within two business days (48 hours) after each qualifying rain event and identify additional BMPs as necessary, and revise the SWPPP accordingly. iv.

obl-2015.title: When effluent monitoring shows a Numeric Action Level exceedance (daily average pH outside 6.5 to 8.5 or daily average turbidity above 250 NTU), have the contractor's QSD revise the SWPPP and immediately modify or add BMPs so later discharges fall below the NALs.
obl-2015.trigger: Risk Level 2 and 3 sites, after an NAL exceedance

locators.excerpt: The CGP also requires the discharger to revise the SWPPP and to immediately modify existing BMPs and/or implement new BMPs such that subsequent discharges are below the relevant Numeric Action Levels (NALs) specified by the CGP. It may be a violation of the CGP if the discharger fails to take corrective action to reduce the discharge below these NALs specified by the CGP. iv.

In accordance with the CGP numeric action level requirements, the project contractor’s QSD will revise the SWPPP and modify existing BMPs or implement new BMPs when effluent monitoring indicates that daily average runoff pH is outside the range of 6.5 to 8.5 and that the daily average turbidity is greater than 250 nephelometric turbidity units (NTUs).

obl-2016.title: Evaluate pervious paving to improve infiltration and reduce runoff to waterways and storm drains
monitorSigns: no pervious paving evaluation on file

locators.excerpt: In addition, DWR will evaluate the potential use of pervious paving to improve infiltration and to reduce the amount of surface runoff from entering waterways and the stormwater system.

obl-2017.title: SWPPP implementation must be supervised by a Qualified SWPPP Practitioner for each construction site or contract

locators.excerpt: For the alternative selected, a series of separate but related SWPPPs will be prepared by a Qualified SWPPP Developer (QSD) and will be implemented under the supervision of a Qualified SWPPP Practitioner (for each construction site and/or each construction contract).

obl-2018.title: Prepare the sediment reintroduction plan to Central Valley RWQCB and USACE permitting standards, consistent with Basin Plan turbidity objectives, and obtain individual NPDES coverage if necessary
obl-2018.trigger: When a sediment reintroduction plan is developed
monitorSigns: plan lacks RWQCB or USACE permit

locators.excerpt: The sediment reintroduction plan will be prepared to meet required permitting standards from the Central Valley RWQCB and USACE. The sediment reintroduction approach will be consistent with objectives for turbidity in the Central Valley Water Board’s Water Quality Control Plan for the Sacramento River and San Joaquin River Basins and, if necessary, will obtain coverage under an individual National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) permit.

restart less than 24 hours after rain

obl-2020.title: Work within 100 feet of rivers, streams, sloughs, ponds, or vernal pools only during low rainfall (under 0.25 inches in 24 hours) and dry weather (under 30% chance of rain).
obl-2020.trigger: Preconstruction, construction and maintenance within 100 feet of water

locators.excerpt: For preconstruction activities, construction activities, and maintenance activities including transmission line construction, transmission line maintenance, ground-disturbing work activities, and facilities maintenance within 100 feet of rivers, streams, sloughs, ponds, or vernal pools, Permittee shall restrict Covered Activities to periods of low rainfall (less than 0.25 inches per 24-hour period) and periods of dry weather (with less than a 30% chance of rain).

obl-2021.title: Do not start work at a site that could put sediment in a waterway if its erosion controls cannot be finished before rain over 0.25 inches in 24 hours.
obl-2021.trigger: Before startup at a site that may introduce sediment into a waterway
monitorSigns: work started with rain forecast and controls incomplete

locators.excerpt: Permittee may not start Covered Activities within a construction site that may cause the introduction of sediments into a waterway if the erosion control measures applicable to that construction site cannot be completed prior to the onset of a rain event (rainfall exceeding 0.25 inches during a 24-hour period).

obl-2022.title: Work outside July 15 to October 15 only with CDFW approval and only during low rainfall (under 0.08 inches per 24 hours and under 40% chance of rain).
obl-2022.trigger: Covered Activities outside the dry season

locators.excerpt: Any Covered Activities conducted outside of the dry season (July 15 – October 15) shall be limited to periods of low rainfall (less than 0.08 inches per 24-hour period and less than 40 percent chance of rain), and subject to CDFW approval with potentially further restrictions.

obl-2023.title: Stop all construction, including ground disturbance and clearing, 24 hours before an NWS rain forecast of 30% or more.
obl-2023.trigger: When NWS forecasts 30% or greater chance of rain

locators.excerpt: Construction activities, including all ground disturbance or vegetation clearing, shall cease 24 hours prior to a 30 percent (30%) or greater forecast of rain from the NWS.

obl-2024.title: Do not start work on a rain-forecast day until the biologist's site survey is done.

locators.excerpt: The Designated Biologist(s) and/or Biological Monitor(s) shall survey each Project site before construction begins on each day any rain is forecasted.
